| | Things are moving extremely quickly now. Far-right lawmakers across the South are rushing to rig new voting maps that erase representation for Black and brown Americans — just days after the Supreme Court — Roberts Court — gave them the green light. It’s a coordinated, region-wide power grab. It’s a blatant attempt to silence voters of color. And if it succeeds, it could lock in Republican control of Congress. **Alongside partners on the ground across the South, we’re now in a state-by-state struggle for fair elections with fair maps. Here are three key fights where you can help turn the tide:** _**Tennessee**_
_What’s happening:_ Tennessee’s governor was the first to call a special state legislative session in response to the Supreme Court ruling. They plan to eliminate a district that gave Black Tennesseans the chance to be fairly represented in Congress. _How you can fight back:_ Our partner, Civic TN, is organizing at the Capitol on Wednesday, May 6th and Thursday, May 7th. **[Sign up and get more info here.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130820648/619028397/-1883456587?refcode=emm_ffa_2026505_T1_CallaisMobz_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YzY0MTIxNi1lMDQ4LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pMSt-bi3kgya9Mty4xc_NzG66P-J36xb1TDhXaCyY2U=&emci=7b641216-e048-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7c641216-e048-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=1037277) ** _**Louisiana**_
_What’s happening:_ The governor moved to suspend an election that was already happening so lawmakers could redraw the voting maps — as soon as tomorrow — and eliminate the state’s two congressional districts that ensure fair representation for Black residents. _How you can fight back:_ The Louisiana legislature is holding a public hearing about the new maps this Friday. Our partner, Power Coalition, is organizing a series of virtual and in-person events this week. **[Check out their schedule here.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130820649/619028398/-583408147?refcode=emm_ffa_2026505_T1_CallaisMobz_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YzY0MTIxNi1lMDQ4LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pMSt-bi3kgya9Mty4xc_NzG66P-J36xb1TDhXaCyY2U=&emci=7b641216-e048-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7c641216-e048-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=1037277)** _**Alabama**_
_What’s happening:_ The governor called a special session following the Supreme Court ruling, giving lawmakers a chance to redistrict and with it, erase a district where Black voters have a fair chance to elect the candidate of their choice. _How you can fight back: _
1. Our partner, United Women of Color, is organizing a bus from North Alabama to Montgomery this Thursday, May 7th, when the legislature is meeting at the Capitol. **[Sign up here.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130820650/619028399/167133809?refcode=emm_ffa_2026505_T1_CallaisMobz_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YzY0MTIxNi1lMDQ4LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pMSt-bi3kgya9Mty4xc_NzG66P-J36xb1TDhXaCyY2U=&emci=7b641216-e048-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7c641216-e048-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=1037277) **
2. Our partners in this fight, Catalyst for Change, are hosting a webinar tomorrow, May 6th, to break down the Supreme Court ruling and what it means for Alabama. **[Sign up here.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130820651/619028400/2040943903?os=ipad&refcode=emm_ffa_2026505_T1_CallaisMobz_v1s2&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNDMvMS84ODQ1MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YzY0MTIxNi1lMDQ4LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pMSt-bi3kgya9Mty4xc_NzG66P-J36xb1TDhXaCyY2U=&emci=7b641216-e048-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7c641216-e048-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=1037277#/registration)**

clean_body: What’s happening & how you can fight back: | | | Things are moving extremely quickly now. Far-right lawmakers across the South are rushing to rig new voting maps that erase representation for Black and brown Americans — just days after the Supreme Court — Roberts Court — gave them the green light. It’s a coordinated, region-wide power grab. It’s a blatant attempt to silence voters of color. And if it succeeds, it could lock in Republican control of Congress. Alongside partners on the ground across the South, we’re now in a state-by-state struggle for fair elections with fair maps. Here are three key fights where you can help turn the tide: Tennessee What’s happening: Tennessee’s governor was the first to call a special state legislative session in response to the Supreme Court ruling. They plan to eliminate a district that gave Black Tennesseans the chance to be fairly represented in Congress. How you can fight back: Our partner, Civic TN, is organizing at the Capitol on Wednesday, May 6th and Thursday, May 7th. Louisiana What’s happening: The governor moved to suspend an election that was already happening so lawmakers could redraw the voting maps — as soon as tomorrow — and eliminate the state’s two congressional districts that ensure fair representation for Black residents. How you can fight back: The Louisiana legislature is holding a public hearing about the new maps this Friday. Our partner, Power Coalition, is organizing a series of virtual and in-person events this week. Alabama What’s happening: The governor called a special session following the Supreme Court ruling, giving lawmakers a chance to redistrict and with it, erase a district where Black voters have a fair chance to elect the candidate of their choice. How you can fight back: 1. Our partner, United Women of Color, is organizing a bus from North Alabama to Montgomery this Thursday, May 7th, when the legislature is meeting at the Capitol. 2. Our partners in this fight, Catalyst for Change, are hosting a webinar tomorrow, May 6th, to break down the Supreme Court ruling and what it means for Alabama. Bottom line: We’re in a new phase of the fight for our democracy. Now’s the time for mass resistance. We’ll be in touch with more opportunities to take action in the places where you can make the greatest impact. And with your support, we’ll stay ready to defend the basic principle of fair elections with fair representation. Yesterday, Fulton County revealed that it had been served a federal grand jury subpoena for the names of its workers in the 2020 election. VRF stands with Fulton County Commissioner Robb Pitts, who on Monday said: “This is yet another act of outrageous federal overreach designed to intimidate and to chill participation in elections.” And this morning, the Supreme Court moved up its ruling on the Voting Rights Act to take effect immediately, allowing Louisiana to racially gerrymander its districts ahead of the midterm elections. Governor Jeff Landry declared an emergency and delayed the primaries, only 11 days away, to implement the new map. body:
Fleming is cashing checks from a DC lobbying firm while holding statewide office

| | |
---

---](https://us.list-manage.com/yWvzl72Accv?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a)
| | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE** May 5, 2026[katherine@julialetlow.com](mailto:katherine@julialetlow.com)
**BOMBSHELL: FLEMING CONFESSES HE IS STILL ON DC LOBBYING FIRM PAYROLL** _Fleming is cashing checks from a DC lobbying firm while holding statewide office_**BATON ROUGE, LA** — During today’s debate, John Fleming said it’s [“perfectly ok”](https://us.list-manage.com/X7rNKUARUpJ?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a) that he is an active employee of The McKeon Group, a Washington DC lobbying firm, while serving as Louisiana State Treasurer and running for the United States Senate.Fleming’s U.S. Senate [financial disclosure](https://us.list-manage.com/_tNMhEfvPrQ?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a), filed under penalty of perjury, lists $41,500 in salary from The McKeon Group, Inc. and $120,217 in salary from the State of Louisiana. The same disclosure lists Fleming’s role with McKeon Group as continuing from January 2024 to present, identifying him as an Advisor while also listing him as Louisiana State Treasurer during the same period.McKeon Group’s [own website](https://us.list-manage.com/18pgFiwIOay?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a) also lists Fleming as an employee. The firm has publicly described itself as a consulting and lobbying firm with Capitol Hill expertise._“John Fleming admitted today that he is still employed by a DC lobbying firm while serving as Louisiana State Treasurer,”_**said Letlow Communications Director Katherine Thordahl.** “ _That is a serious breach of trust that Fleming did not disclose to the voters while running for office.”_ Fleming’s disclosure also identifies a McKeon Group client, Cyber Innovation Center, and describes Fleming’s duties as “consulting and advising on federal funding for national defense projects.”**Fleming should immediately answer the following questions:**
* Did Fleming receive a formal advisory opinion from the Louisiana Board of Ethics approving his continued paid employment with The McKeon Group?
* Did Fleming perform McKeon Group work during state business hours or use any taxpayer-funded resources for firm business?
* Has Fleming used his title, relationships, or access as State Treasurer to benefit The McKeon Group, its clients, or prospective clients?
* Has The McKeon Group used Fleming’s title as Louisiana State Treasurer in pitches, client conversations, business development materials, or federal funding discussions?
* Has Fleming taken any official action as State Treasurer involving an entity that was also a McKeon Group client, prospective client, affiliate, contractor, or partner?
* Is any portion of Fleming’s compensation tied to federal funding, client success, lobbying outcomes, business development, or client retention?
* Will Fleming release his full contract with The McKeon Group, all payment records, all client assignments, and all ethics correspondence related to his outside employment?

Learn more at [JuliaLetlow.com](https://us.list-manage.com/12G64QvQVOv?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a).

# FROM THE DESK OF ALAN DERSHOWITZ
---
| | Dear Reader, In over sixty years in the legal profession, I've experienced first hand the impact of both good journalism and bad journalism -- mostly the latter -- and just how important and rare it is to get things right.

**In today 's media landscape there are far too many publications that get things wrong.** Many are more concerned with the political implications of a story than the basic facts.

**The New York Sun is different.** It's a paper that places principle over politics and people over party.

[ **Join the Sun for 1¢ →** ](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=54fef9be615540499b5f5e4dff6b7d81&_e=nHEFYvqlkT6g5I6NzZvjqHcGCg6__buloJzdGYf7eAA-vK2eJNWRsoQ1urCS8QLMllxFWF6sPCJyd2aK1Y0cCnuG57H7ntlLqHa3N-SgoaqouPW79YgIs_2zv-IPIUUmjvuWYfb_9xQQBv6u1AkIq_91dTM7FsJHVBkZWaazDES7rWYcxyNcVNRGMh1eguDBUJwTvbhZJg785nAhORJ2UNsYe9DLEnuOoPRjcoMP5N-gj7Plo5HPARjQLavQgoHnQWj7ObICTJlUDEOp4Kk_5uZnK1R9_v3iEhyDqoaJ0DhxABfHpUPaDUuNPKumL-CIXWTyRkz8udetNgahKp4-N7kPvWC_kIdr5nfCm_579-ix_GTTLlS-jfktQzxyxomk49KGiZzSvlXb9dzx00XunuqlafNSwKGQaJ2AvWdyK0JfxNRa5qfVoDIHjJVc18TXvj4xWRyUA5FI4BmDMJRaYVT8OTeboIDEtbR9WjHrwm8%3D)

Its in-depth coverage of the legal challenges faced by President Trump serve as a case in point.

When I defended President Trump during his first impeachment, I faced an avalanche of criticism, but few papers made sufficient effort to fully appreciate the significance of the legal arguments.

The Sun's deeply knowledgeable leadership, including its editor Seth Lipsky and associate editor A.R. Hoffman are themselves students of the Constitution. It shows in their coverage, which I find to be first rate.

subject: They tried to take Trump out again
body:
Plus: Iran's regime is cracking | New episode for dpwillis67@gmail.com

| | | | | |

| | | | | |
Three weeks until New Mexicans pick a Republican nominee for governor. The new [Albuquerque Journal poll just dropped](https://us.list-manage.com/lNStxSCAb06?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e) — and it tells you everything about how wide open this thing still is.

Then we get to Iran. The regime is cracking. And what the Wall Street Journal just reported that they're considering...well, you have to hear it to believe it!
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/qZgjoFgxT_I?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
| |
🏛️ **HULL LEADS AT 30% — 40% STILL HAVEN'T DECIDED**
Gregg Hull is in front. Doug Turner is at 21%. Duke Rodriguez is stuck in single digits.
But the number that actually matters is 40% — that's how many Republican and Independent voters still haven't picked a candidate. Three weeks out.
We break down why nobody has been able to lay a glove on Hull, and the one move Doug Turner has to make in the next 14 days — or this race is over.

🔥 **THE ATTACK MAILERS HIT — AND ONE OF THEM ACTUALLY LANDS**
Duke Rodriguez voted in Arizona in 2024. And 2022. And 2018. And 2016.
A PAC mailer just made sure every Republican primary voter knows it.
Meanwhile, Duke's people are firing back at Doug Turner over $6 million in state contracts Turner's firm allegedly took from Michelle Lujan Grisham to push her COVID agenda.
We watch both candidates' ads on the show. One is professional. The other looks — well, you'll see. And we tell you which attack insiders say is actually working.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://us.list-manage.com/q7VRkLrTl3V?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---
| |
🐬 **IRAN'S REGIME IS CRACKING — AND THEY'RE PLOTTING KAMIKAZE DOLPHINS**
70% inflation. Hundreds of millions in losses every day. No oil moving to China. The Iranian regime is desperate.
How desperate? The Wall Street Journal just reported they're contemplating strapping mines to dolphins to go after U.S. ships.
That's not a joke. That's actually being floated.
Mark walks through why Trump's blockade is working better than the media wants to admit — and why Scott Jennings completely lost his cool on CNN this week. We're not defending Jennings. But you have to see what triggered it.

✈️ **WARREN AND BUTTIGIEG JUST TOOK DOWN SPIRIT AIRLINES**
Spirit went bankrupt Saturday. 30 regional airports lost service overnight.
Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent named names on Sunday morning TV: Elizabeth Warren wrote the letter that blocked the JetBlue merger. Pete Buttigieg's DOT killed the deal.
Why does it matter to you in Albuquerque? Half the Sunport's traffic flies Southwest. And when Spirit's discount flyers disappear from connecting hubs, your fares are about to go up across the board. Mark explains exactly how this hits your wallet.
---
| [Stream Episode Now](https://us.list-manage.com/30akolUiyec?e=567664f14c&c2id=f551a60afe6194f7ea2dcf92821ad62e)
---

body:
The Republican Party is propped up by a network of billionaires and special interest groups who can write massive checks without giving it a second thought. Democrats are doing things differently.
#
Peter,
Across the country right now, there are incredible Democratic candidates running for office – up and down the entire ballot, in every single state.
They’ve got organizers knocking on doors. Volunteers making calls. These candidates are tirelessly showing up for their communities day after day.
The energy is there. The people are there.
**Money is the factor that is too often missing.**
**[ELECT DEMOCRATS: CHIP IN NOW](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/103464?refcode=em20260505-10390&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=1&akid=10390%2E614464%2EFZbpsZ)**
Here's the reality we’re facing right now: **The Republican Party is propped up by a network of billionaires and special interest groups who can write massive checks without giving it a second thought.** Dark money flows freely – funding attack ads, voter suppression efforts, and GOP candidates who answer to their donors instead of the people they were elected to serve.
**Democrats are doing things differently.** Our power comes from real people like you – grassroots donors who give what they can, when they can, because they believe that our country can do better than it’s doing right now.
And that matters enormously. But it also means we face hard choices.
**Right now, we’re working to support Democratic candidates in all 50 states.**
We all know there is no shortage of fights worth having – and no shortage of dedicated leaders who are ready to have them. But without adequate resources, we are forced to make impossible decisions about where to invest, which races to prioritize, and which communities we simply cannot reach.
**Every state matters. Every election matters. Every constituent matters.**
**[ELECT DEMOCRATS: CHIP IN NOW](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/103464?refcode=em20260505-10390&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=10390%2E614464%2EFZbpsZ)**
We know what happens when Democrats show up everywhere: We win.
And we know what happens when we give up ground: Republicans entrench themselves for decades, gerrymander maps, restrict voting rights, and make it harder to fight back the next time. _We cannot afford to let that happen._
**If you've been waiting for the right moment to give – this is it.** Your donation today helps us support good candidates running in red and purple states across the country – where the odds are long but the stakes are even higher.
**[Will you chip in $5 or whatever you can to help us show up everywhere and WIN in 2026, Peter?](https://act.lucaskunce.com/go/103464?refcode=em20260505-10390&firstname=Peter&lastname=Willis&email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=10390%2E614464%2EFZbpsZ)**

Millions of North Carolinians could be disenfranchised
| | Peter,
---
Sorry to email so late, but we’re still a few thousand signatures short on Roy Cooper’s emergency petition in defense of voting rights in light of the Supreme Court’s disastrous ruling. **[Can you please take 60 seconds now to add your name?](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/voting-rights-0526?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=email_su_pros_jtk418&t=6&akid=1290%2E124072%2E-9W7Fd)**
Roy refuses to stand on the sidelines while a few far-right extremists try to send us back to the days of widespread voter suppression across the South – **so Peter, neither can you.**
**[It’s going to take a massive grassroots mobilization to ensure our democracy’s survival, and we're counting on 150 more signatures from Englewood. Please join us in the fight by signing the petition without further delay.](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/voting-rights-0526?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=email_su_pros_jtk418&t=7&akid=1290%2E124072%2E-9W7Fd)**

Thank you for taking a stand with us – on the right side of history.
– Team Cooper

Date: Mon, May 4, 2026

[](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/voting-rights-0526?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=email_su_pros_jtk418&t=10&akid=1290%2E124072%2E-9W7Fd)
Peter – the President Trump-stacked Supreme Court just gutted Section 2 of the Voting Rights Act, which bans racially discriminatory electoral laws and maps.
**_[If that’s all you need to hear, please take 60 seconds right now to sign on to Roy’s emergency petition in support of fair representation and voting rights before 11:59 p.m.](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/voting-rights-0526?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=email_su_pros_jtk418&t=11&akid=1290%2E124072%2E-9W7Fd)_**

**By effectively empowering GOP-held state legislatures to silence millions of voters of color – _and millions of North Carolinians_ – ahead of the midterms, the _Louisiana v. Callais_ ruling is an egregious attack on the better part of a century’s worth of progress. It also risks giving MAGA Republicans all the seats they need to lock in control of the House for decades to come.**
The Supreme Court has joined President Trump and his congressional allies in chipping away at the very idea that in our democracy, every vote matters equally.

However, this appalling decision only underscores what Roy has said before: **Democracy is not something guaranteed to us – it’s something we must fight for.**
**_[That’s why we’re counting on at least 50,000 folks like you to join the fight alongside him in support of fair representation and voting rights ASAP. Will you please take 60 seconds now to add your name to our emergency petition before the deadline at midnight?](https://act.roycooper.com/survey/voting-rights-0526?email=dpwillis67@gmail.com&zip=&ask=5&source=email_su_pros_jtk418&t=13&akid=1290%2E124072%2E-9W7Fd)_**

– Team Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

body:
Hi there, it’s Nancy Lacore, the Democrat running to flip South Carolina’s First District.
I have a lot of thoughts about what’s been going on with Pete Hegseth.
Not only did he remove me from my position as Chief of the Navy Reserve after 35 years of service, but he’s actively undermining the foundation of our military.
Hegseth has fired more than a dozen senior military officers, including an Army chief of staff and two other generals who were ousted recently.
And now, he’s waging a war with Iran that could put our national security and countless American lives on the line.
That kind of behavior isn’t just destabilizing – it’s dangerous.
Now more than ever, we need leadership that’s rooted in honor, service, and respect. And that’s exactly why I’m running for Congress in South Carolina’s First District.
If we’re going to flip this seat and take back a Democratic House Majority, I need your help. Can you make a split donation of $25 or whatever you can, to Resist Reclaim Rebuild and my campaign? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-lacore]
DONATE NOW TO HELP NANCY FLIP THIS SEAT! >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-lacore]
I’ll be honest, folks, I’m concerned.
While global tensions rise, the last thing we need is reckless leadership that’s willing to gamble with American lives.
We need steady, experienced leaders who are focused on delivering results – not inciting chaos, playing political games, and putting their own interests above the nation’s.
And I’m running for Congress to restore that kind of leadership – but we have a long road ahead of us to flip this seat and restore some accountability to Washington.
This is one of the most competitive races in the country, and it could decide control of the House. So I need all hands on deck to win. So I have to humbly ask: Will you split $25 today to support Resist Reclaim Rebuild and my campaign? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/rrr-lacore]

So much hard work has brought us to this point, and I’m beyond grateful to everyone who has devoted their time, energy, and dollars to support my campaign so far. Because of you, Ohio is in play and we have a serious shot of flipping this seat and retaking a Senate majority.

National Republicans have already poured a tsunami of outside resources into Ohio to attack me and my record – and I can guarantee they’re about to unleash a new wave of attacks.
I’ll have more to say soon, but in the meantime, I have to candidly ask for your support. We’re entering a brand new phase of this race, and I need you by my side.

name: Katie Porter
subject: What I saw on the debate stage tonight
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Katie Porter for Governor 2026
body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41278%2E3422442%2EgQqfdW)
Peter, I just stepped off the stage from the third debate in this race for governor, and I want to tell you what I saw up there tonight.
I saw **two MAGA Republicans** trying to drag Donald Trump’s extremist agenda into California.
I saw **a candidate who took a maximum contribution from Big Oil and is now backpedaling on single-payer health care** to win the support of powerful health care corporations and insiders.
I saw a **self-funding billionaire who has poured $158 million of his own money into this race** trying to buy himself a governor’s office.
That’s a lot of powerful people and special interests on one debate stage. _And the truth is Californians deserve better._
I’ve spent my career going after powerful interests that think the rules don’t apply to them—Big Banks, giant corporations, pharmaceutical companies, CEOs trying to rip off working people. And I don’t scare easily.
_I know what families are dealing with right now because I've lived it._
I know what it’s like to sit at the kitchen table and figure out which bills can wait another few days, or to stretch every dollar at the grocery store. I know the stress of trying to make everything fit when costs keep going up but paychecks don’t.
**That’s why I’m in this race: to lower costs, deliver single-payer health care, make child care free, make public college tuition-free, and make this state work for the people who actually do the work.**
And unlike some of the people I shared the stage with tonight, I’m not taking corporate PAC money and I’m not spending a personal fortune to buy this seat.
This campaign is powered by people giving what they can because they’re tired of politics working great for billionaires and corporations while everyone else gets squeezed.

| | | | | | 🏛️ State Budget Update: Legislative Action and Governor’s VetoYesterday, the State Senate approved a balanced state budget for Fiscal Year 2026 that focused on protecting core services while delivering targeted tax relief to help Arizona families, seniors, and small businesses manage rising costs. The legislature’s plan fully funded K–12 education, public safety, child protection services, and other essential state responsibilities. The tax relief package included measures such as reductions for working families, retirees, and small business employers—designed to improve affordability and support economic stability across the state. The budget relied on stable revenue projections.
The legislature’s budget protected essential services, prioritized responsible spending, and delivered meaningful tax relief without relying on federal reimbursements or voter‐dependent revenue mechanisms. The legislature’s plan also kept Arizona on solid financial footing while addressing affordability challenges facing families and small businesses. Today, Hobbs vetoed the budget bills. In her veto letter, she stated that she opposed the plan’s reductions to certain safety‐net programs and expressed concern that the Legislature’s revenue assumptions were, in her view, too uncertain to support long‐term fiscal stability. She also objected to the scope of the tax relief provisions mentioned above. As you can see, the legislature and the governor aren’t on the same page when it comes to this year’s state budget. She wants to include a Proposition 123 renewal and higher spending levels for Medicaid and other social service programs. When the governor walked away from budget negotiations in March, the House and Senate crafted a state budget that relied on delivering nearly $1.5 billion in tax relief over the next three years, including
* Elimination of state taxes on tips and overtime pay
* Expanded childcare expense relief
* Increased dependent tax credit
* Additional tax relief for retirees and pension income

The Legislature’s budget spent approximately $800 million less than the budget proposed by Hobbs. The $17.9 billion budget centered on major tax cuts delivering full conformity with federal tax reductions, 5% reductions to most state agencies, and improving affordability for Arizonans. Discussions on next steps continue between the House and Senate. Lawmakers will work to ensure the state has a stable, sustainable budget for the year ahead, but we have a divided government so the process is a bit messy.

[](https://daniellebethell.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akjkyjy-hhlrhljhit-r/) Friends,I'm proud to share that Stand for Health Freedom has endorsed my campaign for Governor.**I 'm also proud to say that I am the only candidate in the Governor's race to receive this endorsement.**This one means a great deal to me.Stand for Health Freedom's endorsement is rooted in principles I share, medical freedom, informed consent, parental rights, religious liberty, privacy, and free speech. Their movement now includes more than one million advocates across the country, people who believe government should be accountable, respect individual liberty, and use common sense.[If you share those values, will you please consider making a donation today?](https://daniellebethell.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akjkyjy-hhlrhljhit-y/) We're two weeks from Election Day. My opponents have the money - either from big donors or personal loans - but we have the momentum and the grassroots. Can you help me close the gap before it's too late? [](https://daniellebethell.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akjkyjy-hhlrhljhit-j/) **My focus in this race is Oregon. If I 'm given the opportunity to serve as governor, I will use that office to make sure Oregonians are heard, served, and protected.** That also means being honest about how government uses data, where privacy is being weakened, and whether tools created in the name of safety are being used in ways that erode basic freedoms.**Long before this race, I was fighting against forced mandates and standing with families who believed government had gone too far in making decisions that belong to parents, patients, and individuals.** I fought against vaccine mandates in 2019 during HB 3063. I stood with communities, including the Russian Old Believer community, who understood deeply what religious and medical freedom mean when government starts narrowing people's choices.That work didn't begin because I was running for Governor. It began because I believed it was right.And I still do. [Can You Chip In Now?](https://daniellebethell.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akjkyjy-hhlrhljhit-t/) Oregonians deserve a Governor who understands that health decisions are personal. They deserve leadership that respects families, protects individual rights, and does not treat people as problems to be managed by the state.This endorsement is another sign of the momentum we are building heading into May 19.But endorsements alone do not win elections. We have to make sure voters hear this message before ballots are cast.[Please consider making a contribution today to help us keep reaching voters in these final weeks.](https://daniellebethell.cmail19.com/t/y-l-akjkyjy-hhlrhljhit-i/)I'm grateful for the support of Stand for Health Freedom, and I'm grateful to everyone who continues to stand with this campaign.Danielle Bethell
Republican for Governor**P.S.**[We are in the final stretch. The House passed the SAVE America Act to finally require voter ID and restore trust in our elections.

But right now, it’s STUCK in the Senate—and it’s being held up by a FILIBUSTER.

That means a small group of senators can BLOCK a BASIC, COMMON-SENSE reform most Americans already support: showing ID when you vote.

So here’s why I’m reaching out.

I’m personally collecting names of Americans who support the SAVE America Act and voter ID requirements to send straight to the Senate.

And I noticed something important—

your name isn’t on the list yet.

That needs to change TODAY! [https://secure.winred.com/friends-of-tim-moore/050526_voterid_samoore/?utm_source=Housefile&utm_medium=SA-Email&utm_campaign=05.05.26_VoterID_SAMoore&utm_content=Link&recurring=true]

Because I’m submitting this petition at MIDNIGHT, and I want to show Washington exactly how many Americans are demanding free and fair elections backed by voter ID.

Not next week. Not after more delay.

NOW.

---
Dear Fellow Patriot, **[I’m writing today because our “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” Petition Drive must be supercharged immediately.](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2z3o8pv6upkn9ept828cc94le8rhfavn2hn0e59pg_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1jmcpj4c3h2bs)** And at a moment like this, we are reaching out to Americans who still believe in election integrity, the Constitution, and the fundamental principle that **only citizens should decide our elections.** If you’ve ever heard of **AMAC Action** , you know that we are one of the nation’s leading conservative advocacy organizations—mobilizing millions of Americans to stand up for limited government, secure elections, and the values that made this country great.Right now, we need your voice. **[Please click here to submit your signed “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” petition in the next 48 hours.](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zdn8jkougflnnl49jhcc1s4hrjk8ssuk32843oh0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1jmcpj4c3h2bs)** My friend, you know that with razor-thin margins in the House and Senate, all bets are off after the midterm elections. That means we must act **now** , while we still have the opportunity.We must **BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING** before it’s too late.Today, millions of illegal immigrants who entered the country are being counted in ways that directly impact political power.And that means:
---
* More congressional seats for states with large illegal populations
* More Electoral College votes
* More federal funding
* More political power

---
And more opportunity for non-citizens to end up on voter rolls.That’s exactly why AMAC Action launched this national petition drive.So far, **more than 100,000 petitions** have already been signed by concerned Americans.But it is not enough.**[To force action—to apply real pressure—we must reach 500,000 signed petitions.](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2zgp4rdbstbubm1ekjn0g0bb1hreo9oes4frk3ue0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1jmcpj4c3h2bs)****Half a million.** That’s the kind of number that gets politicians’ attention.But without your signature, we won’t get there in time.To stop non-citizen voting, concerned citizens across the country must send one loud and unmistakable message:
---
1. **Only American citizens should be counted in the census.**
2. **Only American citizens should have a vote.**

---
[ ** Sign the Petition** ](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2z04474jkvrh8gnl8agv2sgmf9ttklfnie7fkkj4g_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1jmcpj4c3h2bs)
---
You’re receiving this message because you’ve been identified as someone who may be willing to take a stand on critical issues like this. And at a moment like this, every signature matters. Because without action, momentum is lost—and we cannot afford to lose momentum with the midterms approaching.When you sign and submit your petition in the next 48 hours with your petition sponsorship gift you will help AMAC Action:
---
* Distribute hundreds of thousands of additional petitions by mail, email, text, and social media
* Expand digital outreach to recruit more conservative seniors
* Organize state-level petition drives
* Deliver signed petitions directly to lawmakers
* Push election integrity legislation that safeguards your vote
* Fight for census reform so representation reflects citizens only

---
That’s a lot to accomplish.But we’ve seen what’s possible when Americans step forward.With the help of patriots just like you, we’ve already helped:
---
* Pass the Rescissions Act to cut wasteful spending
* Push the “One Big, Beautiful Bill” across the finish line
* Advance the SAVE Act in the House

---
And so much more. But now, we must finish the job. Stopping non-citizen voting is one of the most common-sense issues of our time. And if enough Americans take action—we can get it done.Some have chosen to ignore this issue. The Left is counting on that. But millions of Americans are taking action. We hope you will be one of them. **[Please sign your “BAN NON-CITIZEN VOTING” petition and submit it within the next 48 hours.](http://e.goppresidential.com/rd/9z2z34fl7pdlcd0k9a1goghbhtfh553463vuj54gb4g_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1jmcpj4c3h2bs)**

**Rebecca Weber,_Chairwoman_****AMAC Action**

---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

## Only Nine Summer Camps Licensed
With just a few weeks until kids get out of school, only nine Texas summer camps have [received a license](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0DGuozAQxvHTmA40HsY4FC62ocu2WyKvPQRLBiPbG5Lbr8jTO8GrR_qPft-f-3y3IYb98dtubOprSfPOZ4lcK-e5_Ns2zs5uRwyO98Ils0vZpxkBhxZUC8PsbYjvmRpv_oIfZcNGan2DQfVaNasBRdYNWgKO5AmltwDoFBEptWjFTTBXDBQMUgIq2Tm80ahovGnFNC5OELAPNeWurlz5ZcsS3-nJuXNpa6JZaz2K6H8JnARO53l2bs1pv64Cp4sjcLK5BhdZ4PQptBeq_fK1H8y3sEVE6qnX3bEeTTb-OEOMoQxaEDw2G-Lnbf3ZWE-D_wMAAP__kdx8yQ) to operate. At least 243 are still waiting for approval from the Texas Department of State Health Services (DSHS). The bottleneck stems from implemented by the agency following the passage of camp safety legislation in the wake of the July 4 flash floods, which killed at least 135 people in the Hill Country and Central Texas, including 27 at Kerr County's Camp Mystic. This year, camps are required to submit emergency plans to the state for review, and DSHS deficiencies in 174 of them. A handful of camps have sued to block the requirement to install a fiber-optic internet connection, claiming it's either cost-prohibitive or simply unavailable at their locations. Monday evening, state Rep. Pat Curry (R-Waco) claimed DSHS had told him "NO CAMPS will be closed this summer due to broadband deficiencies," agency staff "indicated a legislative fix will be pursued in the upcoming 90th Legislative Session." Wesley Hunt backing Paxton. The candidates tied at 43% when respondents were asked which would fare better against state Rep. James Talarico in the general election. Joan Huffman break evenly for the two candidates, while those who backed former DOJ attorney Aaron Reitz support Middleton 54% to 38%. Railroad Commissioner Jim Wright leads former Tarrant County GOP Chair Bo French 35% to 28%. Respondents who back Cornyn Wright 46% to 18%, while those who intend to vote for Paxton support French 39% to 26%. Last week, five extremists on the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act, opening the door for Republicans in deep-red states to eliminate majority-minority districts across the country. Nothing illustrates why state Supreme Courts are the firewall more than that.
Elections and redistricting are state issues. Federal courts can't fix this. Congress can't fix this. The only institutions with the power to stop MAGA's gerrymandering operation are state legislatures and state Supreme Courts -- and MAGA has spent years and hundreds of millions of dollars making sure those courts belong to them.
Their investment is about to pay off. Unless we stop them.
Defend Our Courts exists for exactly this moment. We've beaten MAGA's dark money machine in Pennsylvania. We beat them again in Wisconsin. We have two weeks to win in Georgia -- two seats that set up a full court flip before the 2028 presidential election. After Georgia: Kansas in August, and a string of Supreme Court elections in November.
Every race we win is another state where MAGA's revenge tour hits a wall. Indiana just showed us what happens when they win.

### J _im Himes may joke about ADUs to appeal to his progressive base -- but for Connecticut neighborhoods, municipalities, families, and Long Island Sound, parking, sewer capacity, local control, and infrastructure costs are no laughing matter._
[Pledge your support](https://substack..ypc9EW1cFovuGqy2GrY2EpkNeysigLoNPXsDlkBJGqE?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=196647308)
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=1454853&post_id=196647308&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk2NjQ3MzA4LCJpYXQiOjE3NzgwNjg2ODgsImV4cCI6MTc4MDY2MDY4OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTE0NTQ4NTMiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.L0YjgwOHN3sUOa_HKhFHcGnpjQtxVEqv7xSUn18owUw)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/5a2a5890-88f8-48c6-8cdf-256b58c378a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Congressman Himes Post](https://substack.com/redirect/0e3713fd-1504-4133-9365-86c0650829ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Congressman Jim Himes recently joked that relocating 12,000 bees into his backyard was "another success story for accessory dwelling units."
Maybe that line gets a laugh on social media. Maybe it scores points with the progressive zoning activists who see every Connecticut neighborhood as underutilized space waiting for more density.
_**But for many residents across Connecticut -- especially in Fairfield County and along the coastline -- accessory dwelling units are not a joke. They are a serious public-policy issue involving infrastructure, environmental capacity, parking, drainage, neighborhood character, and the future of local control.**_
That kind of joke may play well with Congressman Himes' progressive base, but it erodes the voices of everyone else in the district: homeowners, neighborhoods, local zoning boards, municipal officials, and taxpayers who are left to deal with the real-world consequences.
For them, ADUs are not a punchline. They are a cost.
_**A cost in parking.
A cost in sewer capacity.
A cost in drainage and stormwater management.
A cost in already strained infrastructure.
A cost in schools, emergency services, and municipal budgets.
And ultimately, a cost to the character of Connecticut's communities.**_
I'm sure grassroots organizations like [CT 169 Strong](https://substack.com/redirect/077b692a-89d1-4372-ad70-91fbd13f5c9b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) will take issue with reducing a serious statewide zoning and infrastructure debate into a backyard bee joke while many Connecticut communities are already struggling with overburdened systems and density concerns.
**And not to mention the Sound.**
Connecticut residents are repeatedly told to accept more density as if the pipes, roads, beaches, and waterways can absorb it for free. But Long Island Sound already pays the price when aging sewer systems and overflow events discharge contamination into coastal waters.
In 2023, Connecticut recorded **220 beach action days** across 73 coastal beaches, including **190 closure days** , with state environmental officials pointing to heavier rainfall and combined sewer overflows as major contributing factors.
Organizations like **[Save the Sound](https://substack.com/redirect/96d82452-b0d7-4421-a7ca-98008dd058f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/96d82452-b0d7-4421-a7ca-98008dd058f1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)have repeatedly warned that stormwater and wastewater can overwhelm combined sewer systems, causing untreated sewage and contamination to flow into waterways and ultimately into Long Island Sound itself.
**And what about the kids?**
What about the families who should be able to enjoy Connecticut's coastline without wondering whether the beach is closed because sewage levels are unsafe?
I'm sure Congressman Himes' progressive base will not be laughing when they cannot take their kids to the beach or dip their toes in Long Island Sound for fear of health issues. Sewage-contaminated water is not just unpleasant -- EPA warns it can cause gastroenteritis, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, headaches, fever, and ear, eye, nose, and throat infections. Recreational water contaminated by fecal matter can also expose swimmers to pathogens such as **norovirus, E. coli, Shigella, and Cryptosporidium**.
The progressive base may like the ADU joke -- until the beach is closed, the Sound is contaminated, and their children cannot safely touch the water.
It is time to conserve Connecticut's coastline -- not just environmentally, but functionally. Conservation means protecting the ability of residents to safely enjoy the beauty of the coastline, the beaches, the harbors, and the Sound itself.
Because once infrastructure falls behind density, the consequences do not remain hidden underground.
They wash downstream.
**From Coronado to Connecticut - Another California Warning to Heed**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8b602226-2501-4669-8065-06e136a2c3b8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The [Wall Street Journal](https://substack.com/redirect/3e9d3468-00a5-450f-b5fc-b8fcfc743d13?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) recently warned what this looks like when a coastal sewage problem becomes impossible to ignore. In Coronado, California, sewage-tainted wastewater from Tijuana has reportedly fouled one of America's most famous beach communities, with millions of gallons of contaminated water reaching U.S. shores, forcing closures, damaging tourism, hurting local businesses, and creating public-health fears.
Connecticut should pay attention before Long Island Sound becomes our version of that story. Connecticut's coastline is not just scenery. It is an economic engine supporting tourism, rentals, restaurants, marinas, and small businesses.
But how long does that last if families cannot trust the water, beaches close after storms, and summer rentals start carrying the smell of sewage instead of salt air?
I am sure the realtor population will love trying to market "summer on the Sound" when renters ask whether the beach is open, whether the water is safe, and whether the breeze comes with a summery sewage smell.
Perhaps Congressman Himes should spend less time joking about ADUs and more time considering the **tragedy of the commons** : when everyone is encouraged to add private density, but the public costs fall on shared streets, shared sewers, shared beaches, and Long Island Sound. That may be a better guide for Connecticut housing policy than the old ideological romance with Sandinista-style central planning that critics have pointed to from his college writings.
Housing affordability is real. Connecticut absolutely needs opportunity, economic growth, workforce development, and smarter planning. But affordability cannot become an excuse for one-size-fits-all mandates that ignore infrastructure limits and silence municipal voices. Under limited circumstances with local zoning approval and sufficient infrastructure ADUs may be acceptable.
Bee boxes in a backyard may be harmless.
Public policy is not.
**ADUs are not a joke. They are a cost -- on streets, sewers, taxpayers, municipalities, families, tourism, and even the Sound itself.**

clean_body: Save Our Sound from Sewage | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more The Goldstein Substack - A Father-Son Publication Dr. Goldstein is Running for Congress and his page can be found Save Our Sound from Sewage | | | May 6 | | | | | | | | | | | | J im Himes may joke about ADUs to appeal to his progressive base -- but for Connecticut neighborhoods, municipalities, families, and Long Island Sound, parking, sewer capacity, local control, and infrastructure costs are no laughing matter. | | ---|---|--- Congressman Jim Himes recently joked that relocating 12,000 bees into his backyard was "another success story for accessory dwelling units." Maybe that line gets a laugh on social media. Maybe it scores points with the progressive zoning activists who see every Connecticut neighborhood as underutilized space waiting for more density. But for many residents across Connecticut -- especially in Fairfield County and along the coastline -- accessory dwelling units are not a joke. They are a serious public-policy issue involving infrastructure, environmental capacity, parking, drainage, neighborhood character, and the future of local control. That kind of joke may play well with Congressman Himes' progressive base, but it erodes the voices of everyone else in the district: homeowners, neighborhoods, local zoning boards, municipal officials, and taxpayers who are left to deal with the real-world consequences. For them, ADUs are not a punchline. They are a cost. A cost in parking. A cost in sewer capacity. A cost in drainage and stormwater management. A cost in already strained infrastructure. A cost in schools, emergency services, and municipal budgets. And ultimately, a cost to the character of Connecticut's communities. I'm sure grassroots organizations like will take issue with reducing a serious statewide zoning and infrastructure debate into a backyard bee joke while many Connecticut communities are already struggling with overburdened systems and density concerns. And not to mention the Sound. Connecticut residents are repeatedly told to accept more density as if the pipes, roads, beaches, and waterways can absorb it for free. But Long Island Sound already pays the price when aging sewer systems and overflow events discharge contamination into coastal waters. In 2023, Connecticut recorded 220 beach action days across 73 coastal beaches, including 190 closure days , with state environmental officials pointing to heavier rainfall and combined sewer overflows as major contributing factors. Organizations like repeatedly warned that stormwater and wastewater can overwhelm combined sewer systems, causing untreated sewage and contamination to flow into waterways and ultimately into Long Island Sound itself. And what about the kids? What about the families who should be able to enjoy Connecticut's coastline without wondering whether the beach is closed because sewage levels are unsafe? I'm sure Congressman Himes' progressive base will not be laughing when they cannot take their kids to the beach or dip their toes in Long Island Sound for fear of health issues. Sewage-contaminated water is not just unpleasant -- EPA warns it can cause gastroenteritis, nausea, vomiting, stomach pain, diarrhea, headaches, fever, and ear, eye, nose, and throat infections. Recreational water contaminated by fecal matter can also expose swimmers to pathogens such as norovirus, E. coli, Shigella, and Cryptosporidium. The progressive base may like the ADU joke -- until the beach is closed, the Sound is contaminated, and their children cannot safely touch the water. It is time to conserve Connecticut's coastline -- not just environmentally, but functionally. Conservation means protecting the ability of residents to safely enjoy the beauty of the coastline, the beaches, the harbors, and the Sound itself. Because once infrastructure falls behind density, the consequences do not remain hidden underground. They wash downstream. From Coronado to Connecticut - Another California Warning to Heed | | ---|---|--- The recently warned what this looks like when a coastal sewage problem becomes impossible to ignore. In Coronado, California, sewage-tainted wastewater from Tijuana has reportedly fouled one of America's most famous beach communities, with millions of gallons of contaminated water reaching U.S. shores, forcing closures, damaging tourism, hurting local businesses, and creating public-health fears. Connecticut should pay attention before Long Island Sound becomes our version of that story. Connecticut's coastline is not just scenery. It is an economic engine supporting tourism, rentals, restaurants, marinas, and small businesses. But how long does that last if families cannot trust the water, beaches close after storms, and summer rentals start carrying the smell of sewage instead of salt air? I am sure the realtor population will love trying to market "summer on the Sound" when renters ask whether the beach is open, whether the water is safe, and whether the breeze comes with a summery sewage smell. Perhaps Congressman Himes should spend less time joking about ADUs and more time considering the tragedy of the commons : when everyone is encouraged to add private density, but the public costs fall on shared streets, shared sewers, shared beaches, and Long Island Sound. That may be a better guide for Connecticut housing policy than the old ideological romance with Sandinista-style central planning that critics have pointed to from his college writings. Housing affordability is real. Connecticut absolutely needs opportunity, economic growth, workforce development, and smarter planning. But affordability cannot become an excuse for one-size-fits-all mandates that ignore infrastructure limits and silence municipal voices. Under limited circumstances with local zoning approval and sufficient infrastructure ADUs may be acceptable. Bee boxes in a backyard may be harmless. Public policy is not. ADUs are not a joke. They are a cost -- on streets, sewers, taxpayers, municipalities, families, tourism, and even the Sound itself.** The Goldstein Substack is free today. Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. Derek,
**Last night, it became official: I’m the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Ohio.**
I’m grateful. Truly.
[**Will you help me mark this moment by splitting $20 between my campaign and the Democratic National Committee to help us start the general election push strong and keep building our grassroots momentum?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-brown-split?refcode=em_20260506_7027_fr&amount=20&refcode2=7027_22930333_UmHgaQ&akid=7027%2E22930333%2EUmHgaQ)
**[CONTRIBUTE $20](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-brown-split?refcode=em_20260506_7027_fr&amount=20&refcode2=7027_22930333_UmHgaQ&akid=7027%2E22930333%2EUmHgaQ)**
**I came off the sidelines for one reason: Ohio families.**
Life is too expensive. Paychecks are too low. Costs are too high – utilities, health care, groceries, everything.
Ohioans see more money going out the door, and not enough money coming in.
And it’s because the system is rigged. Too many Ohioans are getting the short end of the stick while people in power are doing favors for billionaires and corporate special interests. You are working harder than ever, but you can’t get ahead.
But instead of working to bring down costs and taking on corporate interests, politicians in Washington are making things worse. Politicians like Jon Husted.
Ohio deserves better and Ohioans are showing up and insisting on change. Last night was an important step in that fight because it brought us _one step closer_ to flipping this seat and retaking Senate control.
**But we also know this battleground race is about to get harder.**
A new poll shows me down by 3 points. National Republicans are pouring nearly $80 million into Ohio to defeat us – more than they’re spending in any other battleground state. And a GOP super PAC just launched a seven-figure ad buy attacking me.
**They know Ohio is in play. They know we can win. And they know that if we do, we can flip the Senate.**
_The Cook Political Report_ now calls this race a “Toss Up.” That matters. So does the grassroots energy we’ve built together.
That’s why we set an ambitious goal: to raise $1 million by the end of the week so we can make critical investments across the state and reach voters in every corner of Ohio. [**So if you’re able, will you chip in $20, split between my campaign and the DNC, to help us start the general election strong and flip this seat and more?**](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/em-dnc-brown-split?refcode=em_20260506_7027_fr&amount=20&refcode2=7027_22930333_UmHgaQ&akid=7027%2E22930333%2EUmHgaQ)

The 14th Amendment was written after the Civil War to protect the rights of freed slaves -- not to grant automatic citizenship to the children of illegal immigrants.
Section 1 is crystal clear in its original intent: "All persons born or naturalized in the United States, and subject to the jurisdiction thereof..." That jurisdiction clause matters. A lot. In my latest video, I break down the history, the text, and why this amendment was never meant to be a blanket "birthright citizenship" policy for those who enter the country illegally.
We've watched this loophole get stretched far beyond what the framers intended -- and the consequences are playing out at our borders every single day. If you care about the Constitution, rule of law, and what "subject to the jurisdiction thereof" actually means, this one is for you. Watch the full video here: [Watch Now: Born in the USA... But Who Was the 14th Amendment Really For?](https://substack.com/redirect/8b365c49-c382-4906-98cd-feecc2bced22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
What do you think? Was the 14th Amendment intended for this? Drop your thoughts below -- and share this with someone who still believes in the actual meaning of our founding documents. Truth over narrative. Always. -- Kathy

### Ohio primary reactions, surprises, and the races that deserve a deeper autopsy
| | [The Angry Democrat](https://substack.com/@theangrydem)

**First, congrats to everyone who won.**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/1d5af07e-575c-4a12-a5ef-63a007ecae7c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Congrats to everyone who put their name on the ballot and actually ran. Now we move on to November.
And thank you to everybody who tuned into the live stream last night. Around 80 people popped in, even with the technical difficulties and the original link having to be changed. I know that left some people scrambling to find the stream, so I appreciate everyone who stuck with it.
I streamed for about two and a half hours and went to bed right before the race was officially called for Poindexter. But honestly, by that point, the writing was on the wall. I was already saying on the stream that it looked like it should be called for him.
Some races were over so fast that you barely had time to boot up the computer, log in, find the results page, and pretend there was suspense.
But that is primary night. Sometimes you get a fight. Sometimes you don't.
So let's go through the races I was watching and what stood out.
* * *
### The Statewide Races Were Mostly Blowouts
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e46f6e9f-2280-4216-ae4e-52d612caacc1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
For governor, it is going to be Vivek Ramaswamy versus Amy Acton in November. Ramaswamy absolutely dominated the Republican primary, beating Casey Putsch, also known as Casey the Car Guy, in a race that was called almost immediately after the polls closed.
I do not think there is some massive insight to pull from that race. Of course, if there is a competitor on the ballot, some people are going to vote for the competitor. That does not mean there was a real movement. That does not mean the party was in trouble.
The Republican-endorsed candidate, who had the endorsement behind him long before the signature deadline, won easily. It was not close.
* * *
### Sherrod Brown
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/59c482ca-461f-4573-9898-ca2d6d39ebcd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In the Senate race, it will be Sherrod Brown versus Jon Husted. Brown also had his race called in like 12 minutes after the polls closed, defeating Ron Kincaid in the Democratic primary.
You still have to give people like Ron Kincaid credit for making the attempt. Running is not easy. Putting your name on the ballot is not easy. But this race was never really in doubt.
* * *
### Ohio's 7th District Deserves a Deep Dive
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/657e7f1e-14e5-4ae8-8f76-d95752558855?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ohio's 7th District was the number one race on my radar, for obvious reasons.
Brian Poindexter took command of that race once the votes really started coming in. Early on, it looked closer between Poindexter and Ed FitzGerald, but as the night went on, the margin kept growing. Poindexter ended up winning the race with about 37 percent of the vote, beating FitzGerald by around 10,000 votes, followed by Laura Rodriguez-Carbone and Michael Eisner.
This is one of those races that needs a deeper dive. There were a lot of candidates, a lot of perspectives, and honestly, a lot of strong people in the field. The votes were spread all across the ballot, which tells me voters were actually looking, thinking, comparing, and making their own personal decisions.
But in the end, Poindexter dominated.
* * *
### The Congressional Races Set Up Some Real November Fights
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f9af5279-e2bd-4fbc-bfe3-fa966539ef08?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In Ohio's 11th District, Shontel Brown dominated her primary and will be heading back to Congress. The general election there is more procedure than actual suspense.
* * *
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/9c74f725-6c7b-4716-9780-c2280f1e40d6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
**HOWEVER** , Over in Ohio's 9th District, Derek Merrin won the Republican primary and will face Congresswoman Marcy Kaptur in November. Multiple outlets projected Merrin's win, setting up a rematch against Kaptur, who has represented the district since 1983 and remains one of the toughest people in Ohio politics to beat.
And yes, I am still calling her the Iron Babushka (I just cant stop laughing about that name from [D.J. Byrnes](https://open.substack.com/users/737165-dj-byrnes?utm_source=mentions) _The Rooster_).
Republicans poured a lot of money and energy into that primary because they think Kaptur is vulnerable. Derek Merrin won clearly, Josh Williams raised serious money, and Madison Sheahan also had attention around her campaign. But Merrin came out on top, and now Republicans get the matchup they were looking for.
To be perfectly honest, I would still not bet against Marcy Kaptur. I do not care how the district looks on paper. I do not care how much money Republicans raise. I do not care how many times people say this is the year she is finally vulnerable. People have been trying to take her down for a long time, and she is still standing.
* * *
### The Attorney General and Secretary of State Races
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/8b15a1bd-8247-4f07-a012-b1643e074ba7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
In the attorney general race, Democratic-endorsed candidate John Kulewicz won the nomination and will face Keith Faber in November.
To be perfectly honest, I think Elliot Forhan overperformed statewide. Considering the easily Googleable baggage attached to him, rightfully or wrongfully, I was surprised by how well he did overall. But in Cuyahoga County, where he is more known, he got trounced. That tells you something too. Sometimes familiarity helps. Sometimes familiarity hurts.
* * *
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bec64785-e7b9-469d-9984-5e0d456f9830?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The Secretary of State race was the one that surprised me more. Allison Russo beat Bryan Hambley pretty decisively.
That one deserves an autopsy.
Hambley's support seemed extremely robust. He raised real money. He had grassroots energy. He had people talking. He looked, at least from the outside, like someone who could make the race close or maybe even pull off the upset.
And then he got beat by a lot.
That does not mean the campaign was fake. It does not mean the support was meaningless. But it does mean we need to be honest about the limits of online enthusiasm, grassroots visibility, and fundraising when you are going up against the party-insider candidate. Russo is now headed to November against Robert Sprague, and that race will be one to watch.
* * *
### Congrats!
Congratulations to everyone who ran. **Seriously**. Running for office is hard. Putting your name on a ballot is hard. Taking criticism, raising money, knocking doors, answering questions, and asking people to trust you is hard.
And congratulations to the winners who are now moving on to November.
Now it is time for the party to back the Democratic candidates. Ohio is still a heavily gerrymandered state, and these races are still uphill battles. Winning a primary is one thing. Winning in November is something else entirely. There is a lot more work ahead.
Over the next couple of months, we are going to keep analyzing these races. We are going to look at what happened, what worked, what did not, where the money went, where outside spending mattered, where endorsements mattered, and where voters made their own decisions despite all of it. And trust me, we are still going to call balls and strikes when it comes to spending, strategy, messaging, and anything else that happens along the way.
That is the point of **The Angry Democrat.** It is to make sure the conversation keeps flowing, even when that conversation is uncomfortable, and even when it is about our own party.
But in the meantime...
## Stay Angry.

| Greater Georgia Newsletter May 2026
---
| Georgia is heading into a critical stretch and the decisions being made at the ballot box will shape what comes next.
Elections are underway, and your voice will determine the direction of our state.
That's why Greater Georgia is focused on registering voters, educating Georgians on the issues, and expanding engagement in every corner of the Peach State.
Because when informed voters show up, Georgia wins.

|
## Next250
---
| For 250 years, America has been defined by those willing to step up and lead.
Now, it's our turn.
Join Greater Georgia this summer for Next250, an exclusive conference for Georgia's top activists to gain the training, skills, and strategy necessary to shape what comes next for Georgia and our nation.
Apply below to be among the first to see our rollout of featured speakers!
The Next250 starts here. You won't want to miss it.

## Georgia Judicial Voter Guide
---
Today, Greater Georgia launched our online voter guide focused on the state's judicial races, including the Georgia Supreme Court and Georgia Court of Appeals.
The voter guide includes an interactive tool for voters to look up county-based judicial races occurring throughout Georgia, an overview of the Georgia Supreme Court and Court of Appeals with background information on candidates, and key details to help voters better understand the role and importance of these courts.

## Voter Registration Push
---
| Greater Georgia Action recently wrapped its latest push to register new voters ahead of the state's April 20th registration deadline.
The effort targeted a universe of approximately 100,000 unregistered Georgians and included a coordinated mix of direct mail, digital ads, and text messages encouraging registration ahead of the May primaries.
By the end of the campaign, the program delivered more than 200,000 direct contacts to Georgians across the state - significantly expanding awareness and engagement at a critical moment.

| **🚨 BREAKING NEWS FROM OKLAHOMA 🚨** As we await the Supreme Court's decision in _Louisiana v. FDA_ , which will determine whether mail and pharmacy access to mifepristone can continue while litigation proceeds, we have disastrous news out of Oklahoma to share.

[Oklahoma lawmakers just passed HB 1168—a bill that criminalizes providing medication abortion as "drug trafficking"—and they did it in secret.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/130832560/619088613/2141984067?sourceid=1151334&utm_campaign=26emama-0501aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=vetohb1168&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YmQxOTYzMy00YzQ5LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pwFjz2W7qpLBYEZpICRoCjtbI2vL4JzfDGC90AuS4zw=&emci=7c83ea0a-b045-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7bd19633-4c49-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)

Under this bill, even a parent could be convicted of a felony and thrown in jail for 10 years for helping their child get an abortion. [This is a disgusting attempt to scare Oklahomans out of seeking abortion care and scare parents, friends, and providers away from helping them.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/130832564/619088615/2141984067?sourceid=1151334&utm_campaign=26emama-0501aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=vetohb1168&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YmQxOTYzMy00YzQ5LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pwFjz2W7qpLBYEZpICRoCjtbI2vL4JzfDGC90AuS4zw=&emci=7c83ea0a-b045-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7bd19633-4c49-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)

The bill sat dormant for over a year. Then, without warning, without public notice, without giving senators a chance to respond, it cleared the Senate last week and is now headed to the Governor's desk. | [FIGHT BACK NOW](https://click.everyaction.com/k/130832566/619088616/2141984067?sourceid=1151334&utm_campaign=26emama-0501aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=vetohb1168&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YmQxOTYzMy00YzQ5LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pwFjz2W7qpLBYEZpICRoCjtbI2vL4JzfDGC90AuS4zw=&emci=7c83ea0a-b045-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7bd19633-4c49-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)
---
This dangerous bill would:
* Create a new felony crime called "trafficking an abortion-inducing drug"—punishable by up to 10 years in prison and $100,000 in fines
* Target anyone who delivers medication abortion with the intent to provide it to someone in Oklahoma
* Makes it a crime to even possess medication abortion if they can prove it was to help someone get an abortion
* Put patients at risk, with no explicit exemption for pregnant people themselves

This is not just about Oklahoma. [It's part of a growing national strategy—with similar laws already enacted in Mississippi—to equate mailing medication abortion with "drug trafficking" and criminalize the networks that help people access care.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/130832567/619088618/2141984067?sourceid=1151334&utm_campaign=26emama-0501aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=vetohb1168&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YmQxOTYzMy00YzQ5LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pwFjz2W7qpLBYEZpICRoCjtbI2vL4JzfDGC90AuS4zw=&emci=7c83ea0a-b045-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7bd19633-4c49-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237) More states are watching. More states will follow.

Oklahoma politicians are so fixated on forcing people to have children that they are willing to tear families apart and throw parents in jail. These anti-abortion legislators are using backroom tactics to pass these laws without scrutiny. [We cannot afford to be caught off guard.](https://click.everyaction.com/k/130832568/619088622/2141984067?sourceid=1151334&utm_campaign=26emama-0501aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=vetohb1168&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YmQxOTYzMy00YzQ5LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pwFjz2W7qpLBYEZpICRoCjtbI2vL4JzfDGC90AuS4zw=&emci=7c83ea0a-b045-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7bd19633-4c49-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)
[DEFEND MEDICATION ABORTION](https://click.everyaction.com/k/130832573/619088623/2141984067?sourceid=1151334&utm_campaign=26emama-0501aax-on&utm_medium=ea&utm_source=email&utm_content=vetohb1168&amtOpts=&recurringAmtOpts=&am=&recurringAm=&is_optimized_ask=true&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9DRlJSL0NGUlIvMS85NTk4MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI3YmQxOTYzMy00YzQ5LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=pwFjz2W7qpLBYEZpICRoCjtbI2vL4JzfDGC90AuS4zw=&emci=7c83ea0a-b045-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=7bd19633-4c49-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=954237)
