I wrote last time1 about how, as older people accumulate more wealth and political power, [young people are falling behind in this country](https://substack.com/redirect/90d909d9-2a2b-49a6-a92e-0c40e6ce234c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
[](https://substack.com/redirect/90d909d9-2a2b-49a6-a92e-0c40e6ce234c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Younger Americans are falling behind (Part 1)](https://substack.com/redirect/90d909d9-2a2b-49a6-a92e-0c40e6ce234c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
---
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/profile/12425779-ben-samuels)| | *
---|---|---
| Apr 8
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/90d909d9-2a2b-49a6-a92e-0c40e6ce234c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
What I left out of that: housing. Housing is, by far, the largest expense for American families; it [accounts for more than one-third of household spending](https://substack.com/redirect/45d5b23d-9e8e-402d-982f-af876a5708f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).2 Over the past few decades, housing has become increasingly unaffordable and increasingly concentrated in the hands of seniors.
If policymakers are serious about helping younger Americans keep up, addressing rising housing costs is the most powerful thing that they can do.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MTk0ODA4ODM1LCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzc4MDczMjIxLCJleHAiOjIwOTM2NDkyMjEsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.N4Pv243mJxDSgoOl-e2wSLv6g5BHwEG4oXoF_IhZTW0?)
> _**Article summary:**_
> * _Homeownership is less and less attainable for young people and lower-income people._
> * _Missouri 's proposed tax policies to address housing affordability will make things worse, not better._
> * _Immigration and tariff policies are driving up the cost of housing. We may be stuck with both until '28, but policymakers have other options to reduce housing costs._
>

### Housing is getting more expensive
The data backs up what all of us already know: housing has gotten much more expensive.
Since 1970, as far back as this measurement goes, inflation-adjusted residential property prices have gone up 2.6×.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/075799ae-8fcb-4996-abfa-173312df30db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis](https://substack.com/redirect/075799ae-8fcb-4996-abfa-173312df30db?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The situation is [much more acute for renters](https://substack.com/redirect/a4286ed7-edfb-48ca-8a09-340d3fbe6812?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and renters are already poorer to begin with: the [median net worth for a homeowner is 38× more](https://substack.com/redirect/fdd3bd69-1d14-412b-8ecd-3d7ca87cad61?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) than the median net worth for a renter.3
A recent report from the Joint Center for Housing Studies at Harvard found that a [first-time homebuyer needs to be making at least $126,700](https://substack.com/redirect/a17c9d06-2252-4f9e-af41-143f76833a24?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to afford the median American home, a dramatic increase from just five years ago, when a first-time homebuyer needed only $79,300.4 [Only 33% of American households can afford to buy a median-priced home](https://substack.com/redirect/89d2f1ad-c223-43e0-9f3a-51a6524daf22?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
All of this paints a clear picture: housing is increasingly unaffordable and unattainable.
### Younger people and lower-income people are hit hardest by this
A [stat that blows me away](https://substack.com/redirect/cd0604c6-30bf-42bd-b9ff-4f4162182a16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
* In 2007, the median homebuyer was born in 1968.
* In 2024, the median homebuyer was born in 1968.5

That's nuts! Seventeen years on, the median cohort of homebuyers hasn't budged. It's an alarming lack of generational movement.
And even that doesn't tell the full story.
In 2024, the most recent year for which there's data, the average age of a [householder](https://substack.com/redirect/08f35861-ecde-49ac-bc5a-bf6cdacb3f42?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)6 was 52.2,7 but in lower-income homes, that average age is significantly higher.8
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/756d45c3-96fd-4ad5-a15d-9de8fa41e9e8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: [U.S. Census Bureau](https://substack.com/redirect/8a1e358e-940f-432f-9ec2-80914f6e8da8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Homeownership is an extremely powerful path to building wealth](https://substack.com/redirect/225dd2b8-363c-49c3-868c-eb5a50204ba3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). What this shows us is that the door to homeownership is available to fewer and fewer lower-income Americans, and we're deepening wealth inequality in the U.S.
Housing has never been cheap, but in decades past, lower-income families were able to buy houses in a way that's much less attainable today.
That isn't limited to homeownership. Regardless of whether they own or rent, poor households spend significantly more (as a percentage of total annual spending) on housing than higher-income households do.9
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/02a358fc-0c7b-4128-9c90-74414982bfa6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Source: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis; Bureau of Labor Statistics
There's really only one easy way to afford a home in the U.S.: inherit it. In California, [18% of all property transfers last year were inheritances](https://substack.com/redirect/7e854a68-2137-4d75-85e1-c8ee992ec899?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and while that's unusually high, 9% of all home transfers nationwide in 2025 were inheritances. That [number is climbing fast](https://substack.com/redirect/cb394b05-0cbe-440f-8f02-56a607e5f013?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
But not everyone stands to inherit a house from their parents, and--to state the plainly obvious--[rich people tend to inherit more money](https://substack.com/redirect/2599bacf-4b51-4e6c-8040-226627912c1c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).10
What does all of this tell us? It's not easy for even middle- and high-income people to afford homes, necessarily. Higher housing prices hit everyone. But for anyone young and lower income, it's completely out of reach.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=194808835&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk0ODA4ODM1LCJpYXQiOjE3NzgwNzMyMjEsImV4cCI6MTc4MDY2NTIyMSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.kpBwruDsg4VTMI1NtTbKdoPOAq-VN_H5xSHOXrfFwhQ)
### What shouldn't we do about this?
Well, let's start with what _not_ to do: property tax freezes are a bad idea.
[Prop 13 in California](https://substack.com/redirect/1d01ecc3-7029-4926-8e9e-7bf6bc6b37a0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which passed in 1978, is [uniquely bad policy](https://substack.com/redirect/29e42cc1-93ad-4924-819a-6b3c31e97273?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It drives up the cost of housing and makes it artificially expensive to move; its [unique provisions protecting people who inherit properties](https://substack.com/redirect/2ea167c9-8256-4af6-8528-2289e9b7dc9a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) are part of the reason California has such a high inherited property rate.
I'm bringing this up because of [Senate Bill 3 in Missouri](https://substack.com/redirect/908290bc-0e30-418f-bb72-ed4d1c179a6d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which does something substantively similar. In the (low-turnout) municipal elections last month, 97 of the state's counties11 voted on [whether to take up the legislature's offer to freeze or limit property tax increases](https://substack.com/redirect/68ea4445-de7c-4fdc-9141-f3714dd40501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
**This is bad policy**. It risks creating many of the same issues in Missouri that exist in California: artificially depressed housing supply and higher housing costs, for starters.
If the goal is to make housing broadly affordable, this risks doing the exact opposite, particularly if you're young and don't already own a home.
### What can we do about this?
Addressing housing affordability is tricky, because costs are driven by so many different factors, and because those factors vary so much between rural areas and cities (and from one city to another).
But two things that'd address housing costs right away:
1. **Tariff reform**. Last year, tariffs [increased the cost of new home construction](https://substack.com/redirect/ac4c4de5-416e-454c-90aa-c03ee4bfb3b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by $10,900.12 Who knows what the latest with tariffs is--it seems to change just about every week--but their impact on the cost of housing is real and lasting.
2. **Immigration reform**.

Among construction workers in America, [26.3% are immigrants](https://substack.com/redirect/c2fc37e1-62fc-4306-b744-dc1773454d88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--meaningfully higher than the [14.8% of residents in America who are immigrants](https://substack.com/redirect/4d97262d-8dd0-4401-9e0d-ed8e86e5e1c5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). It's even higher in certain construction specialties.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c2fc37e1-62fc-4306-b744-dc1773454d88?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Of these immigrants, many are undocumented. In 2023, **[undocumented immigrants were 19%](https://substack.com/redirect/3cdb6d9a-ea2b-4209-941c-8f0510001cc3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of the country's construction workers**.
Like it or not, the way that we've set up the system today, undocumented immigrants are a vital part of the nation's construction economy. Indiscriminately deporting people without any plan for how we're going to address the labor shortages is a problem for housing costs.13
In the wake of the California wildfires last year, Realtor.com--hardly a partisan voice--reported that [homes were taking longer to rebuild](https://substack.com/redirect/b1201440-1d5f-41d6-a47c-a380d594a459?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) because of ICE raids.14 Federal policy is having a real impact on our ability to build new housing.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2440398&post_id=194808835&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk0ODA4ODM1LCJpYXQiOjE3NzgwNzMyMjEsImV4cCI6MTc4MDY2NTIyMSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI0NDAzOTgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.kpBwruDsg4VTMI1NtTbKdoPOAq-VN_H5xSHOXrfFwhQ)
I don't expect Congress to meaningfully address immigration anytime soon. But a temporary work visa for people to come to the U.S. and work construction jobs would alleviate these concerns--and it'd reduce incentives for people to come to the U.S. illegally.
Immigration and tariffs are intensely partisan; there are bipartisan policies in the works too. The [21st Century ROAD to Housing Act](https://substack.com/redirect/c2aac02b-cdaa-4369-b443-a647d32c5142?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)15 that's currently meandering through Congress has strong support from both parties and a good shot of passing.
The [Bipartisan Policy Center has a rundown of what's in the bill](https://substack.com/redirect/e76ec11c-3ae3-40eb-b491-a345a9803a1b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), if you're curious to read more. A good number of the provisions will help address housing affordability.
At the state level, there are other common-sense reforms that'd reduce housing costs: [getting rid of parking minimums](https://substack.com/redirect/b9efa534-d65e-49a7-8930-21f23ff2cc16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [changing zoning around ADUs](https://substack.com/redirect/d96e8555-d237-4e7d-a40d-c905be03c71c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), for instance.
Finally: throwing money at this is always a tempting, and politically easy, solution. It shouldn't be the only solution, and the U.S. is already way too deep in debt, but I'd be remiss if I didn't discuss it as an option.
Setting aside my aversion to the name, [Trump Accounts](https://substack.com/redirect/6c64de6e-d49e-4ca6-8498-c733c463c046?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) had potential, but their implementation was flawed: because [parents have to opt in](https://substack.com/redirect/258d8200-6d5e-4c6a-9a67-9a82e11874d7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and because of its structure, it [heavily favors higher-income families](https://substack.com/redirect/5aae9f6d-aab4-491b-93fe-b26b9f48b78f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) over lower-income ones. But so-called [baby bonds](https://substack.com/redirect/f267514e-1970-4a06-90cc-b73ae76a8acb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), done right, can reduce income inequality.
Something similar when it comes to housing--a tailored, targeted plan that'd help lower-income people buy homes--could make housing more attainable for more Americans. Moreover, it's possible even at the state level.
The status quo isn't working. Younger Americans are being left behind. Something has to change--and states can't rely on a dysfunctional federal government to do much.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MTk0ODA4ODM1LCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzc4MDczMjIxLCJleHAiOjIwOTM2NDkyMjEsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.N4Pv243mJxDSgoOl-e2wSLv6g5BHwEG4oXoF_IhZTW0?)
_**Feel free to share this post with someone who will find this interesting.** If you're reading this email because someone sent it to you, [please consider subscribing](https://substack.com/redirect/d6d51870-c08f-4c1a-907a-71149b52ecef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)._
1
I try to write every two weeks or so, but sometimes work and other obligations get in the way. So it's been a month this time.
2
Not related to this post at all, but it's interesting to me that "Tobacco products and smoking supplies" is a [standalone measure in the Bureau of Labor Statistics data](https://substack.com/redirect/45d5b23d-9e8e-402d-982f-af876a5708f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), as is alcohol. (Together, smoking and booze make up 1.2% of U.S. household spending.)
3
One interesting note here is that adjusting for inflation, housing costs actually went _down_ slightly for homeowners, [according to Census data](https://substack.com/redirect/a4286ed7-edfb-48ca-8a09-340d3fbe6812?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), despite the cost of homes going up. Here's why: "Part of the reason for the drop in owner cost was that more homes did not have a mortgage. The share of owned homes with a mortgage fell from 67.9% in 2005 to 59.7% in 2024."
That's also part of the reason why keeping homes within families, which the _[Wall Street Journal](https://substack.com/redirect/7e854a68-2137-4d75-85e1-c8ee992ec899?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[ article](https://substack.com/redirect/7e854a68-2137-4d75-85e1-c8ee992ec899?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) I mention above discusses, is such an appealing option for families who can afford it.
4
The two main drivers here are property values, which have increased by 16%, and interest rates, which have more than doubled.
5
A few things to note on this:
* The math here comes from p. 10 and is reasonably straightforward:
* In 2007, the median buyer was 39. 2007 − 39 = 1968.
* In 2024, the median buyer was 56. 2024 − 56 = 1968.
* This is survey data from the [National Association of Realtors](https://substack.com/redirect/cd0604c6-30bf-42bd-b9ff-4f4162182a16?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and while I do believe it's robust, it's not always quite as reliable as Census or Fed data. In practice, that doesn't mean it's wrong, but it probably will be a bit noisier from year to year.
* h/t to my friend A. for pointing this out to me.

6
Here's the definition of "householder," which is very close to--but not exactly the same as--homeowner:
> The householder refers to the person (or one of the people) in whose name the housing unit is owned or rented (maintained) or, if there is no such person, any adult member, excluding roomers, boarders, or paid employees.
For our purposes, it's close enough to homeowner, but it's not exactly the same thing, so I wanted to call that out.
7
One thing worth noting: homeowner, householder, homebuyer, and home resident all measure different, though related, things. It's why some of the numbers might not always line up perfectly, though I am trying to be precise with my wording.
8
How I calculated this:
* I used this Census data: [Age of Householder-Households, by Total Money Income, Type of Household, Race and Hispanic Origin of Householder.](https://substack.com/redirect/8a1e358e-940f-432f-9ec2-80914f6e8da8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
* By $5,000 income brackets, there's a category for "mean age of householder." With that, I pulled three weighted averages:
* Incomes up to $59,999.
* Incomes between $60,000 and $99,999.
* Incomes above $100,000.

9
I expected this data to be easier to find, but it really isn't; I had to aggregate it myself. Here's where this data comes from:
* The St. Louis Federal Reserve, which has data on housing costs by quintile: [1-20](https://substack.com/redirect/ae944687-15c0-4c7f-9191-ca60db0570f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [21-40](https://substack.com/redirect/e0c8425e-f0c8-4b82-9544-5d8b8acf2e36?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [41-60](https://substack.com/redirect/99543731-f03f-47de-92d1-89aec89dd984?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [61-80](https://substack.com/redirect/1acf7a51-3eff-4c56-b2ef-bac0d15e940f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [81-100](https://substack.com/redirect/1914e776-5a87-4d98-9f5e-1f6c14ed2216?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Then, I took annual expenditures data [from the Bureau of Labor Statistics](https://substack.com/redirect/6510109d-a0d8-4424-9c68-e663a8f892d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
* Together, that gave me the data I needed to get to a percentage of overall spending.

10
I probably didn't need a citation for this, but you're getting one anyway.
11
Your reminder that Missouri has _way_ too many counties.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/62bd7162-fead-4e82-8dc2-d219ea251892?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |
#### [Missouri's insanely bloated government(s)](https://substack.com/redirect/62bd7162-fead-4e82-8dc2-d219ea251892?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/profile/12425779-ben-samuels)| | *
---|---|---
| April 8, 2025
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/62bd7162-fead-4e82-8dc2-d219ea251892?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
12
[Costs for existing homeowners went up too](https://substack.com/redirect/6d8137af-3292-4b7b-95fe-5c6936301742?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), because of increased costs of appliances, renovations, etc.
13
Undocumented immigrants live in the places they work, and that has an impact on local housing costs. An uptick in undocumented immigrants led to [rents increasing by 1.4% and house prices increasing by 2.2%](https://substack.com/redirect/1b6f704d-564f-4070-9594-e79de6d3961e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), though the impacts of that vary considerably from one metro area to the next. Immigrants, documented or otherwise, are not evenly distributed across the U.S.
14
This is a telling passage [from that Realtor.com article](https://substack.com/redirect/b1201440-1d5f-41d6-a47c-a380d594a459?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg):
> George Carrillo, CEO of the Hispanic Construction Council, points to a [jobsite in Tallahassee](https://substack.com/redirect/6dc4c50a-1de4-4b54-9eeb-848caadf4b2c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) where ICE detained 100 out of 180 workers.
> "You would think that the next day at least 80 people would show back up to work," he says. "Actually, only 20 showed up the next day."
> That kind of fear ripples through every layer of the rebuild. These aren't easily replaced workers--they're skilled, experienced teams. And when they disappear, the replacements often aren't equal.
> "There's an added complication," explains Pia Orrenius, vice president at the Federal Reserve Bank of Dallas, who studies the labor impact of immigration policy. "You might think the equivalent worker would cost more, but if you can't find someone with the same skills and experience, you may be hiring a replacement who's less qualified."
15
An unimportant point: we're 26 years into the 21st century. I don't think we should be labeling things as "21st century" anymore if they're meant to signal innovation and improvement.

subject: I haven’t felt this hopeful since organizing for Bernie in 2016

body:
[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37772?t=1060&refcode=email-20260506_v&akid=10691%2E5885482%2EKR8ZQj ]Our Revolution logo

Hi Peter Willis,

I'm Susana, a proud organizer with Our Revolution in California.

I never really thought of myself as an “organizer” until the 2016 Bernie
Sanders campaign and now it’s pretty much my life. From mobilizing my
community for the No Kings protests to standing up to ICE to fighting for
Medicare for All, I’ve done it all.

But the truth is it’s been an incredibly tough and scary year. I’m writing
today because I’m finally feeling hopeful once again.

This election cycle we have a real chance to change our future. In the
coming months, we can elect Tom Steyer as our next Governor in California
– a candidate who is steadfast in his commitment to Medicare for All and
making billionaires pay their fair share – while winning other progressive
victories up and down the ballot.

I haven’t been this excited since I knocked on doors for Bernie and felt
history was in our hands. And I mean that. I see a path for us to win
major victories this cycle, and I hope you'll step up with me to make it
happen.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37772?t=1106&amount=22&amounts=9%2C22%2C27%2C46%2C66&refcode=email-20260506nd&firstname=Peter%20Willis&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&akid=10691%2E5885482%2EKR8ZQj ]Will you chip in $10 (or whatever you can) today to power our work to
elect a powerful slate of progressive leaders up and down the ballot?

If you've stored your payment information with ActBlue Express, your
donation to Our Revolution will process immediately.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37772?t=1096&express_lane=true&amount=66&refcode=email-20260506nd&amounts=9%2C22%2C27%2C46%2C66&firstname=Peter%20Willis&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&akid=10691%2E5885482%2EKR8ZQj ]CHIP IN $66 [ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37772?t=1097&amount=9&refcode=email-20260506nd&amounts=9%2C22%2C27%2C46%2C66&firstname=Peter%20Willis&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&akid=10691%2E5885482%2EKR8ZQj ]CHIP IN OTHER AMOUNT

This is about so much more than one governor’s race. We fought to get the
billionaire tax on the California ballot, and now we’ve gotta pass it.
We’re backing a set of AMAZING progressives to take back Congress: Mai
Vang, Audrey Denney, Randy Villegas, Eric Jones, and Aisha Wahab.

And I love organizing with Our Revolution because of its focus on
down-ballot races — critical seats on city councils and school boards that
have a huge impact on our lives. There are too many great unsung local
leaders to list.

If we win, California can be a model for the rest of the country, showing
what we can achieve on issues like housing, childcare, and Medicare for
All.

Organizing like this is happening across the country because Our
Revolution is rooted in the grassroots and doing the work every day. Every
text, every donation, every neighbor volunteering at a phone bank means we
are that much closer to winning real change — here in California and
around the country.

Together, we are the backbone of the movement, and times are heavy. But I
truly believe we can make the spark of hope I feel right now a reality.

[ https://act.ourrevolution.com/go/37772?t=1103&amount=22&refcode=email-20260506nd&amounts=9%2C22%2C27%2C46%2C66&firstname=Peter%20Willis&lastname=&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=18326&city=Cresco&state=PA&akid=10691%2E5885482%2EKR8ZQj ]I know folks are hurting in a lot of ways, and it makes me want to fight
even harder for those who can’t. So if you’re able to spare anything at
all, $5 or $15, I want to say thank you for making it possible for me and
our whole Our Revolution community to do this work.

It’s an honor to be with all of you in this fight.

When we organize, we win.

| | | [](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqsFlYb8tSgv_iNH9eUO8IibbLOfX6PT-3gGyMq8W09rTWGkhpOgx1v3_y0wksFDKhC57umKjg75i7zm7NBFpOE9lWw97IYC8yPYy0Kk-UeyQi8kYtPLtV6LYtIE7v0wNmAQstewwxV4vS1BlpBZR1AeLoLGLMmjaj0k1dmfeZt3IcnQbbJTE683AGvP4UdS6JbB5Kqxgx4wrB4qPO3gNSXETASqfbQ7MjyR88TPTrLcxQIWYhOqT2ae2IAsrzJ_jNaVxLnXMz9SX3TZfAYFsZzE1PCkoMRq5MrTYIeYvsKFHmX4GI-VOh8tWuiZ2cpV_ajRZsD31M8Q18Vtz50FTVPp/4qe/kd1rISiFQSaIGKfa75aUzw/h0/h001.53lI4hDKFKQJWGF6fV6u0Cn-RVEBhfhOW6PFdONDdB0)Friend — On May Day, or International Workers Day, I took a moment to reflect on where this fight for workers’ rights began. I celebrated Día del Trabajador with FACETS, a nonprofit serving our neighbors facing homelessness, hunger, and poverty here in Fairfax County. And I went back to Fairmont Gardens — the first place I called home after moving to this country. Back then, I was working three jobs just to make ends meet. I remember what that felt like. The stress. The exhaustion. The constant pressure just to get by. That experience is why I’ve spent my life fighting for working families. clean_body: | | | — On May Day, or International Workers Day, I took a moment to reflect on where this fight for workers’ rights began. I celebrated Día del Trabajador with FACETS, a nonprofit serving our neighbors facing homelessness, hunger, and poverty here in Fairfax County. And I went back to Fairmont Gardens — the first place I called home after moving to this country. Back then, I was working three jobs just to make ends meet. I remember what that felt like. The stress. The exhaustion. The constant pressure just to get by. That experience is why I’ve spent my life fighting for working families. Because no one working full-time, or multiple jobs, should be struggling to survive. And that’s why this campaign is powered by people — not corporate PACs, special interests, billionaires, or Super PACs. If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately. Working people deserve a livable wage. They deserve dignity. They deserve leaders who will fight for them. That’s why I’m running for Congress, and why I’m committed to flipping this swing seat blue and the House blue this November. [**FIRST:**]() Clarence Thomas voted to unleash _Citizens United_ on our Democracy.

[**THEN:**]() He tried to DESTROY all remaining campaign finance laws.

Patriot,

Letter writing is such a lost art these days.

When I first joined the Marine Corps, nothing felt better than getting letters from loved ones.

And as I was looking back on that experience, I got the idea to write a letter to you.

You're so important to me - no, really.

If it weren't for you, I wouldn't have the incredible opportunity to serve our country that I have as Vice President.

Your opinion matters to me. That's why I want to personally invite you to take our America First Survey.

As the America First movement continues to take on new challenges, I need to know that we're best representing you.

Please, take our survey as soon as you can so I can see your responses.

It will only take five minutes, but it would mean the world to me.

Sincerely,

JD Vance
Vice President of the United States of America

#

Team --
We always knew that Donald Trump was in the pocket of the gun lobby. Now, he and his family are profiting from it too.
[](https://go.giffords.org/go/14457?c0=giffords-em-q22026.j3JysD&refcode=em260506-1-b&t=1&akid=11454%2E3935704%2EKq9FvC)
Donald Trump Jr. recently joined the board of an online firearms retailer trying to become the “Amazon of guns.”
This comes as the Trump administration is trying to change the rules to let the USPS deliver guns through the mail with no background checks, licensing, or training.
More guns isn’t the answer. We need leaders who have the courage to push back against powerful gun lobby interests — not profiting off of them.
That’s the mission we have at GIFFORDS PAC. As we get closer to the midterm elections, we are working tirelessly to elect a gun sense majority and end the gun lobby’s influence on our politics.
To do that, we need your help.

# **Penn State law school vows to center entire institution around antiracism despite legal risks**
Penn State Dickinson Law distributed an internal five-year strategic plan pledging to make antiracist principles central to all operations--from faculty hiring and student admissions to curriculum design and research priorities. The document, **[obtained by the Washington Free Beacon](https://substack.com/redirect/a9237837-cf54-486d-b712-e79fc3bc4bda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , commits the school to prioritizing candidates from underrepresented backgrounds and implementing what it calls "antiracist critical pedagogy" throughout the institution, though the plan doesn't appear on the law school's public website.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a9237837-cf54-486d-b712-e79fc3bc4bda?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
* **Legal experts warn strategy likely violates civil rights law** : Civil rights activist Ed Blum said the approach amounts to illegal racial consideration in decision-making and predicted courts would strike it down, while the American Civil Rights Project's Dan Morenoff flagged the plan's demographic focus as potentially unconstitutional. The Justice Department has specifically warned against using "underrepresented" as a hiring criterion in recent guidance, making the written pledge particularly risky for the university.
* **Bucking national trend away from DEI** : Most universities have quietly removed antiracism language from their websites amid Trump administration scrutiny of higher education, but Penn State maintains an entire Administrative Council on Anti-Racism and Equity.

# **Chinese, Iranian foreign ministers meet in Beijing days before Trump-Xi summit amid Strait of Hormuz crisis**
Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi met with Iranian counterpart Abbas Araghchi **[in Beijing Wednesday](https://substack.com/redirect/99b1bf85-0c76-4ee3-9682-58ae33eaa9d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** --about a week before President Trump travels to China's capital for a high-stakes summit with Xi Jinping. Wang called for a "comprehensive ceasefire" and said China hopes relevant parties will quickly respond to international calls for restoring safe passage through the Strait, with Araghchi later describing the talks as "constructive" and saying both sides affirmed Iran's sovereignty rights.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/99b1bf85-0c76-4ee3-9682-58ae33eaa9d8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

They don't challenge us." Trump suggested Xi's deference stems from their personal relationship.
* **Iran praises Chinese four-point peace proposal** : Araghchi said in an X statement that Iran "appreciates the four-point proposal put forward by the Chinese side on upholding and promoting regional peace and stability" and "expects the Chinese side to continue playing a positive role in promoting peace and stopping war," while supporting establishment of a new regional security architecture.

name: Andrew Sypher, Turning Point USA
subject: We don't have enough of these right now
body:
I want to give you a picture of what’s really happening right now

| | | [](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zgh4a6svicinvinsg10vfhif9ju1kn5q0soc3ov0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1ie4oj4cjh2bs)
---
| | Friend,
---
I want to give you a picture of what's really happening right now -- not the polished version, but what it actually looks like on the ground.

Inside our office, tables are covered in supplies and open boxes. Coworkers are coming together, packing materials, sealing kits, and sending them out the door as fast as possible.
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z8j4d199gk5qbt7tl5gcb2sb6j4c7dp75i0ulbc8_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1ie4oj4cjh2bs)
---
_Above: Activism kits bound for new chapters being packed with Constitutions, chapter handbooks, American flags, and more at TPUSA HQ in Arizona_
---
These boxes aren't sitting around waiting for someone to need them.

They're already claimed. And we don't have extras.

By the time one batch goes out, more requests come in.

Different schools, different students, same situation -- they want to start something, and they're asking us to help them do it.

That's where things stand right now.

We have more students stepping up than we can fully support at the moment.

And I don't say that lightly.

Because for years, the challenge wasn't getting students the tools -- it was getting them to speak up at all. Most kept their heads down.

The Left has spent years trying to convince this generation to sit down, stay quiet, and be ashamed of their country and everything that makes it great.

And for a long time, it worked. But that's all changing.

Now, we're seeing students stand up and push back.

**We saw it clearly at Wheeling High School in the Chicago suburbs -- Charlie's alma mater. **

For the first time, students there launched a Club America chapter. It took months to get approved, but a chapter is finally there.

And now, students are standing outside with signs about free markets and freedom -- not because it's easy, but because they've decided it matters more than staying quiet.
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2z9de7c9i9k4u29c5qk3o11qiagorvjr8b4m2gq88_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1ie4oj4cjh2bs)
---
That's not something you can just manufacture. But it is something you can support when it happens.

And it's not isolated growth anymore.

**We 're now working with more than 1,450 college chapters and over 3,400 high school chapters across the country. That's real scale. **

But if you zoom out, there are roughly 27,000 high schools in America.

That means tens of thousands of campuses where the Left still dominates the conversation...

And where students are waiting for someone to help them stand up and speak.

So as much as this has grown, we're still in the early innings of what Charlie actually set out to build.

What's different now is the pace.

**Many states are moving to bring Club America chapters to every high school statewide, including: **

✅ Arkansas
✅ Florida
✅ Idaho
✅ Indiana
✅ Montana
✅ Nebraska
✅ Oklahoma
✅ South Carolina
✅ Texas
✅ Tennessee

That brings us to ten states now taking this seriously -- not just talk, but action.
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zgbhj0dpq5enpvhg31uio5j8s8s043rns5irqc40_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1ie4oj4cjh2bs)
---
That kind of expansion doesn't happen slowly.

It stacks quickly -- and it creates pressure behind the scenes to keep up.

Because every new chapter, every new student leader, every new school means more materials, more support, more follow-through.

And right now, that's where we're stretched.

We're not lacking interest or momentum.

We're working to keep up with both.

_So here 's how you can help... _

Right now, there are students ready to step up -- they just need the tools to do it.

**An activism kit puts everything they need directly into their hands: **

✅ Constitutions.
✅ Chapter guides.
✅ Flags.
✅ Materials to organize and lead.

It turns a student who wants to speak up... _into one who actually does. _

And you'll make it possible for us to keep saying yes when a student reaches out and says, "I want to start something here."

**[Each activism kit costs $25 to pack and ship to a student chapter. Will you put one into a student's hands today?](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zuj9okii5eurtumnjt5dmua3um4kgkrfvcipdu5g_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1ie4oj4cjh2bs)**
---
[ **Sponsor an Activism Kit**
**Make Your Gift Here**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zigi3h8kqb2d2jbja4vh5unohhhe5kanhcn7j39g_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1ie4oj4cjh2bs)
---
Every activism kit you help sponsor means one more student is ready to lead instead of sitting on the sidelines.

That's how we keep saying "yes" when the next student steps forward.

That's how this movement actually scales.

Because the reality is, the demand is here now.

The only question is whether we're equipped to meet it.

And that comes down to whether people like you decide to step in and help carry this forward.

**[Please commit to sending an activism kit to a conservative student today-- and help us keep building a generation that's willing to stand up and fight for this country.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zmtu6r33jetll7kuokrs18l98kql1n17jurmhgsg_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1ie4oj4cjh2bs)**
---
[ **Sponsor an Activism Kit**
**Make Your Gift Here**](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2za8odv3294h76hmq4nodjop22tt0cc38hb6l8cn0_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1ie4oj4cjh2bs)
---
One final thing: I also wanted to say thank you.

If you've supported Turning Point USA before -- whether once or many times -- you've already played a role in building what you're seeing right now.

Students finding their voice. More state partnerships. New TPUSA chapters like the one at Charlie's former high school.

This kind of momentum doesn't happen without people willing to stand behind it.

And we don't take that lightly.

I appreciate you taking the time to read this, and for everything you've already done to support this work.
---
| | **For Charlie,** **Andrew Sypher** Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA
---
[](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zrs5mt0smdhetq9dd4pk8n03n81h0ca5r1ftani8_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1ie4oj4cjh2bs)
---
[ _**Support Turning Point USA**_](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zvv64gdhjgcn1iaf99mfiouogceepgqgcqufn3n8_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1ie4oj4cjh2bs)
---
**P.S.** Friend, what you're seeing right now is something we've been working toward for years -- a generation of young Americans who are no longer willing to sit quietly while the Left dominates their schools and culture.

But moments like this don't sustain themselves.

If we don't keep up, we lose ground. It's that simple.

**We need to keep pace with the growth happening right now -- to fund more activism kits, support more chapters, and make sure no student is left standing alone after they decide to speak up. **

If you've already supported Turning Point USA in the past, thank you for carrying this movement forward every single day.

If you haven't yet, I'm asking you to step in now.

**[Help sponsor more activism kits today-- and help us keep building the next generation of Americans who are proud of their country and willing to fight for it.](http://e.americanactionnews.com/rd/9z2zh4tjipe6910n6hj09lbekf337jasvjkpv65avgo_rp22sh2s8i6epr0s1ie4oj4cjh2bs)**
---

---

Phoenix, Arizona 85044

disclaimer_text: Paid for by Julia Letlow for Louisiana
body:
Letlow’s Ballot Score Continues to Rise While Cassidy and Fleming Falter

| | |
---
| | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/uuOeuZHqOdw?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a)
| | | | | | **FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
May 6, 2026katherine@julialetlow.com
**NEW POLL: Trump-Endorsed Julia Letlow Surges Ahead in Louisiana Senate Race** _Letlow’s Ballot Score Continues to Rise While Cassidy and Fleming Falter_
**BATON ROUGE, LA** — A new Rigamer [poll](https://us.list-manage.com/FwIxZw6pMNo?e=95355a072c&c2id=cd64ea42b1b0eeac0fd7d107db75288a) shows Congresswoman Julia Letlow pulling away from the field and solidifying her position as the clear frontrunner in Louisiana’s Republican primary for the United States Senate, while support for Senator Bill Cassidy continues to erode and Fleming collapses as voters learn he is employed by DC lobbying firm while also serving as state treasurer.
The survey, conducted April 28–30, shows **Letlow surging to 32.5 percent**. At the same time, both Cassidy and John Fleming have lost ground, with **Fleming at 21.2 percent** and **Cassidy falling to 20.5 percent**.
As voters make their decisions, the race continues to move in Letlow’s direction.
The poll also highlights the depth of Cassidy’s vulnerability. **In a head-to-head runoff, Letlow defeats Cassidy by more than 22 points, 50.5 percent to 28.3 percent**.
**Letlow also leads Fleming in a head-to-head runoff by a wide margin, 42.3 percent to 30.7 percent** , further demonstrating her strength as the candidate best positioned to unite Republican voters and win.
_“This is a clear sign that Louisiana Republicans are ready for new leadership,”_**said** **Congresswoman Julia Letlow**._“They want a conservative senator who will stand with President Trump, fight for our values, and never waver. That’s the message we are taking to every corner of this state, and we’re going to keep working every single day to earn every vote.”_
_“Momentum has been building for months, and it’s unmistakable,”_**said Katherine Thordahl, communications director for Letlow for Louisiana.**_“Voters continue to break Julia’s way because they trust her to stand with President Trump and deliver for Louisiana. At the same time, Bill Cassidy’s support continues to collapse under the weight of his record. This race is coming into focus, and Republican voters know exactly who they can count on.”_
Letlow’s continued surge reflects a campaign with strong grassroots momentum, a proven record of delivering for Louisiana, and the trust of President Donald Trump.
With early voting underway, the contrast in this race is becoming clearer by the day, and Republican voters are rallying behind a candidate they trust to represent them and stand firm when it matters most.

**I came off the sidelines for one reason: Ohio families.**

Life is too expensive. Paychecks are too low. Costs are too high – utilities, health care, groceries, everything.

Ohioans see more money going out the door, and not enough money coming in.

And it's because the system is rigged. Too many Ohioans are getting the short end of the stick while people in power are doing favors for billionaires and corporate special interests. You are working harder than ever, but you can't get ahead.

But instead of working to bring down costs and taking on corporate interests, politicians in Washington are making things worse. Politicians like Jon Husted.

Ohio deserves better and Ohioans are showing up and insisting on change. Last night was an important step in that fight because it brought us _one step closer_ to flipping this seat and retaking Senate control.

**But we also know this battleground race is about to get harder.**

A new poll shows me down by 3 points. National Republicans are pouring $79 million into Ohio to defeat us – more than they're spending in any other battleground state. And Jon Husted's super PAC just launched a six‐figure ad buy attacking me.

**They know Ohio is in play. They know we can win. And they know that if we do, we can flip the Senate.**

_The Cook Political Report_ now calls this race a "Toss Up." That matters. So does the grassroots energy we've built together.

name: Case Dixon
subject: Dixon Campaign Update: 13 Days Until Election Day
body:
**Hello everyone****,**

I hope you all are having a great year so far. With just **thirteen days remaining** until Election Day, I wanted to give a quick update on the campaign and the momentum we’re continuing to build across the district.

**Endorsements**

Since my last update, we’ve been honored to receive several important endorsements, including:
* [Republican Liberty Caucus](https://www.alreporter.com/2026/03/10/republican-liberty-caucus-endorses-case-dixon-in-cd6/)
* [Alabama Republican Assembly](https://tuscaloosathread.com/gary-palmer-case-dixon-race/)
* [Stand for Health Freedom](https://www.alreporter.com/2026/04/24/case-dixon-touts-endorsement-from-anti-vax-group-in-cd6-race/)
* [Focus on America](https://alpolitics.com/case-dixon-earns-focus-on-america-endorsement/)

I’m incredibly grateful for the trust and confidence each of these organizations has placed in our campaign. Their support reflects the **growing grassroots momentum** behind this effort as we head toward May 19.

**Straw Poll Results**

On Saturday, April 25, the Jefferson County GOP hosted its Straw Poll Breakfast. I [received 47% of the vote](https://1819news.com/news/item/hudson-gentry-allen-chen-win-jefferson-county-straw-poll) in our race, showing that we are within striking distance of my opponent with less than three weeks remaining.

**This race is far from over.**
**
**
The reality is this race can absolutely be won, but only if our supporters actually show up and **vote****on May 19**.

Please make a plan now to be at the polls on Election Day, and don’t come alone. **Bring friends** , family members, neighbors, or anyone you know who believes Washington needs real reform. If every supporter brings five people to **vote for Case Dixon****on May 19** , we can win this race.

**Media and Public Statements**

I’ve continued making media appearances and issuing public statements on the issues facing our country and district. To stay up to date on interviews, articles, and campaign news, I encourage you to visit the “[News](https://dixonforuscongress.com/news/)” section of my website.

One issue I especially want to highlight is my repeated [public challenge](https://alpolitics.com/case-dixon-again-challenges-gary-palmer-to-a-no-excuses-debate/) to my opponent for a debate or public forum before Election Day. Voters deserve the opportunity to hear both candidates discuss the issues and defend their records. Unfortunately, every challenge has been **ignored**.

**Out In The District**

I’ve continued traveling across the district nearly every day, meeting with voters at city council meetings, county GOP meetings, Republican women’s clubs, grassroots events, and community gatherings.

The schedule has been nonstop, and **I’m grateful** for every conversation, handshake, and opportunity to share our message. I encourage you to follow my social media pages to stay updated on where we’ve been and where we’re headed next.

**Yard Signs**

Our yard signs are now up all across the district and continue helping us spread the message to voters every day.

If you would like a yard sign, or several to place around your community, please reply to this email with how many you’d like and the address for delivery. We’ll gladly deliver them **free of charge.**

**VERY IMPORTANT**

We are now in the **final stretc** h of this campaign with less than two weeks remaining until the Republican primary.

If you’re able, I’m asking you to consider making one **final contribution** to help us finish strong. Every donation, even modest ones, helps us continue voter outreach, distribute campaign materials, and communicate our message during these critical final days.

body:
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
Folks,
The MAGA justices on John Roberts' Supreme Court just made it easier for opponents of voting rights to rig our elections — and not for the first time.
In their latest decision, these billionaire-backed justices gutted a key part of the Voting Rights Act, making it easier for state legislatures to draw up district maps that dilute the voting power of Black and brown communities. This is how they help politicians control election results before votes are even cast.
This is not normal. This is power being taken from us. For years, John Roberts and his fellow conservative justices have chipped away at voting rights, siding with billionaire interests and politicians who don’t want to compete for our votes. Now they’ve gone further — clearing the way for maps that decide who wins before Election Day .
Send a letter to Congress: Restore the Voting Rights Act and protect our votes >> [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/maga-justices-just-gutted-voting-rights-tell-congress-to-restore-them-now/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
START WRITING NOW ⇨ [https://actionnetwork.org/letters/maga-justices-just-gutted-voting-rights-tell-congress-to-restore-them-now/?source=direct_link&referrer=group-integrity-first-voter-action-project&redirect=https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-actions]
Across the country, people are already facing real barriers — being wrongly purged from voter rolls, waiting in hours-long lines after polling places are shut down, or being blocked from voting by restrictive rules. Now, even when we fight through those obstacles and cast our ballots, politicians can redraw the map to cancel out our votes.
That’s the plan: take our votes, twist the maps, and control the outcome.
But we can fight back. When we organize, speak out, and demand action together, we can force change . Send your letter now and join the growing movement demanding Congress restore voting rights protections.

Dear Patriot, They're trying to put an innocent cop in prison for **life**. Why? For defending himself against a fleeing suspect who dragged him with a car. I've been in law enforcement for decades. I've seen the system abused. But what is happening to Officer James Brennand of San Antonio, Texas makes my blood boil, and it should make yours boil too. On October 2nd, 2022, Officer James Brennand — a decorated Army veteran who swore an oath to protect his community — spotted a car he suspected was stolen outside a McDonald's in San Antonio. He called for backup. He approached the vehicle. He ordered the driver to step out. The driver's response? He threw the car into reverse and used it as a weapon. | [Defend Officer Brennand →](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=dd391bc7552a4c049fd180cab53fcdbe&_e=yzuq-WJXG40h31sK4ZkbVFBUEi_psxT_wkwSGqt0JIa3iR6BK1l7KtgxX9ZT0-UZ2Ic22pmWLINlNi9Dzh4fAttCGSG3FU0e2q2K75O0rp_Gco8wuhoyi5Mhufk603ZS03fidc3aEZFK3aP8poTf-7-ciFu1EJPOcQMiBFvTYuFpGpsKx3wTrItSgqQ4XhIVGjLd17SuJdnRP8gw4PK_7ovDG18lMrJ8_v27DTdlHYoHojwsO1BgxNF3P5ONGmrvAALGfniYsj-uLOOm3TmjKuSB1XL8dsnjrZFR0AsCT6o5cltskFgH90_1dePunNwekSyEwKrqYe1Yu8qFs10EhK7y17ngwUe3t3yEp3fgnKcKPTfAmjHp6RIqQUym36wbT07G7nm2-ofSSfXJ0YuD-Cm2Y6MH-w_xV2SxZ1j4U9Qzy96BM6JD2gdyQOoGk6WU)

The car door slammed into Brennand. He was dragged. In that split second — outnumbered, without backup, in genuine danger — James did what every officer is trained to do. **He protected himself.**
The driver survived. The passenger was unharmed. And since that night, the driver has racked up four more arrests. **Four.**
While the man who attacked James faces no meaningful consequences, Officer Brennand has been stripped of his badge, his paycheck, and his future. A politically hungry District Attorney — more interested in headlines than justice — charged James with aggravated assault and deadly conduct. If convicted: **five years to life.**
Let that sink in. A man who served his country in the Army, who volunteered to protect the streets of San Antonio, who was dragged by a car in the line of duty — could die in prison.

| | **Spartz Wins Republican Primary**
---
| | Dear Friends,

Last night, Congresswoman Victoria Spartz issued the following statement on her renomination for the 5th Congressional District:

“I am honored that my fellow Republicans have placed their trust in me for another term. As we approach the 250th anniversary of our Republic, we are reminded of the courage and sacrifice that secured the ideals of liberty and opportunity that so many Americans fought and died for. We cannot let them down by allowing the radical left to prevail. I look forward to a fall campaign focused on real policies that benefit all Americans - and a clear contrast between my professional and legislative record and that of my opponent."

We appreciate all your help and support!
Team Spartz

Hey folks,
**Adam Mockler** joined me for a brutally honest conversation about Trump's threats toward Iran, the absolute chaos inside the Republican Party, and why so many of the same failed voices from the Iraq War era are suddenly back on TV pretending they learned something.
**Here 's what we got into:**

* [**00:10:24**] Adam opens up about taking nonstop attacks from right-wing pundits and why "debate culture" completely collapses when one side refuses to engage in good faith.
* [**00:14:41**] We dig into why Trump's economic promises are falling apart, why voters are furious, and why Republicans suddenly look politically vulnerable again.
* [**00:19:51**] We end on hope -- the coming midterms, building a new generation of leaders, and why this dark moment could still become a turning point for the country.

When people hear that Bitcoin may one day need to defend itself against quantum computing, the first question is usually technical. What code changes? What cryptography replaces what? But the more important question is institutional, not mathematical: **who actually decides to make those changes, and how do they happen in a system with no central authority?**
Bitcoin does not have a CEO, a board, or a government agency that can mandate an upgrade. There is no switch that can be flipped. Strengthening Bitcoin against a future quantum threat would be a process of coordination across a loose, global network of participants who all have different roles and incentives.
It starts with developers.
A relatively small group of open source contributors, often referred to as Bitcoin Core developers, are responsible for proposing and implementing changes to the software that runs the network. These developers do not have unilateral power. What they do have is influence through expertise. When a potential improvement is identified, such as adopting quantum resistant cryptography, it is first discussed publicly, often for years.
Those discussions are formalized through Bitcoin Improvement Proposals, or BIPs. A BIP lays out a specific change, explains the reasoning behind it, and invites scrutiny from the broader community. Anyone can propose one, but only ideas that survive intense review and debate gain traction. In the case of quantum resistance, proposals would likely involve new address types or new ways of signing transactions that are designed to withstand future attacks.
From there, the process becomes even more decentralized.
Node operators, the individuals and organizations that run Bitcoin software, ultimately decide whether to adopt a proposed change. They choose which version of the software to run. If enough of them upgrade to a version that includes new quantum resistant features, those features become part of the network's accepted rules. If they do not, the proposal effectively stalls.
Miners also play a role. They produce blocks and enforce certain rules in practice. While they cannot unilaterally change Bitcoin's protocol, their participation is necessary for any major transition to function smoothly. Exchanges, custodians, and wallet providers are equally important. They are the interface most users rely on, and they would need to support any new address formats or migration strategies.
Then there are the users themselves.
If Bitcoin were to transition to quantum resistant systems, it would likely require individuals to move their funds to new types of addresses. That is not automatic. It would require awareness, education, and action. The success of any upgrade would depend on whether millions of users actually follow through.
This is where Bitcoin's greatest strength and greatest challenge intersect. The system is resistant to control, which makes it resilient against unilateral decisions, but it also means that change is slow and requires broad agreement.
There are different ways such a transition could unfold. Some changes could be introduced gradually, allowing users to opt in over time. Others might require more coordinated action, especially if a credible quantum threat emerged quickly. In extreme scenarios, the community could even face difficult decisions about how to handle vulnerable coins that have not been moved. None of these paths are simple, and all would involve tradeoffs.
What matters is that the process already exists.
Bitcoin has gone through upgrades before. Features like SegWit and Taproot were not imposed from the top down. They were debated, refined, and ultimately adopted through a combination of developer work, community consensus, and user choice. A future effort to address quantum computing would follow a similar pattern, though likely with higher stakes.
The key takeaway is that Bitcoin does not defend itself automatically. It is defended by people. Developers propose solutions. Node operators choose to run them. Businesses integrate them. Users adopt them.
That is how a decentralized system evolves.
And if quantum computing ever becomes a real threat to Bitcoin, the response will not come from a single decision maker. It will come from a network of participants, slowly and deliberately, deciding together how to adapt.

They act like our enemies, but we know better. They are just pawns in a larger strategy being manipulated by dark spiritual forces trying to extinguish the light. If they knew better, they would do better. There are numerous military terms for what spiritual war is like. A proxy war is when you attack an ally of your enemy or encourage one of your allies to attack one of their allies. A similar move is called a false flag operation. [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom. "https://secure.anedot.com/okeefemediagroup/omg-cannot-be-beaten-mb?utm_source=omg-cannot-be-beaten&utm_medium=tld&utm_campaign=mb&amount=35")Dear Friend,

I posted a picture of myself this weekend. Buzzed head. Cold stare. No smile.

A friend of mine looked at it and said, "You don't even look like the same person."

He's right. I'm not.

I'm 41 years old. I've been doing this work for twenty-two years. And every single one of those years left a mark — not on my face, but on my spine. On my will. On the thing inside me that refuses to quit.

They tried to destroy me. They arrested me. They raided my home. They sued me. They conspired against me from the inside. They sent a former board member to the FBI to feed them information and try to put me in prison.

And I'm still here.

Not just still here. Stronger than I've ever been. And I need you to understand why — because your [**support right now is what keeps me in the fight**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.). ****[STAND WITH JAMES — DONATE NOW](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**** Let me take you back to January 2010. I was twenty-five years old. A kid with a camera and a conviction that the truth mattered more than my comfort.

Federal agents put me in handcuffs inside a United States senator's office in New Orleans. They led me out in front of the cameras. Every network in the country ran the footage. "Conservative activist arrested," the chyrons said. They wanted that to be the end of my story.

I was twenty-five. I had no money. No legal team. No powerful friends. Just a belief that citizens had a right to know what their government was doing — and a willingness to pay the price for acting on it.

That false arrest was supposed to scare me into silence. It did the opposite. It taught me that the people in power will use every weapon they have against anyone who threatens the narrative. And it taught me that I could take the hit and keep walking. ****[KEEP JAMES AND OMG IN THE FIGHT — DONATE NOW](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**** Eleven years later, they came for me again. This time they didn't just arrest me. They kicked in my door.

November 2021. FBI agents swarmed my apartment in New York. They put me in handcuffs in my own hallway. They seized my phones. They rifled through my belongings. A journalist — treated like a criminal in his own home.

Why? Because someone gave us a diary that belonged to the President's daughter. We didn't publish it. We turned it over to law enforcement. **And they raided me anyway**.

Think about that. We did the right thing — and the FBI showed up at my door at dawn with guns and handcuffs.

The message was clear: We don't care what you did or didn't publish. We want you to know that we can reach you. Anywhere. Anytime.

**[**Can you chip in $35, $50, or $100 right now to help me keep fighting?**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**

The raids and the arrests — those I expected. What I didn't expect was the betrayal from inside.

A man who sat on my own board — a man I trusted — went to the FBI and became an informant against me. He admitted it on our hidden cameras. He told our undercover journalist he'd fed "tons of information" to federal law enforcement. Every agency that called, he answered.

Then we found his copy of my book, Breakthrough — with a rifle bullet fired straight through the heart on the cover. Exit wound out the back. When I confronted him in Miami Beach and asked him about it, he said: "I needed a target."

When I asked if he'd kill me, he called it "a figure of speech."

A figure of speech. A bullet through my heart. From a man who was supposed to protect the organization I built. ****[BACK JAMES AND OMG — DONATE NOW](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**** I could fill a filing cabinet with the lawsuits they've thrown at me. Pentagon contractors. DOJ officials. Corporate executives. My own former organization sued me after I was forced out by the very board that harbored an FBI informant.

Every lawsuit is designed to do the same thing: bleed me dry. Tie me up in discovery. Drain the resources I need for investigations and redirect them to lawyers. That's how lawfare works — you don't have to win in court. You just have to make the fight so expensive that your target gives up.

They've been waiting sixteen years for me to give up.

I haven't.

**[**Help me keep going**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.). $35 helps cover a day of fieldwork. $100 funds legal review on an investigation. $250 helps launch the next undercover operation.**

I want to be honest with you about something, because I think you deserve it.

I don't have a normal life. I can't. The opposition is always watching. Always looking for a way to set me up, take me down, catch me in something they can twist into a headline. I've accepted that. There's no turning it off. There's no weekend where I stop being James O'Keefe.

So I channel everything into the work. Into the training. Into the mission. The kid they arrested in Louisiana is gone. In his place is something their attacks created — a man who has been hit so many times that he's stopped flinching. A man who walks into Antifa headquarters in disguise with hidden cameras rolling. A man who flies to Miami Beach to confront the traitor who shot a bullet through his book. A man who goes back to Minneapolis after receiving a death threat.

**They wanted to break me. Instead, they built something they can't beat.**

And the results speak for themselves. This year alone, OMG investigations have triggered $253 million in federal contracts being suspended. We forced the Secret Service to suspend an agent who was leaking the Vice President's security details. We've recorded seven FBI and DOJ officials on hidden camera admitting the system is broken. We've generated millions of views — not because we write opinion columns, but because we show up with cameras where nobody else will.

That's what your donation buys. Not talk. Results.

[**I'm asking you to stand with me today**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.). Not because I need sympathy — I don't. [**I need resources.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

**[**$35 covers a background check**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** before we send someone undercover.

**[**$50 helps pay for encrypted equipment**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** that keeps our journalists safe.

**[**$100 funds the legal review**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** that lets us publish what the powerful want buried.

**[**$250 helps us launch the next investigation —**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** because we have more targets than budget.

**[**$500 or more funds a full day of protected field operations.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)**

They arrested me at twenty-five. They raided me at thirty-seven. They betrayed me from the inside. They sued me from every direction. And here I am at forty-one — still standing, still fighting, and stronger than I've ever been.

**The only question is whether you're standing with me.**

Rush your best gift right now — [**$35, $50, $100, or whatever you can**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.). Thank you for being part of something they can't stop.

In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder and CEO O'Keefe Media Group

**P.S.** Sixteen years ago they put me in handcuffs and thought that would be the end of it. Then they raided my home. Then they turned a board member into an informant. Then they sued me from every angle. And every single time, I got back up. I'm not going anywhere. But I need you in this fight. [**Donate today — any amount — and stand with the man they couldn't break.**](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)

## Momentum is Building in WI-05 — But We Need Your Help
---
Hello,
**First —** **thank you!**
Our nomination paper signature effort is going well, but we still need more signatures to ensure a strong showing for the collection process. Every signature, every conversation, and every volunteer hour helps build momentum across Wisconsin’s 5th Congressional District. Please reply to this email with a rough count of signatures you have collected so I have a better estimated count.
Over the past week, I had the opportunity to speak at the Wisconsin 5th Congressional District Convention and at the Jefferson County Democrats Spring Gala on Sunday, May 3rd. I had a great time at both events and was encouraged by the energy, enthusiasm, and determination I saw from people ready for real representation and real change. Thank you to Alicia (the new Waukesha Democratic Mayor!), Kevin and Kelli for their hard work on these events!
The campaign is now entering the next phase.
As of June 1st, we officially begin ramping up for the General Election — **just 156 days away**. I’m proud to be **the only Democrat running in WI-05** , and we are building a campaign focused on lowering costs, creating good jobs, and improving healthcare for working families across southeastern Wisconsin.
To win, we need to grow our team immediately.
We are currently looking for:
• Campaign Manager (Paid)
• Finance Manager (Paid)
• Communications Volunteers
• Events & Outreach Volunteers
• Calendar Maintenance & Scheduling Help
• Volunteer Coordination Support
• General Campaign Supporters and Organizers
If you have time, ideas, skills, or simply want to help bring change to WI-05, please reach out.
We’ve also been informed that the **Common Threads Coalition** in Brookfield is working on organizing a candidate forum between **Scott Fitzgerald** and myself sometime in August or September. We’ll see what happens, but I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the issues facing our district directly with **Fitz** and with voters.
This campaign is growing because of people like you. But campaigns are powered by volunteers and donations — and we need both to compete and win.
Please consider helping however you can:
• Volunteer your time
• Share ideas and connections
• Donate to help us build the campaign infrastructure needed to compete across the district
**A change will do you good!**
**Thank you again for your support,****Andy**

clean_body: | | | | | | | | | | | | | Momentum is Building in WI-05 — But We Need Your Help Hello, First — thank you! Our nomination paper signature effort is going well, but we still need more signatures to ensure a strong showing for the collection process. Every signature, every conversation, and every volunteer hour helps build momentum across Wisconsin’s 5th Congressional District. Please reply to this email with a rough count of signatures you have collected so I have a better estimated count. Over the past week, I had the opportunity to speak at the Wisconsin 5th Congressional District Convention and at the Jefferson County Democrats Spring Gala on Sunday, May 3rd. I had a great time at both events and was encouraged by the energy, enthusiasm, and determination I saw from people ready for real representation and real change. Thank you to Alicia (the new Waukesha Democratic Mayor!), Kevin and Kelli for their hard work on these events! The campaign is now entering the next phase. As of June 1st, we officially begin ramping up for the General Election — just 156 days away. I’m proud to be the only Democrat running in WI-05 , and we are building a campaign focused on lowering costs, creating good jobs, and improving healthcare for working families across southeastern Wisconsin. To win, we need to grow our team immediately. We are currently looking for: • Campaign Manager (Paid) • Finance Manager (Paid) • Communications Volunteers • Events & Outreach Volunteers • Calendar Maintenance & Scheduling Help • Volunteer Coordination Support • General Campaign Supporters and Organizers If you have time, ideas, skills, or simply want to help bring change to WI-05, please reach out. We’ve also been informed that the Common Threads Coalition in Brookfield is working on organizing a candidate forum between Scott Fitzgerald and myself sometime in August or September. We’ll see what happens, but I look forward to the opportunity to discuss the issues facing our district directly with Fitz and with voters. This campaign is growing because of people like you. But campaigns are powered by volunteers and donations — and we need both to compete and win. Please consider helping however you can: • Volunteer your time • Share ideas and connections • Donate to help us build the campaign infrastructure needed to compete across the district A change will do you good! Thank you again for your support,Andy | | | | | | | | | | ---|--- | | ---|--- | | ---|--- | | ---|--- | | ---|--- | | ---|--- | | ---|--- | | | | | Beck for Congress | PO Box 253 West Bend WI 53095 | This email was sent to dpwillis67@gmail.com | Paid for by Beck for Congress | [Update your preference]() | | | |

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]
