Dell , including about 7,400 people in Round Rock. Dell has ramped up investment in Texas in recent months, renovating parts of its Round Rock headquarters as its chief executive focused on artificial intelligence. Amid an ongoing AI boom, Dell , up 30% from the prior year, on $113.54 billion in revenue. The move comes as Texas positions itself to compete with Delaware for corporate incorporations. Delaware has long been the preferred state for companies and startups because of its business-friendly legal system. As of last year, more than 60% of Fortune 500 companies were incorporated there. () » » » “SpaceX files plan for $55 billion Terafab chip facility in Texas” via – Elon Musk’s SpaceX, in a joint project with Tesla, has proposed investing $55 billion to build a semiconductor manufacturing facility, called Terafab, in Texas, according to a filing made public on Wednesday. The billionaire has been seeking to secure in-house access to advanced chips, though analysts have said the scale of capacity he has outlined would likely require far greater investment. SpaceX is targeting a June IPO that could value the company at around $1.75 trillion. The project would involve a multi-phase chip fabrication and advanced computing complex designed to boost domestic semiconductor production capacity in the United States. ( ) “Corpus Christi to begin talks on privately built desalinization plant” via ‘s Colleen DeGuzman – Seven months after axing their own seawater desalination plant project — and five months from when a water crisis is expected to surface — Corpus Christi City Council voted 6-2 Tuesday to begin preliminary talks with a new company to build a desalination facility for the Coastal Bend area. AXE H20, a 2-month-old private company based in Houston, is seeking to build a plant that could produce 150 million gallons of drinking water a day. According to a presentation Tuesday, the city could pay $6.50 per 1,000 gallons — about 30% cheaper than a controversial plan to revive a city-built desalination plant known as the Inner Harbor Project. John Olson , the company’s chairman, said using natural gas rather than electricity enables it to offer a cheaper rate than other proposals. He said the company would need two years to build the facility. “It involves no public funds, no debt, no bond rating issues,” he told council members. “No taxpayer risks, no operating expenses. This is absolutely a private venture.” ( ) “Texas ranks among worst for health care disparities” via ‘s Nicole Villalpando – Medical assistant Sarai Vences takes the blood pressure of patient Eloy Herrera at the Central Health East Austin Specialty Clinic. Having access to both specialty care and primary care can improve health outcomes. Central Health’s Medical Access Program provides a health insurance-like program for people who make less than 200% of the federal poverty level. How equitable is Texas’ health care system? Turns out, not very. That’s true across the United States with people who are Hispanic or Black having less access to care and worse health outcomes, according to a new report from the Commonwealth Fund. The fund is a nonprofit that supports independent research into creating a better healthcare system. For Texas, though, the disparities show up in greater amounts because of the number of people who are uninsured. “There are opportunities to do better,” said David Radley , a researcher with the fund, of Texas’ situation. “Having health insurance is the first step to making sure that people can get access to primary care.” Equity should be a concern for everyone, said Dr. Laurie Zephyrin , the senior vice president at Commonwealth Fund and an obstetrician-gynecologist. “Disproportionate access doesn’t just affect people who are marginalized,” she said. Right-wing groups are still using his political playbook. Duane Rollins needed to be careful. The winding drive through Houston’s tony West Oaks neighborhood took only a few minutes. But he could easily draw suspicion from constables patrolling the sprawling lawns and manors of the city’s elite. One swerve or rolled stop could foil his vengeance plan. They’d pull him over, smell the booze on his breath, and unearth the vodka bottle and pistol shoved under his seat. And then he would go straight back to prison. It was 2016, months since Rollins had last been released and plunged back into the addictions that had kept him behind bars for much of his adult life. He’d turned fifty in a cell and always expected he’d return. This time, he’d have something to show for it. Though it was late, surely Paul Pressler would welcome him. Rollins had been a standout in Pressler’s church youth group, earning special visits from the Southern Baptist icon, Republican kingmaker, and prominent judge. They’d traveled the world together in between Rollins’s arrests. He was Pressler’s “dear brother” and longtime assistant, tasked with writing his letters, running his errands, and safeguarding a secret that could destroy his pious legacy. No more. Squinting and weaving past immaculate mansions, he imagined how it would feel to press the pistol against Pressler’s bug-eye spectacles. To demand answers—to free himself. ( ) “1 dead, several injured in mass shooting in Pflugerville” via KVUE — One person was killed and at least four were injured in a deadly shooting early Wednesday morning at a restaurant in Pflugerville. According to the Austin Police Department (APD), the shooting happened sometime before 2 a.m. inside Down South CaJJun Eats along the 15400 block of FM 1825, near Vision Drive and Pecan Street. Police say the incident ended in the parking lot. In a media briefing Wednesday morning, Austin police said the victim killed is a man in his 20s. His identity has not been shared with the public at this time. Police say four others have been taken to a hospital with non life-threatening injuries. It’s unclear exactly what led up to this incident. APD said several suspects were detained at an apartment complex on East Howard Lane in northeast Austin. Law enforcement did not specify the exact number of suspects. ( ) | 2026 “Dan Patrick backs Mayes Middleton for Texas attorney general” via ‘s Alejandro Serrano – Dan Patrick on Tuesday threw his support behind state Sen.Mayes Middleton in the GOP primary for Texas attorney general, giving the Galveston Republican a boost in the final weeks of his May 26 runoff against U.S. Rep. Chip Roy. Patrick also endorsed Railroad Commissioner Jim Wright in his contest against Bo French , the GOP activist and energy investor whose controversial comments have drawn Patrick’s past ire. In a pair of social media posts, the lieutenant governor said Middleton had “established a record as one of the most conservative senators in Texas history” and that Wright had the experience needed to guide the agency that regulates the oil and gas industry, amid high gas prices and a rocky energy market. The endorsements from the state’s second-highest elected official came several hours after a new statewide poll found Middleton leading Roy by nine points among likely voters. The Galveston lawmaker has served in the Senate under Patrick, the chamber’s presiding officer, since 2023. ( ) “Can Ken Paxton Win a Senate Primary in Texas Without His Biggest Donors?” via ‘sLauren McGaughy –Ken Paxton , the firebrand Texas attorney general, said last year that he thought he would need about $20 million to unseat Senator John Cornyn. So far, Mr. Paxton is far short of his mark. Many of the wealthy donors who bankrolled his political career in Texas have decided to watch from the sidelines during the U.S. Senate race, according to an analysis of state and federal campaign finance data by The New York Times. Several businessmen who spent millions on Mr. Paxton’s campaigns for state attorney general have not given to either his Senate campaign or a political action committee backing his run, including a former top donor who gave far more to Mr. Cornyn. ( ) “Allred, Johnson on collision course in District 33 runoff after shared path” via ‘Gromer Jeffers Jr. – Colin Allred andJulie Johnson have followed the same path through North Texas politics. Now they’re on a collision course. Allred flipped Texas’ 32nd Congressional District in 2018 and held it for three terms. Johnson took over after he gave it up for a Senate bid that fell short. That handoff has turned into a head-to-head contest, with Allred of Dallas and Johnson of Farmers Branch facing off in the May 26 runoff for the newly revised District 33. Allred led the first round with 44% to Johnson’s 33% in a four-candidate field. ( ) “Democrats Home In on South Texas as Bobby Pulido Added to National ‘Red to Blue’ Program” via ‘s Mary Elise O’Grady – With South Texas being the home to several congressional districts coveted by both parties, the Democratic Congressional Campaign Committee (DCCC) announced the addition of Congressional District (CD) 15 candidateBobby Pulido to their “Red to Blue” program, among others. Pulido, a Latin singer and Latin Grammy winner, is preparing to face off against incumbent Congresswoman Monica De La Cruz (R-TX-15), who has held the seat since 2023 after flipping the district — a South Texas territory that encircles McAllen and stretches northward to flank the right side of San Antonio — from blue to red. ( ) | STATE GOVERNMENT “Civil rights groups sue to stop Texas immigration law” via ‘s Alejandro Serrano – A group of civil rights organizations on Monday filed a new lawsuit seeking to stop parts of the law that would let Texas police arrest people suspected of illegally crossing the U.S.-Mexico border. The law can go into effect next week after a federal appeals court lifted a lower court ruling that had kept it paused for years. Senate Bill 4 , as the law is known, created a state-level crime for entering the country without authorization and created pathways for state authorities to remove such people from the country if convicted. Courts have long held that immigration enforcement is the sole responsibility of the federal government, but with the state law, Texas Republicans sought to challenge that precedent. ( ) “Is your Texas school district at risk of a state takeover? Explore our tracker.” via ‘sAshley Soebroto – After decades of infighting among South San Antonio Independent School District’s elected officials, the Texas Education Agency last year took over the public school system with just over 7,000 students. The state currently has a hand in daily operations at South San Antonio ISD and several other Texas school districts. Many of these state interventions are for academic reasons. When a public school campus scores five consecutive failing letter grades from the state, the poor performance may trigger a state takeover of the entire district. That could mean the state replaces the district superintendent and elected board members with new leadership. Campus grades are largely based on State of Texas Assessments of Academic Readiness, or STAAR, exam results. Last year, the state announced it would take over four more school districts, including Fort Worth ISD. Here are the public school districts under TEA management or at risk of takeover. In December, Education Commissioner Mike Morath announced that he would install a superintendent, conservator and board of managers to oversee the district about 90 miles east of Houston. The takeover was triggered by two schools — Martin Luther King, Jr. Middle School and Fehl-Price Elementary — receiving five straight failing grades. ( ) | LOCAL GOVERNMENT “Houston Texans, Rodeo commit to Harris County for stadium plans, Cal McNair says” via ‘s Jonathan M. Alexander – The Texans and the rodeo say that they want to make things work in Harris County with either stadium renovation or a new stadium at Reliant Park. Team ownerCal McNair said the Houston Texans and the Houston Livestock Show and Rodeo have decided to make things work in Harris County. Team president Mike Tomon said the Texans have not ruled out building a new stadium within the park but are focusing on renovating Reliant Stadium, which is said to be significantly behind on needed maintenance. “What we’ve talked to the Rodeo (about) is we’re going to make it work, and so we’ll figure out a way to make it work and have everybody a winner in this thing,” McNair said Monday at the team’s annual charity golf event, which raised more than $565,000. In February 2025, the Texans began negotiating a new lease with Harris County and the Rodeo. The current lease expires in 2032. At the time, the Texans said they wanted to remain in the greater Houston area but not necessarily in Harris County. ( ) “Three-point seat belt law could cost Texas schools millions” via ‘s Xochilt Garcia – Local school districts say it’s not “financially feasible” to install three-point seat belts on all school buses, even though the state expects them to by the 2029-30 school year. “This is a classic, classic unfunded mandate,” said John Craft , superintendent for Northside Independent School District. “If there is such a thing, this is textbook definition.” Passed last year, Senate Bill 546 builds on school bus safety requirements by requiring that all buses have three-point seat belts, regardless of the year they were made. Before that, only buses made after 2018 were required to have the safety belts. Currently, districts have bus fleets with a patchwork of seat belt types, operating buses with three-point belts, two-point belts and some with no seat belts. ( ) “Airbnb, Vrbo rules help Austin rein in STRs” via ‘s Kiah Collier – Austin officials say a sweeping overhaul of the city’s short-term rental regulations is beginning to show results, with higher compliance and a surge in hotel occupancy tax revenue as new enforcement tools come online. In a recent memo to the mayor and City Council, Austin Development Services Director Keith Mars said recent changes to the city’s short-term rental, or STR, program are improving oversight and bringing more operators into compliance. The update follows City Council’s September 2025 vote to tighten STR rules after years of legal setbacks and uneven enforcement. At the time, city leaders described the issue as “thorny and difficult,” noting lawsuits had weakened earlier regulations and made it difficult to track or penalize illegal rentals. The new ordinance, paired with some other changes, shifted the city to a business-licensing model and, for the first time, imposed requirements on platforms like Airbnb and Vrbo. Those rules require platforms to display license numbers, remove unlicensed listings and collect hotel occupancy taxes on behalf of hosts — changes aimed at addressing widespread noncompliance. City data last year showed about 94% of complaints involved unlicensed rentals. ( ) “McCombs’ partners sue over downtown San Antonio property deal, say they were cut out” via ‘s Patrick Danner – A lawsuit against companies tied to the McCombs family alleges minority co-owners were excluded from a multimillion-dollar lease deal involving a downtown San Antonio property and the city. The property, a former Holiday Inn at 318 W. César E. Chávez Blvd., was first used by the city early in the pandemic under a temporary agreement and later subleased for longer-term use as a homeless shelter. SAMMinistries operates the shelter. The plaintiffs — three siblings who hold a minority stake in the property — allege the sublease and a later transfer of control were carried out without their consent. Siblings Brant Oser Miller , Jay Robert Miller and Robin Nancy Miller Holbrook filed the lawsuit, seeking more than $5 million in damages and a forced sale of the property. ( ) “Austin ISD proposes larger class sizes, cuts to teacher planning time” via KUT – A highly anticipated summary of cuts from Austin Independent School District leaders on Tuesday provided few new details about classroom changes next year as the district grapples with a yawning budget deficit. Campus-level changes are set to phase in over the next two school years, the district said in the summary of potential cuts. All Austin ISD schools under a state-mandated improvement plan and those with D or F ratings under the state’s academic accountability system will see little change next year. Meanwhile, elementary campuses with passing ratings will see an increase in class sizes next year, and teachers at those campuses will move to a single planning period the following year. Teachers of non-foundational courses at middle and high school campuses with passing ratings will be assigned to teach seven of eight periods next year, a change that will expand to include all courses the following year. In a letter to families and staff, Superintendent Matias Segura suggested there would be layoffs. However, it’s unclear how many educators or other school employees would lose their jobs. Principals and department leads will meet with affected staff by mid-May. Librarian and counselor positions will not be cut, Austin ISD said. However, bilingual and special education stipends will now be tiered depending on position and qualification requirements, according to the proposal. ( ) | BUSINESS NEWS “Texas, Nevada Laws Can’t Be Measured Against Delaware Benchmark” via ‘s Carliss Chatman – Recent arguments over Nevada corporate law expose a deeper problem in corporate law scholarship that is now shaping how Texas is being evaluated as a corporate jurisdiction. Corporate law, which has for decades been taught and studied with Delaware as the default framework, has treated other jurisdictions largely as variations on that model. That framing is convenient, but it is also wrong. When Delaware is treated as the default, jurisdictional competition becomes a debate about perception rather than substance. A group of Nevada officials, practitioners, and academics late last month publicly responded to a draft academic article about their state’s corporate law. They were joined by Nevada Gov. Joe Lombardo (R), Nevada Secretary of State Francisco Aguilar , and more than 20 lawyers and faculty. Their core claim is straightforward: Widely circulated critiques of Nevada corporate law are based on incomplete analysis, selective use of authority, and in some instances, unsupported quotations. They’re not trying to declare Nevada “better” than Delaware; they’re insisting that investors, advisers, and corporate leaders make decisions based on an accurate account of the law. ( ) “AT &T;’s multibillion-dollar HQ with ‘mini Reunion Tower’ moves forward” via ‘sNick Wooten – Plans for AT&T;’s new multibillion-dollar headquarters in Plano — complete with a 280-foot structure that one official called a “mini Reunion Tower” — got key approval from the city’s Planning and Zoning Commission on Monday night. Commissioners unanimously recommended approval for four items tied to the telecom giant’s new 54-acre campus at 5400 Legacy Drive and adjacent sites. The Plano City Council will get the final say. Preliminary site plans show there will be 2.3 million square feet of building space. The office campus will also include a daycare center, a pedestrian bridge, 3⁄4 of an acre of public green space, and the tower. The southern half of the site will include parking garages. The tower may not exceed 280 feet. The tallest building, excluding the tower, will be 8 stories. The 280-foot tower will feature AT&T;’s logo and include an enclosed communications antenna. City codes prevent the tower from flashing, strobing or displaying other related light effects between 10 p.m. and 6 a.m. The structure must still be approved by the Federal Aviation Administration, city planners said. ( ) “$1.6B North Texas team joins financial giant Wells Fargo” via ‘s Leonardo Rosas (Dallas Business Journal) – A Frisco-based wealth management firm with $1.6 billion in assets under management has joined Wells Fargo Advisors as the financial giant continues to grow its presence in North Texas. Wells Fargo Advisors, the wealth management arm of San Francisco-based Wells Fargo & Co. announced on May 4 the addition of AGT Private Wealth Advisors. The team, previously affiliated with Swiss financial giant UBS, consists of six financial advisers and eight support staff based in Frisco. Wells Fargo Advisors has had a presence in Dallas-Fort Worth since 1985, according to the announcement. A spokesperson declined to disclose the firm’s assets under management in DFW. Chris Gerrish , Mid-America market leader at Wells Fargo Advisors, said the latest additions help strengthen the company’s “growing presence” in North Texas. Gerrish sits in the Wells Fargo Advisors branch office in Frisco and oversees financial advisers across DFW. ( ) “A $27M Austin property just sold for half that — here’s why” via AAS – An Austin developer has acquired the IHOP at 707 E. Cesar Chavez St. following an auction Tuesday at the Travis County Courthouse. Natin “Nate” Paul’s battle to keep a valuable piece of property on the edge of the high-rise-strewn Rainey Street has ended, as the lot at 707 E. Cesar Chavez was auctioned off Tuesday on the steps of the Travis County Courthouse. Only three groups competed for the foreclosed property in a slow, low-volume auction that drew more than 100 bids over two hours. Most of the bidding came from Cesar Rainey LLC, which held the defaulted note, and the eventual winner, Austin-based real estate investment firm Travis County Exchange Corp. The largely undeveloped site, which hosts only an IHOP along Interstate 35, was valued at $27 million by the county appraisal district but sold for just over $12.7 million. Voting in federal elections is not a privilege granted by paperwork; it's a right guaranteed by citizenship. This bill deliberately conflates the two. The SAVE Act aims to disenfranchise millions of Americans, especially women and queer folks who have changed their legal names, by making it harder for them to exercise their constitutional rights.

**Trump and MAGA Republicans are pushing this legislation to strategically narrow the electorate ahead of the 2026 midterms — because they’re scared.**

They've seen what full participation looks like, and they don't like the result. So rather than listening to voters and fixing their broken policies, they've chosen to restrict the pool. The SAVE Act is the legislative equivalent of moving the goalposts. Except in this case, the goalposts are the ballot box, and the people being moved away from them are American citizens with every legal right to be there.

Dear Patriot, They're trying to put an innocent cop in prison for **life**. Why? For defending himself against a fleeing suspect who dragged him with a car. I've been in law enforcement for decades. I've seen the system abused. But what is happening to Officer James Brennand of San Antonio, Texas makes my blood boil, and it should make yours boil too. On October 2nd, 2022, Officer James Brennand — a decorated Army veteran who swore an oath to protect his community — spotted a car he suspected was stolen outside a McDonald's in San Antonio. He called for backup. He approached the vehicle. He ordered the driver to step out. The driver's response? He threw the car into reverse and used it as a weapon. | [Defend Officer Brennand →](http://links.makingamericathegreatest.com/u/click?_t=79fa4a3daf024a0a886c5b498ff32e32&_m=c0147ce6cf33456bad4b110f22a6e108&_e=LJVP8IBy1dhVo5jX2NtQJCg_LhjRC-bvm5c58ZiJPMDrgA4wIKwIxSFTEhzpn4k2EqXINN-IDP-2dvReqX5e2GvJrie4U_NVb4G56wRWpSP__Np3ZMXhpwg15ptRby5WA66xrjYLGVqRknIQm11GpydR9lvbS41bLGw2SKcUfdLvTQXs_TpNc5ZUIEW8UFiPlZSyOxXI1dOuv978fa246zucoVzZnjELcY4ioQ5SYJPKXO9A8afsdk6rQUZDyS0QWhBK8EJj2_KEHYLO6ZlnXRaPC_G3thnKAG4P7FO-2gqppgRwI4nlRyeNvm34wcJvk4X-IkWXT-PK4ml2C-vIDPZNIRVVSFNt6b8ZiB1BZ3DuwsQIRhkfQMTPxk8WJ4EALdauiywEOPP7GUr-8q2VZ2yoqRfioKVAlqpFERJ_qHmlPq8YFJdH4mLU_-FmETw-)
---
The car door slammed into Brennand. He was dragged. In that split second — outnumbered, without backup, in genuine danger — James did what every officer is trained to do. **He protected himself.**
The driver survived. The passenger was unharmed. And since that night, the driver has racked up four more arrests. **Four.**
While the man who attacked James faces no meaningful consequences, Officer Brennand has been stripped of his badge, his paycheck, and his future. | **Family spending on kids' sports nearly DOUBLED in just 5 years.** Families are being charged up to $25,000 a year just to let their kids play sports. It’s all because private equity and big corporations are turning kids’ sports into a luxury only some can afford. Youth sports shouldn't be a ripoff. That’s why Chris Deluzio is leading the fight in Congress and introducing the Let Kids Play Act, which would ban private equity from youth sports, ending practices like stay-to-play policies, all while redirecting financial resources back to the community. **Join Chris Deluzio:_[Sign the petition urging Congress to pass the Let Kids Play Act →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130867571/619190833/843921625?refcode=email_050626_kidssports&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjU0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZWVkMGQwYi02ZDQ5LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cVsqzE44mQ90vdcF1IPwtG_pedFPlufZD_iGRmOx84c=&emci=75251380-6c49-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=5eed0d0b-6d49-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=13185894)_** | | [Sign the petition →](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130867573/619190906/843921625?refcode=email_050626_kidssports&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTIvMS85MjU0MyIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI1ZWVkMGQwYi02ZDQ5LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=cVsqzE44mQ90vdcF1IPwtG_pedFPlufZD_iGRmOx84c=&emci=75251380-6c49-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&emdi=5eed0d0b-6d49-f111-8ef2-000d3a14b640&ceid=13185894)

The price of kids’ sports is off the charts, Derek.
It didn’t used to be this way. Local leagues were run by nonprofits—Little League teams backed by small businesses, social clubs, volunteer fire departments, and churches. It was about community.
Today, it’s often private equity and other big investors that are behind the leagues. They’re treating youth sports like a business, not a public good. Too often, profit comes before kids.
Chris Deluzio is a dad to young kids, so he sees it firsthand—the cost of signing them up is getting out of control. Like so many ripoffs in our economy, powerful firms are gobbling up leagues, killing competition, and jacking up prices on parents because they can.
**Kids' sports should be for fun, competition, and team-building. A place where any kid—no matter where they come from—can show up, work hard, and be part of something bigger than themselves.**
But that’s slipping away. More and more, a family’s bank account decides whether a kid even gets to step on the field. That’s wrong—and it needs to end.
We’ve got to crack down on this consolidation, enforce antitrust laws, and get corporate power out of youth sports so they’re no longer a luxury. Every kid deserves the chance to play.
That’s why, as a dad of young athletes, Chris Deluzio is leading the fight in Congress—alongside Senators Cory Booker and Chris Murphy—to pass the Let Kids Play Act and make youth sports affordable again.

Peter, It’s been less than a week since the Supreme Court gutted the Voting Rights Act. And yet Republican officials across the country are already sprinting forward to accelerate the redistricting crisis and grab even more unearned power. Here’s where things stand:
* Within hours of the Supreme Court decision, **Florida** had passed its new egregiously gerrymandered map — which Gov. DeSantis just signed into law.
* **Alabama** has already started a sudden special session to move its primary election dates and potentially redraw its map before the midterms.
* **Tennessee** kicked off its special session yesterday in an effort to eliminate the state’s only Democratic district.
* **Arizona** Republicans are scheming to use this ruling to redraw maps to dilute majority-Latino districts.
* And the Republican governor of **Louisiana** went even further, declaring a “state of emergency” in order to suspend the congressional primaries — even though voting was already underway.

There is no secret plan behind closed doors. They are openly plotting ways to manipulate our maps by robbing communities of color of the ability to choose their own representatives. **And make no mistake: This is coming straight from the top: Trump took to social media to call on every single red state to push through extreme gerrymanders _before the midterms. _** **Peter, it’s our democracy that is in a state of emergency. ** [**We can stop them. But that means fighting every day, in every state, necessary to ensure their cynical, anti-voter maneuvers fail. As a coach with over 30 years of experience helping people change their bodies and mindsets, there's one topic that always comes up: **alcohol**.
I often get asked: What's the healthiest alcohol to drink? How bad is it for me? Does it have carbs? How can I drink and still lose weight? You get the idea.
That's because alcohol is deeply woven into our social fabric. Whether it's a wedding toast, a football game, a family BBQ, a date, or on a vacation, alcohol is often present. We're sold the idea that it makes life more fun, more celebratory, and more connected. And to some degree, there's truth in that as we release the happy hormones and vasodilate increasing blood flow fully euphoric. Consuming alcohol in moderation, and in the right context, can be a positive part of social bonding and enjoyment.
But if your goal is health, longevity, and staying lean -- especially as a **LVSTR** (our member of the _**Fast.Eat.Live.** _community) then you need to understand **how to drink smart**.
[Share](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=6729589&post_id=196682157&utm_source=substack&utm_medium=email&utm_content=share&utm_campaign=email-share&action=share&triggerShare=true&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MTk2NjgyMTU3LCJpYXQiOjE3NzgwODcxNTEsImV4cCI6MTc4MDY3OTE1MSwiaXNzIjoicHViLTY3Mjk1ODkiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.qpKeQlYj1HZVjcLVVPjqxrQlwWGa9u-nn6a3C8bcwF0)
* * *
**Step One: Know What Alcohol Does in the Body**

Alcohol is not a nutrient. It's a **toxin** , and your body knows it.
That's why when you drink, your liver immediately prioritizes metabolizing alcohol over everything else -- protein, carbs, and fats all get put on the back burner. The result?
* **Fat burning stops temporarily**
* **Other calories you consume (especially carbs and fried foods) are more likely to be stored as body fat**
* **Nutrient absorption is impaired**
* **Your brain is working harder to manage inflammation and neurotransmitter disruptions**

It's not just the alcohol -- it's what you eat with it, and what you do afterward that compounds the effects. Ever notice how nobody orders grilled salmon and asparagus at the bar? It's typically chips, mozzarella sticks, wings, fries, pizza, nachos, and lots of beer. That combo is a metabolic wrecking ball.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9oZWFydGxhbmRqb3VybmFsLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.bJcdTb7EPwRozUFK--tDwOPeu4kUbEfikzNiKJldHKQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=196682157)
* * *
**Step Two: Understand Where the Calories Come From**
Let's break it down simply:
**Alcohol TypeCarbs?Calories?Main Source of CaloriesTequila** (100% agave)❌ No~96 per 1.5 ozAlcohol (ethanol) only**Vodka/Gin** (unsweetened)❌ No~96 per 1.5 ozAlcohol only**Dry Red Wine** ✅ Low~120 per 5 ozAlcohol + minimal residual sugar**Sweet Wines / Champagne** ✅ Yes140-200+ per 5 ozAlcohol + sugar**Beer** ✅ Yes150-300+ per 12 ozAlcohol + carbs/sugars**Mixed Drinks (Margaritas, etc.)**
✅ Yes200-500+Alcohol + sugar-loaded mixers
**The Takeaway:** Pure alcohol (like tequila or vodka) has no carbs -- the calories come purely from alcohol itself, which clocks in at 7 calories per gram (more than carbs or protein).
* * *
**Coach Scott 's Alcohol Ranking: From Best to Worst (Metabolically Speaking)**

When you _do_ decide to enjoy a drink, make a **smart choice**. Here's how I rank them for my clients and fellow LVSTRS:
1. **Agave-Based Spirits** - Tequila and mezcal (100% agave) are the cleanest, least inflammatory, and don't spike blood sugar. Pro tip: skip the sugary mixers and go with soda water, lime, and a salt rim.
2. **Clear Spirits** - Vodka and gin are low in impurities and easy on the liver when consumed moderately.
3. **Dry Red Wines** - Higher in polyphenols like resveratrol, lower in sugar -- a good middle-ground.
4. **Brown Liquors** - Whiskey, bourbon, scotch... more congeners (flavors from the casts), more sugar byproducts, tougher on the brain and liver.
5. **Sweet Wines, Champagne, and Beer** - High in sugar, high in carbs, highly inflammatory. These are the ones that sneak up on your waistline.

* * *
**Step Three: Hydrate Like a Pro**

Alcohol **dehydrates** the body. Always has, always will.
I coach my clients to **plan ahead** :
* Drink at least 16 oz of water with electrolytes **before** drinking.
* Alternate alcoholic beverages with a full glass of water in-between.
* Rehydrate **after** with more water and electrolytes before bed.

This helps reduce the toxic burden, keeps your brain and body sharper, and can even stave off that dreaded hangover.
* * *
**Food Pairing and Metabolic Strategy**

One of my pro tips is this: **never drink on an empty stomach** -- especially if you want to protect your brain, liver, and keep your metabolism working.
Here's what I recommend to my LVSTRS before a night out:
* **Eat a small protein-based meal beforehand** (like grilled chicken, eggs, or grass-fed steak).
* **Avoid greasy carb-heavy meals** after drinking -- this is when poor decisions hit, and the metabolic cost skyrockets.

Let's be honest, nothing productive happens after day drinking. Las Vegas may tell you otherwise, but your metabolism disagrees.
* * *
**Alcohol, Brain Health, and Acetaldehyde**

When your liver processes alcohol, it converts it into acetaldehyde -- a compound more toxic than alcohol itself. It damages DNA, impairs mitochondria, and is linked to cancer and cognitive decline.
Clear, clean alcohols produce less acetaldehyde and inflammatory byproducts. That's why, again, tequila, mezcal, and vodka win the day here -- especially when consumed with food and hydration.
* * *
**Drinking in Community -- A Historical Perspective**

While I coach from a science-based lens, I also see the bigger picture. Historically, societies like the Greeks, Romans, and Egyptians used alcohol as part of communal feasts -- central planning their cities around it. Huge spaces filled with music, fellowship, and shared meals.
At _**Fast.Eat.Live**._, we encourage community, celebration, and living life fully -- not self-medicating alone. I always say:
"Only drink when you're happy, surrounded by people you love, and never use it as an escape from your circumstance."
* * *
**Takeaways:**

Alcohol is not the villain -- but the decisions you make before, during, and after drinking can either support your goals or sabotage them.
Want to enjoy alcohol and stay lean, sharp, and strong?
* Prioritize clear spirits like tequila or vodka
* Avoid sugary mixers and beer
* Hydrate before, during, and after
* Eat clean protein beforehand
* Skip the wings and fries
* Enjoy in community, not isolation
* Never make life-altering decisions after drinking at a Hooters

You've got one body/temple. Treat it like it matters. Drink smart, live better.

---

George Saunders is the author of nine books, including the novel _Lincoln in the Bardo_ , the miniature MFA course _A Swim in a Pond in the Rain_ , and some of the funniest, sweetest, weirdest short story collections ever written. His latest novel, _[Vigil](https://substack.com/redirect/6755cd90-ceba-4b11-bb87-8f0751a59f62?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , describes how a climate-denying Big Oil CEO is visited on his deathbed by Jill, a spirit whose task is to comfort people transitioning to the afterlife.
When I first heard about this book, it almost seemed too good to be true. Saunders is my favorite living writer. Climate-denying Big Oil CEOs are my bread-and-butter (and I mean that literally--I direct the Climate Accountability Project at Public Citizen, where I spend my days advocating for fossil fuel companies to pay for their [climate crimes](https://substack.com/redirect/9725022d-a9e8-475d-b390-fe581988c616?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). What could possibly be better than putting these together?
Then I started getting jittery. The pre-publication characterizations of _Vigil_ all [described](https://substack.com/redirect/4cd8883f-02c0-4e6c-9286-4d63296dd5af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the novel as exploring "the thorny question of absolution." If there's one topic I don't want to consider in connection with climate-denying Big Oil CEOs, it's absolution.
So I asked Saunders if he'd be willing to do an interview with me for _The New Republic_. You can find that interview--which is much better edited than this post--[right here](https://substack.com/redirect/20fb7280-b6cb-4a25-a53b-24b1783bf317?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). But I thought I'd share an extended version with you, as well, because it includes a reference by George to Big Oil CEOs getting their penises chopped off in hell, and I think we can all agree that is the kind of content we deserve right now.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack..j39VBgOiPQ3K386rq8Sv7nAKECLUldHMuY49DqySQHI?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=195863538)
_**Vigil**_**takes us inside the head of a climate-denying Big Oil executive at the end of his life. Did you have hopes for what effect the novel might have on readers?**
When I started, there was an overlay of, "Well, I'm 67, what's the most urgent thing happening in the universe? Climate change." But I realized that while climate change is in this book, it's not _about_ climate change. It's like how people will say _Schindler 's List_ is about the Holocaust, but it actually isn't--it's set there, but it's a book within that setting that does its own particular thing which is, for example, examining if it's possible to work for good within an evil system. The goal, I guess, is really just to wake a reader up a little bit--to make a person more aware of the world around them, to maybe feel a little more fond of the world.
Now that I'm done with it, I can see that it's an agitating book for a lot of people. Some people really loved it, some hated it. And that's kind of a first for me. That's sort of a nice accomplishment, at this late stage--to do something slightly new, even if it's annoying.
**There was so much I loved about this book. But I was really upset by the ending.**
I think a lot of people either thought "Oh it's the most beautiful ending" or "I hate it." Tell me what got under your skin.
**We live in a world that has been so corroded by elite impunity. We see again and again how the wealthy and powerful get away with murder. So to watch K.J. Boone, who experienced no worldly accountability for Big Oil 's climate denial, finally face the prospect of punishment in the afterlife, and then to see Jill swoop in and save him at the last minute--it's kind of like my favorite writer looked into my brain and conjured up my literal worst nightmare.**
But can I say . . . you're missing a step. Because yes, in life, he couldn't make any repentance, and he dies a dick. But then when he's free of his body, suddenly he sees the horror that he's done. So given that in the fictional world this transformation happens, now the question is, do you still want to kick that guy? I would argue I don't want to kick him anymore.
**I think there still needs to be punishment.**
In the real world I agree with you--if you could rouse him up and put him on his feet and march him to jail, I'm all for that.
You could easily argue that she lets him off the hook. But I would console you by saying the real hook is in a book I'm not going to write, after K.J. Boone runs around the earth for 10,000 years. Then it may very well be that he goes to hell and burns there for a while.
**Well that is a relief.**
Oh yeah, they beat the fuck out of him. Lances through the head, they cut off his penis, it's horrible what happens. [Laughs]
But I hear what you're saying, I really do. It's true that we don't get the result we want for him. But it's because of Jill, and her partially correct but also partly erroneous idea of how things should be.
**Jill has this extreme perspective on moral responsibility --that we are all "inevitable occurrences," and that therefore to pass judgment on someone for doing anything is absurd. Another character, the Frenchman, asks, "Do you really believe it? That bad and good are the same?" I've heard you say that both Jill and the Frenchman's perspectives are true, despite being at odds.**
I think that idea of an "inevitable occurrence" is probably demonstrably true by logic, if you look at eternity. But it's very uncomfortable. And you can't live like that. I think basically we all live with both those ideas alive in us all the time. So for example, when somebody offends you, part of your mind goes, "Well, that sucks, but you know, given who he is, I get it," and you move slightly in the direction of mercy. And __ at the same time, when somebody rears back their fist to hit you, if you can get a quick left hook in, you do that. So I think the book is uncomfortable because it's kind of making it a binary. And the reason it's a binary is because . . . she's dead.
**Dying kind of fucks with your head a bit, huh?**
Yeah, it does. At least the people in these Bardo realms, they are in extremity. But for me, Jill's idea is correct, and the other idea is correct, and we're always negotiating between the two. Because otherwise, why mercy? Why try to understand somebody? If everybody is infinitely malleable and can completely fix their shit, why don't they? And therefore you don't have to be merciful, you just call them on it.
**You 've talked about how empathy does not dull our action against bad actors, but in fact can sharpen it. I'm skeptical that this idea applies when it comes to a K.J. Boone-type figure, like the executives at ExxonMobil. Because these companies are not going to be persuaded to do the right thing--they need to be forced.**

But I would say you _are_ doing the Jill thing in your climate accountability work, because you're looking at the problem, you're looking at the villain, with curiosity, and you're saying, "That approach doesn't work, but this one might." What I would argue for is "know thy enemy"--and nothing's off the table at that point. All kinds of religious traditions are full of stories of enlightened beings who were super harsh in order to have a positive outcome. So it's not about kid gloves, but about informing oneself and not impeding your understanding with some pre-existing agenda. For example, if you are an activist and you say, "This Big Oil CEO is Satan embodied and he's in the back room eating human flesh," well, you've imagined the enemy incorrectly, and I would imagine then your actions would be inefficient. Whereas if you have a complete understanding of who that person is, with empathy underneath it, you're going to have a sharper idea of what must be done.
**I guess my perspective is we already know what must be done. I think most of our problems are not technical in nature, they 're political--we know the solutions, it's just a question of overcoming the interests opposed to them. From that perspective, there can be utility in caricature--and even, I'd argue, truth to it, because a lot of these guys do, by any reasonable approximation, look a lot like Satan eating human flesh.**

Boone's house who had your deep understanding of the issues and your political viewpoint, and at one point Jill came into his mind and we got the whole story. I can't help but read "Escape from Spiderhead" as moralizing against our carceral system, or "Pastoralia" as moralizing against capitalist exploitation. It's not a bad book, but it's so inflamed with Steinbeck's political views that you don't buy it. | | Peter,No one could hear her. A young girl named Kristen was locked in an attic. No windows. No fresh air. No way out. The door was locked from the outside. For months she lived there.
Alone. There was no bathroom.
Just a bucket. No shower. No clean clothes. And the only time she left that attic was when she was sold for sex.
Over. And over. And over. **This is the reality of child trafficking.**

Millions of children are trapped in exploitation around the world. But Kristen's story did not end in that attic. One night she knocked on a hotel room door. Her trafficker had arranged and forced her into another "date." But instead...**she met a rescue team - Freedom Strike Force. **They were working alongside law enforcement to identify victims and traffickers. When Kristen realized she was safe... She collapsed into the arms of one of our female advocates. **Free.** Law enforcement then raided the house where she was held. Traffickers were arrested. Kristen was taken to a safe place. For the first time in months, she had a real bed and a hot meal**.**

**She took the first step toward healing.** **This rescue was possible because people chose to act.**

The **Sound of Freedom Foundation** exists to _stop_ _ __the sale __of God 's children._ Inspired by the film _Sound of Freedom_ , the Foundation works around the world to **prevent trafficking, support rescue efforts, educate families, raise awareness, and push for stronger laws that protect children.** Our mission is simple. **To stop the sale of God 's children.** And right now we are preparing a new mission, happening in just a few weeks in Phoenix. Our **Freedom Strike Force** partner will train local law enforcement for two days, teaching them how to identify traffickers and victims hidden in plain sight. Then on day three...they go into the field. **Real operations. Real arrests. Real rescues.**

**I** n the summer of 2025, **[Intel was in a very dark place.](https://substack.com/redirect/c6e6a7cf-4b41-465b-8b4d-02840283e893?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** The once-dominant American chipmaker was bleeding market share, struggling with manufacturing delays, and watching its stock price languish as competitors raced ahead in the AI boom. Many on Wall Street had written the company off as a relic of a bygone era, another victim of America's long habit of offshoring critical technology infrastructure.
**[Then the U.S. government stepped in and took a minority stake.](https://substack.com/redirect/62728177-db1d-49cd-b59e-a876b4a82036?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/86fa63d9-fa2d-4488-a38f-9d979766a3b2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### Intel over the last 5 years
Since that investment last August, Intel's share price has more than quintupled. The stock has hit all-time highs, **[surged 114% in April alone,](https://substack.com/redirect/ce99f697-a3b7-4fcb-93ad-a44812e9892b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** and continues to climb on reports that Apple is in serious talks to use Intel as a domestic chip supplier for its U.S. devices. **[This is not a dead-cat bounce.](https://substack.com/redirect/c6e6a7cf-4b41-465b-8b4d-02840283e893?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** This is a genuine turnaround, and it is a textbook example of what the Trump administration's policy of investing in American industry actually looks like in practice. If you had put $1,000 in Intel **[the day the deal was announced on August 22nd 2025](https://substack.com/redirect/62728177-db1d-49cd-b59e-a876b4a82036?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** you would have $4,400 today.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4b027d59-5bdc-4107-8e7b-77945d50f21b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
### Intel over the last year
This is a win for American manufacturing, American Investors and it fits squarely into the broader Trump agenda of correcting decades of reckless offshoring. For years, critical supply chains were shipped overseas in the name of short-term cost savings. The result was a **[dangerous dependence on foreign nations for everything from semiconductors](https://substack.com/redirect/d852a7b6-749d-47f4-b5a9-6e374adc61f2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** to pharmaceuticals. The Intel investment represents a deliberate reversal of that trend. By putting government capital behind a foundational American company, the administration has helped stabilize and revitalize a strategically vital industry.

Warren Buffett famously said that "If you don't find a way to make money while you sleep, you will work until you die."
But what if your phone could do it for you? **📲**
That's exactly what**[Mode Mobile](https://substack.com/redirect/150874a2-41ea-447f-8b65-46c5c74ad79c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/150874a2-41ea-447f-8b65-46c5c74ad79c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)has created - **[technology that turns idle phone time into passive income](https://substack.com/redirect/150874a2-41ea-447f-8b65-46c5c74ad79c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).**
With **[490M+ users in their ecosystem and $1B in earnings and savings](https://substack.com/redirect/150874a2-41ea-447f-8b65-46c5c74ad79c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[,](https://substack.com/redirect/150874a2-41ea-447f-8b65-46c5c74ad79c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) their EarnPhone is being called the _Uber_ of smartphones.
With 32,481% revenue growth, they were named[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/150874a2-41ea-447f-8b65-46c5c74ad79c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[the fastest-growing software company in 2023](https://substack.com/redirect/150874a2-41ea-447f-8b65-46c5c74ad79c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** by Deloitte, and with 7 billion smartphones worldwide their market could be significantly larger than Uber's.
**[They've just secured their Nasdaq stock ticker $MODE](https://substack.com/redirect/150874a2-41ea-447f-8b65-46c5c74ad79c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[,](https://substack.com/redirect/150874a2-41ea-447f-8b65-46c5c74ad79c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and you now have a limited time to invest in their pre-IPO offering at $0.50/share.
**[Invest now at $0.50/share and earn up to 20% bonus shares.](https://substack.com/redirect/150874a2-41ea-447f-8b65-46c5c74ad79c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
* * *
* * *
There is also a clear national security dimension to this policy. Just as Trump's "drill baby drill" energy policy has insulated America from the worst effects of the Hormuz crisis by ensuring domestic production, (you only need to take a look at Europe to see how THAT is going,) the support for Intel is doing the same thing in the semiconductor space. A strong, domestic chipmaking capability means the United States is **[not wholly dependent on Taiwan or other vulnerable locations](https://substack.com/redirect/d839d952-f3fc-4a4a-aea5-29afe645f85a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** for advanced processors. When Apple, one of the most important chip buyers on the planet,[ ](https://substack.com/redirect/d79d764f-c0b2-4577-8ffa-042adc56024d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**[is reportedly in talks to buy Intel chips](https://substack.com/redirect/d839d952-f3fc-4a4a-aea5-29afe645f85a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** that is not just good business. It is strategic resilience.
The contrast with the previous administration's approach could not be starker. For years, the focus was on subsidies for green energy and social spending while critical manufacturing atrophied. Intel's resurgence under the current policy shows what happens when government capital is deployed toward actual strategic industries **rather than ideological pet projects.**
Of course, none of this would have happened without Intel's own internal efforts. The company has been aggressively repositioning itself as a major foundry player, signing major contracts with Amazon and Google, and expanding its manufacturing footprint. But the government's minority stake provided the stability and confidence the market needed **to believe in the turnaround.** The results speak for themselves: a stock that was once considered a has-been is now one of the best-performing names in the entire semiconductor sector.
This is what successful industrial policy looks like when it is done with focus and discipline rather than ideology. The Trump administration did not try to micromanage Intel or turn it into a political football. It made a targeted investment in a strategically important American company and then got out of the way. The market has rewarded that approach handsomely. We've seen the same story play out with rare earth minerals. The Trump administration recognized that without guaranteed buys, any US mine would be undercut by Chinese mines, so they stepped in choosing to "buy American" rather than just buy on price alone.
## [The Green Left Crippled America While Empowering China For 25 Years](https://substack.com/redirect/514d2729-917c-46b3-8976-6c018cd52cb1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

The broader lesson should not be lost on policymakers. When you support domestic manufacturing in critical sectors, you don't just create jobs. You build resilience. You reduce dependence on adversarial nations. You position American companies to compete and win on the global stage. Intel's resurgence is living proof that this approach works.
The company still faces challenges, but the trajectory has changed dramatically. From near-death in the summer of 2025 to a resurgent powerhouse less than a year later, Intel's story is a powerful reminder that American industry is not finished. It just needed the right combination of leadership, capital, and policy support to get back on its feet.
This is exactly the kind of outcome the Trump agenda was designed to produce. Invest in American companies. Bring critical production back home. Protect national security through economic strength rather than endless subsidies and virtue-signaling. The results are starting to speak for themselves.
Intel is not just recovering. It is roaring back. And the American people -- not just shareholders -- are the ultimate beneficiaries.

This is why I'm in this race

| | | | | |
---
[](https://eot.cameronforkentucky.com/f/a/eHPg2PiYQLxOAHq1ouj0Gw~~/AAAHURA~/9W87yJc4Q91D2gGnacheb0NYCrjInRYxXAj_I67Q9BCTqwilOU-yB4uB00V1U2WOkLmQ00__c6UMk5Q6K8LVtDmsDtUrPoh_VUgNb4WexmRkOfXm1DgYYzeDEhxjhHEkv2VwpWD0OwKBI6UH_SDISWTwfuuP7zYtyUA7mU0xdplytHuiZky1SBh3bIwDuybyYKmIpyY4N0bwam_fywwk-Y4q2ydJyS6-Z3-t-SXBTZx911l9ERXW5sBOsFM0LrKqR8XXN4206_DXPs7gWsXT-Q~~)

| | Friend,
I want to tell you about last night.
I was supposed to be on a debate stage with my opponent Andy Barr. He chose not to show up.
In politics, you can run ads. You can send mail. You can say anything you want behind a camera. But when the time comes to stand in front of voters and answer for your record – that's when it counts. And when that moment came last night, Andy Barr decided he didn't want to be there.
I'm not writing to vent about that. I'm writing because I think it tells you something.
Makenze and I are raising our three boys in Kentucky. We're raising them here because we want them to grow up in a Commonwealth, and a country, that lives up to the ideas of its founding. We want them to have more opportunity than the generations before. None of that is guaranteed. It takes leadership willing to make hard decisions and put Kentucky – and the country – ahead of Washington, D.C., ahead of the lobbyists, ahead of the political class.
**That's why I'm in this race. And it's why what happened last night matters.**
Andy Barr has spent fourteen years in Washington, D.C. He has voted with Nancy Pelosi over 1,200 times. He voted to give amnesty to illegal immigrants. He voted to fire pilots who refused the COVID vaccine. He voted against repealing ObamaCare. And he calls himself a conservative.
Last night, when given the chance to defend that record, he ducked.
I'm doing the opposite. I’ve just officially kicked off our **Kentucky First Tour.** Over the next two weeks leading up to the May 19th primary, my team and I will be on the road across every part of the Commonwealth – answering questions, shaking hands, and listening. Real conversations, with real people. The way it should be done.
**If we’re coming to your area, I hope to see you along the way. Our schedule is at **[_**www.cameronforkentucky.com/tour**_](https://eot.cameronforkentucky.com/f/a/Edl1NFa9Q2K_6m6dCv7zRg~~/AAAHURA~/xHGfHGFtIIQ9CmHG6dGYB37oQyZd4954j2W9JOYeHOAZOKSZRboFaLYKLmetuY0j1CUAYQmF7M3t8sOkh-dIw6u2vRsMLook-vKc871HJICiovy42wG9w-dKLT1-ZaEJuZ4D_2IDQrbJaImX8nNp27LY71vIKBq_b024wAbHCDFB4jqsthQfnZc9PNh4FnSG)**.**
If you don't live in Kentucky but you've been watching this race because conservatives across the country have a stake in who replaces Mitch McConnell in the Senate – [**I'd be grateful for your help getting us across the finish line.**](https://eot.cameronforkentucky.com/f/a/eHPg2PiYQLxOAHq1ouj0Gw~~/AAAHURA~/9W87yJc4Q91D2gGnacheb0NYCrjInRYxXAj_I67Q9BCTqwilOU-yB4uB00V1U2WOkLmQ00__c6UMk5Q6K8LVtDmsDtUrPoh_VUgNb4WexmRkOfXm1DgYYzeDEhxjhHEkv2VwpWD0OwKBI6UH_SDISWTwfuuP7zYtyUA7mU0xdplytHuiZky1SBh3bIwDuybyYKmIpyY4N0bwam_fywwk-Y4q2ydJyS6-Z3-t-SXBTZx911l9ERXW5sBOsFM0LrKqR8XXN4206_DXPs7gWsXT-Q~~)
Thank you. May God bless you, may God bless the Commonwealth of Kentucky, and may God bless the United States of America.
Sincerely,
Daniel Cameron

clean_body: This is why I'm in this race | | | | | | ~~ | | Friend, I want to tell you about last night. I was supposed to be on a debate stage with my opponent Andy Barr. He chose not to show up. In politics, you can run ads. You can send mail. You can say anything you want behind a camera. But when the time comes to stand in front of voters and answer for your record – that's when it counts. And when that moment came last night, Andy Barr decided he didn't want to be there. I'm not writing to vent about that. I'm writing because I think it tells you something. Makenze and I are raising our three boys in Kentucky. We're raising them here because we want them to grow up in a Commonwealth, and a country, that lives up to the ideas of its founding. We want them to have more opportunity than the generations before. None of that is guaranteed. It takes leadership willing to make hard decisions and put Kentucky – and the country – ahead of Washington, D.C., ahead of the lobbyists, ahead of the political class. That's why I'm in this race. And it's why what happened last night matters. Andy Barr has spent fourteen years in Washington, D.C. He has voted with Nancy Pelosi over 1,200 times. He voted to give amnesty to illegal immigrants. He voted to fire pilots who refused the COVID vaccine. He voted against repealing ObamaCare. And he calls himself a conservative. Last night, when given the chance to defend that record, he ducked. I'm doing the opposite. I’ve just officially kicked off our Kentucky First Tour. Over the next two weeks leading up to the May 19th primary, my team and I will be on the road across every part of the Commonwealth – answering questions, shaking hands, and listening. Real conversations, with real people. The way it should be done. If we’re coming to your area, I hope to see you along the way. Our schedule is at . body:
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
The Supreme Court just ruled in favor of voter suppression and against underrepresented communities in Louisiana v. Callais , folks.
This is a devastating blow to voting rights, but it only serves to strengthen our resolve . If anti-voting forces are going to stack the deck against the communities we serve, then we will work even harder to engage and rally these voters, lift their voices, and defend their right to vote .
How? Voter registration is a critical part of grassroots efforts to protect voting rights. The more people who vote, the more our government looks like we, the people. But to get to the point where every voice is heard, we need your help .
Just $3 can help us register a new voter. If you're with us in this fight, chip in $30 or whatever you can today to help register 10 new voters >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=050626_2&amount=30]
If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately:
GIVE $15 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=050626_2&amount=15] GIVE $25 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=050626_2&amount=25] GIVE $50 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=050626_2&amount=50]
GIVE $100 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=050626_2&amount=100] GIVE $250 NOW ➜ [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?express_lane=true&refcode=050626_2&amount=250] OTHER AMOUNT [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=050626_2&amount=36]
Despite vote-suppressing courts and state legislatures making it harder to register to vote -- passing bills to stop organizations like ours and our partners on the ground from helping potential voters navigate the increasingly murky rules around voter registration -- we're still pulling out all the stops to bring voters into the system.
Voter participation has been increasing, and young people -- a major target of opponents of voting rights -- see the importance of voting now more than ever. Voting quickly becomes a habit -- a habit our democracy sorely needs to fulfill the promise of the American dream. Overwhelming key states with new voter registrations can help turn the tide against the voter suppression laws we've seen passed the last few years.
The midterm election will determine whether our democracy stays mired in the darkness and conspiracy theories we hear every day or if we can reclaim our rights -- from voting to choice and more -- and move forward to a better future.
Our voter registration work -- at just about $3 per new voter -- is more necessary now than ever. Can you pitch in with $30 and give us the resources we need to register a tidal wave of new voters ahead of the 2026 deadlines? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-voterregistration?refcode=050626_2&amount=30]
Thank you,
Voter Action Project's Registration Team

It’s our goal to bring awareness to these laws wherever they may crop up and organize voters to take action to ensure the right to vote is available to everyone in their states and communities.

[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130873586/619208721/701031031?refcode=em-5.6.26-expanded-b&amount=27&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjIvMS8xMTc1MjUiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiYmI5YWIyMTEtNzc0OS1mMTExLThlZjItMDAwZDNhMTRiNjQwIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=FuDM8z27mT8wnRuYZ00sEh8leF7IDALc83StsRwEYEQ=) Peter, it's Senator Bernie Sanders.

Let me start with something most of us instinctively know to be true.

And that is that running as a progressive in this country is never easy. You are often taking on the corporate establishment, the media establishment, and sometimes even your own party's political establishment.

But as progressives, we also understand something that most in the Democratic Establishment does not:

And that is that while it is essential that we defeat Trumpism and all its ugly and destructive policies, we need to do more. We need to elect candidates who have the guts to stand up to the wealthiest people on earth, not simply beg those people for money.

No more tinkering around the edges. No more status quo politics.

In the United States every man, woman and child can and must enjoy a decent standard of living. That’s what the American people want, and that’s what we have to deliver.

| | Friend,No one could hear her. A young girl named Kristen was locked in an attic. No windows. No fresh air. No way out. The door was locked from the outside. For months she lived there.
Alone. There was no bathroom.
Just a bucket. No shower. No clean clothes. And the only time she left that attic was when she was sold for sex.
Over. And over. And over. **This is the reality of child trafficking.**

Millions of children are trapped in exploitation around the world. But Kristen's story did not end in that attic. One night she knocked on a hotel room door. Her trafficker had arranged and forced her into another "date." But instead...**she met a rescue team - Freedom Strike Force. **They were working alongside law enforcement to identify victims and traffickers. When Kristen realized she was safe... She collapsed into the arms of one of our female advocates. **Free.** Law enforcement then raided the house where she was held. Traffickers were arrested. Kristen was taken to a safe place. For the first time in months, she had a real bed and a hot meal**.**

**She took the first step toward healing.** **This rescue was possible because people chose to act.**

clean_body: No windows. No escape for months. It’s unimaginable A rescue team changed Kristen's life. Another mission begins in Phoenix. | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | Friend,No one could hear her. A young girl named Kristen was locked in an attic. No windows. No fresh air. No way out. The door was locked from the outside. For months she lived there. Alone. There was no bathroom. Just a bucket. No shower. No clean clothes. And the only time she left that attic was when she was sold for sex. Over. And over. And over. This is the reality of child trafficking. Millions of children are trapped in exploitation around the world. But Kristen's story did not end in that attic. One night she knocked on a hotel room door. Her trafficker had arranged and forced her into another "date." But instead...she met a rescue team - Freedom Strike Force. They were working alongside law enforcement to identify victims and traffickers. When Kristen realized she was safe... She collapsed into the arms of one of our female advocates. Free. Law enforcement then raided the house where she was held. Traffickers were arrested. Kristen was taken to a safe place. For the first time in months, she had a real bed and a hot meal. She took the first step toward healing. This rescue was possible because people chose to act. The Sound of Freedom Foundation exists to stop the sale of God 's children. Inspired by the film Sound of Freedom , the Foundation works around the world to prevent trafficking, support rescue efforts, educate families, raise awareness, and push for stronger laws that protect children. Our mission is simple. To stop the sale of God 's children. And right now we are preparing a new mission, happening in just a few weeks in Phoenix. Our Freedom Strike Force partner will train local law enforcement for two days, teaching them how to identify traffickers and victims hidden in plain sight. Then on day three...they go into the field. Real operations. Real arrests. Real rescues. | | | | | Children like Kristen are waiting. But these missions cannot happen without support from people who care. That is why I am reaching out to you today. When you've taken hundreds of thousands of dollars from weapons manufacturers and AIPAC, it's not hard to understand why.

clean_body: | | | | Team, I need to share something with you that will probably anger you, and I hope it will inspire you to act. Here's the story. Days after signing a $500 million contract to manufacture weapons of war, Honeywell International wrote a maximum contribution to Doris Matsui's campaign. And she had no problem cashing that check. A company that locked in half a billion dollars in weapons contracts turned around and wrote the maximum allowable donation to our sitting Congresswoman — and she took it. This is how it works. Defense contractors and weapons manufacturers write checks to the people who are supposed to oversee them — and those people look the other way while the wars keep going and the profits keep flowing. And the proof is in her record. Over 60 Democrats have signed on to HR 3565, the Block the Bombs Act. It's a straightforward bill. Stop sending weapons that are killing civilians. Doris Matsui has not signed it. When you've taken hundreds of thousands of dollars from weapons manufacturers and AIPAC, it's not hard to understand why. I don't take a dime from corporate PACs. subject: Early voting started yesterday–with an endorsement by CAIR Action
body:
This moment is here

| | | | | [|
---](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=3c61230063&e=53c7d12fc7)
| | | | | | Dear Peter,Early voting started yesterday in California. I’m reaching out because your involvement in this campaign matters and I’m asking for your vote.[](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=bd9b476e52&e=53c7d12fc7)**I’m proud to share that our campaign has been endorsed by CAIR Action.** This endorsement means a great deal to me. It reflects the kind of coalition we’re building—one rooted in dignity, accountability, and a belief that our government should work for everyone, not just the well-connected.
**The Council on American–Islamic Relations (CAIR) is a Muslim civil rights and advocacy group.** Through civil rights actions, media relations, civic engagement, and education, CAIR works to promote social, legal and political activism among Muslims in America. I am very honored to receive their recognition and endorsement as a candidate for Congress.
Across our district, I’ve been hearing the same thing over and over: people are ready for leadership that shows up, speaks out, and fights for them.
Families are feeling the pressure of rising costs. Immigrant communities are living with fear and uncertainty. Too many people feel like Washington isn’t listening—or worse, doesn’t care.
That’s why I’m running for Congress — to move our district forward with bold ideas that create real change and a better way of representing the people of CA-32.
[**If you can, chip in $32 today to help us reach voters as early voting gets underway.**](https://chrisahuja.us2.list-manage.com/track/click?u=67424df89870d1cac00e55f46&id=74e051e889&e=53c7d12fc7)
This is our chance to meet the moment—with urgency, clarity, and a campaign that reflects the people it’s fighting for.
Let’s get to work.

A kid with a camera and a conviction that the truth mattered more than my comfort. Federal agents put me in handcuffs inside a United States senator's office in New Orleans. They led me out in front of the cameras. Every network in the country ran the footage. "Conservative activist arrested," the chyrons said. They wanted that to be the end of my story. I was twenty-five. I had no money. No legal team. No powerful friends. Just a belief that citizens had a right to know what their government was doing -- and a willingness to pay the price for acting on it. That false arrest was supposed to scare me into silence. It did the opposite. It taught me that the people in power will use every weapon they have against anyone who threatens the narrative. And it taught me that I could take the hit and keep walking. Eleven years later, they came for me again. This time they didn't just arrest me. They kicked in my door. November 2021. FBI agents swarmed my apartment in New York. They put me in handcuffs in my own hallway. They seized my phones. They rifled through my belongings. A journalist -- treated like a criminal in his own home. Why? Because someone gave us a diary that belonged to the President's daughter. We didn't publish it. We turned it over to law enforcement. And they raided me anyway. Think about that. We did the right thing -- and the FBI showed up at my door at dawn with guns and handcuffs. The message was clear: We don't care what you did or didn't publish. We want you to know that we can reach you. Anywhere. Anytime. The raids and the arrests -- those I expected. What I didn't expect was the betrayal from inside. A man who sat on my own board -- a man I trusted -- went to the FBI and became an informant against me. He admitted it on our hidden cameras. He told our undercover journalist he'd fed "tons of information" to federal law enforcement. Every agency that called, he answered. Then we found his copy of my book, Breakthrough -- with a rifle bullet fired straight through the heart on the cover. Exit wound out the back. When I confronted him in Miami Beach and asked him about it, he said: "I needed a target." When I asked if he'd kill me, he called it "a figure of speech." A figure of speech. A bullet through my heart. From a man who was supposed to protect the organization I built. I could fill a filing cabinet with the lawsuits they've thrown at me. Pentagon contractors. DOJ officials. Corporate executives. My own former organization sued me after I was forced out by the very board that harbored an FBI informant. Every lawsuit is designed to do the same thing: bleed me dry. Tie me up in discovery. Drain the resources I need for investigations and redirect them to lawyers. That's how lawfare works -- you don't have to win in court. You just have to make the fight so expensive that your target gives up. They've been waiting sixteen years for me to give up. I haven't. . $35 helps cover a day of fieldwork. $100 funds legal review on an investigation. $250 helps launch the next undercover operation. I want to be honest with you about something, because I think you deserve it. I don't have a normal life. I can't. The opposition is always watching. Always looking for a way to set me up, take me down, catch me in something they can twist into a headline. I've accepted that. There's no turning it off. There's no weekend where I stop being James O'Keefe. So I channel everything into the work. Into the training. Into the mission. The kid they arrested in Louisiana is gone. In his place is something their attacks created -- a man who has been hit so many times that he's stopped flinching. A man who walks into Antifa headquarters in disguise with hidden cameras rolling. A man who flies to Miami Beach to confront the traitor who shot a bullet through his book. A man who goes back to Minneapolis after receiving a death threat. They wanted to break me. Instead, they built something they can 't beat. And the results speak for themselves. This year alone, OMG investigations have triggered $253 million in federal contracts being suspended. We forced the Secret Service to suspend an agent who was leaking the Vice President's security details. We've recorded seven FBI and DOJ officials on hidden camera admitting the system is broken. We've generated millions of views -- not because we write opinion columns, but because we show up with cameras where nobody else will. That's what your donation buys. Not talk. Results. . Not because I need sympathy -- I don't. before we send someone undercover. that keeps our journalists safe. that lets us publish what the powerful want buried. because we have more targets than budget. They arrested me at twenty-five. They raided me at thirty-seven. They betrayed me from the inside. They sued me from every direction. And here I am at forty-one -- still standing, still fighting, and stronger than I've ever been. The only question is whether you 're standing with me. Rush your best gift right now -- . Thank you for being part of something they can't stop. In Truth, James O'Keefe Founder and CEO O'Keefe Media Group P.S.** Sixteen years ago they put me in handcuffs and thought that would be the end of it. Then they raided my home. Then they turned a board member into an informant. Then they sued me from every angle. And every single time, I got back up. I'm not going anywhere. But I need you in this fight. # Meet Dan Cox and Rob Krop TOMORROW - and pick up your signs and campaign materials
---
|
---
|
---
| Fellow Marylander,
We have just five (5) days until ballots begin to be mailed out to voters. We need your urgent support today to reach every voter with the consistent conservative message of our Republican values.

As a lifelong Republican who is the only Republican in the race ever elected to public office while also being a 30-year small business owner, demonstrating a voting record you can trust, I know how to work across the aisle and have done so to advance lower taxes, increased parental rights and civil liberties, and to defend our constitution.

And I have the experience and opportunity to win this fall and put Maryland back on track with common sense and affordability for all.

Come on out and meet me and my running mate Rob Krop at the Kent Island American Legion, 800 Romancoke Road, Stevensville, MD, tomorrow from 6pm-8pm and pick up your yard signs and campaign materials!

This race is important and we must win. If you can chip in to help with any amount, thank you.

See you tomorrow!

Authority: Dan Cox for Governor; Nick Krop, CPA, Treasurer.

name: Wes Moore
subject: Our mission must continue
disclaimer_text: Paid for by United for Virginia's Future PAC United for Virginia's Future PAC
body:
Five years ago, I had never run for political office. I was a former Army Captain, a dad to two young kids, and I ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country.

| Peter, it’s Governor Wes Moore.

Five years ago, I had never run for political office. I was a former Army Captain, a dad to two young kids, and I ran one of the largest poverty-fighting organizations in the country.

But I knew more had to be done. While career politicians were saying that everything was great, **I was hearing from folks all across Maryland who were feeling left behind.** So I ran for Governor with a mission to make Maryland a state that serves all our people — and won. (And I’m not done yet!)
