**I came off the sidelines for one reason: Ohio families.**

Life is too expensive. Paychecks are too low. Costs are too high – utilities, health care, groceries, everything.

Ohioans see more money going out the door, and not enough money coming in.

And it’s because the system is rigged. Too many Ohioans are getting the short end of the stick while people in power are doing favors for billionaires and corporate special interests. You are working harder than ever, but you can’t get ahead.

But instead of working to bring down costs and taking on corporate interests, politicians in Washington are making things worse. Politicians like Jon Husted.

Ohio deserves better and Ohioans are showing up and insisting on change. Last night was an important step in that fight because it brought us one step closer to flipping this seat and retaking Senate control.

**But we also know this battleground race is about to get harder.**

A new poll shows me down by 3 points. National Republicans are pouring $81 million into Ohio to defeat us – more than they’re spending in any other battleground state. And Jon Husted’s super PAC just launched a seven-figure ad buy attacking me.

**They know Ohio is in play. They know we can win. And they know that if we do, we can flip the Senate.**

_The Cook Political Report_ now calls this race a “Toss Up.” That matters. So does the grassroots energy we’ve built together.

That’s why we set an ambitious goal: to raise $1 million by the end of the week so we can make critical investments across the state and reach voters in every corner of Ohio. | | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | | | | | A small government task force just finished a 20-year project. I have to be honest with you.
There are days this fight feels impossibly heavy. My trauma from January 6th didn't end the next day. I've relived that day through testimonies and received death threats.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3e1adaa9-aa52-4570-b5e2-e13b86a4b26a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
But then I think about one specific man. A January 6th rioter. Someone who called on that mob to kill officers like me. Someone who now collects a government paycheck -- courtesy of Donald Trump and the Department of Justice.
**And I remember exactly why I 'm doing this.**
I'm doing this because someone has to hold Trump and his cronies accountable -- and it sure as hell isn't going to be the House Republicans who are too busy cheering him on to remember the oath they swore.
I'm doing this because Washington is riddled with corruption -- and the American people deserve better than a government that ignores subpoenas, rewards rioters, and treats the Constitution like a suggestion.
I'm doing this because everyday Americans are getting crushed while Trump plays political games with people's lives. Working families, kids, seniors -- they deserve a Congress that fights for them. Not one that rolls over for a wannabe king and his MAGA mob.
**That 's why I'm running.**
But look, winning this race won't be easy. I'm in a crowded primary with self-funding opponents, and dark money groups are already pouring funds into MD-05 to defeat me. If I'm going to fight back and win, I need Democrats like you by my side.
#### **[So please chip in whatever you can to my grassroots campaign today. Every single dollar will get us one step closer to a Democratic Majority that will hold Donald Trump accountable once and for all:](https://substack.com/redirect/3e1adaa9-aa52-4570-b5e2-e13b86a4b26a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
[ JOIN THE FIGHT](https://substack.com/redirect/3e1adaa9-aa52-4570-b5e2-e13b86a4b26a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Want to know what pisses me off?
The same Republican members of Congress who we carried to safety on January 6th -- who we shielded with our bodies -- are now cheering these rioters on.
_They 're pretending January 6th was a "tourist visit."_
They've had a million chances to hold these rioters accountable. They know it's what their constituents want. But they don't give a damn. The only thing they care about is pleasing Donald Trump and their wealthy donors.
I'm done waiting for them to grow a backbone. That's not a strategy -- it's a fantasy.
**The only way we restore accountability in Washington is by flipping the House.**
#### **[Please pitch in whatever you can to my campaign today, and together, we can bring justice back to Washington:](https://substack.com/redirect/3e1adaa9-aa52-4570-b5e2-e13b86a4b26a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**

Together in the fight,
Harry

clean_body: | = = Peter, I’m Shannon Bird, the Democrat running for Congress in Colorado's 8th Congressional District. This race is one of the most competitive in the entire country — and it will determine control of the House majority. I'm stepping up because the stakes are simply too high to sit on the sidelines. = | = I was raised by my mom and grandmother. My mom was an insurance clerk, and my grandmother was a blackjack dealer who used her tip money to put me through college. They both worked long hours and taught me how to work hard, give back, and fight for what's right. When I settled in Westminster to raise my family, I saw firsthand how our public schools were underfunded. I rolled up my sleeves and became chair of our school district's bond campaign, and later co-founded an education advocacy organization dedicated to empowering students and their families. That work inspired me to run for office — first for Westminster City Council, then for the state House, where I proudly served. In the legislature, I’ve fought to create and protect jobs, support small businesses, combat climate change, and defend abortion rights. Now, I'm running for Congress to stop Donald Trump and Gabe Evans' assault on our way of life and make sure Colorado remains a place where everyone can achieve their dreams. = = | = ---|--- = | = = | = Thank you, Shannon Bird | = | | | | | ---|---|---|---|--- Thank you for being a supporter of EMILYs List. | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/130886709/619252010/30495591?refcode=BLU_EM_HSC_2026-05-06_1&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMzMvMS85NTY0MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJjMjY1OTkzOC05ZDQ5LWYxMTEtOGVmMi0wMDBkM2ExNGI2NDAiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=gTrI49puE0HkLBkRbIH5rL3oac7DJUmRj2ugK2NA1QU=) Team,

Republicans have wanted this seat back ever since we flipped it in 2022. I’m the first Democrat in a CENTURY to hold this longtime Republican stronghold, and now they believe they have an opening.

name: Greisa, United We Dream
subject: Help keep families together
body:
The Defending Our Neighbors Fund is a lifeline for many immigrants. | | | Peter,
**** **“America's strength lies in its diversity and inclusion. Let's not betray the American Dream.”** — Community member Right now, families across the United States are being torn apart. People of all ages are being held in detention centers where some do not receive medical care, and some have died. **In 2024, over 2.5 million people in immigration proceedings lacked legal counsel.** The Defending Our Neighbors Fund is a lifeline for many immigrants. It fills a dangerous gap in our immigration system by funding trusted legal representation. The Fund prioritizes those most at risk: Families with children, long-time residents, survivors of violence, and people with urgent medical or humanitarian needs. The Fund partners with community legal providers across the country to get help where it’s needed most. **More than 6 million U.S. households have someone at risk of detention or deportation.** Legal representation is one of the strongest predictors of whether a family can stay together. Without it, parents and children face court systems they don’t understand and _decisions that change lives forever._ Peter, your donation today can help cover experienced immigration attorneys and legal teams to represent people in removal proceedings, support outreach so people can find help in their language, and, when possible, cover emergency bond costs to prevent separations. **[Will you make an urgent gift today to help defend our neighbors?](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.yjJN_MEbNx94PLaWzZ6hWzadU9N9RNMkN_aPwx_gUWMyhrdkC01LWf7qDIV-X_SfNT1mpyRhipiKDWZuKh9G2xnm3a8Q_ZTLc3CbCqOIqON6ZQygnT0hQY4z4WXmvEuKWG7KJ-NxY7YsZVPzBeBGfoaIYsBrD4cl9l0-ngA4cMGhulYF3pqd1PW7c5dOwyIPrHThk6-mAjpInS3V1ZpM9pWbnIQ3o1IC708cCnJ4eBv-3ci94FcCg_ulhCvmePE6PTXeT1iTfccIMGf_VvKHRxGPKcojFcWO0CGSgV2l_2LRNTibaFvJLy7FVULSv6DrY8Ejr4ST1nw0tJNOCxN8W2J2HIi2ZE1PoTAy79kIAbKmgzRAiJi7tLYfORjD_WOhiGb08Xh-lokICEGNq6K-0g/4qe/m7eedKXhQWKic_TODInwPw/h0/h001.40Vld21z_izXCelfl1AdAQbl3LuvCO15L4Y9ktmSsb8)** | | [DONATE](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.yjJN_MEbNx94PLaWzZ6hWzadU9N9RNMkN_aPwx_gUWMyhrdkC01LWf7qDIV-X_SfNT1mpyRhipiKDWZuKh9G2xnm3a8Q_ZTLc3CbCqOIqON6ZQygnT0hQY4z4WXmvEuKWG7KJ-NxY7YsZVPzBeBGfoaIYsBrD4cl9l0-ngA4cMGhulYF3pqd1PW7c5dOwyIPrHThk6-mAjpInS3V1ZpM9izX9VXCr52ixoaKEfj0APZYKpM2lcdH-TTTG6kb0WceTgP186c8VhjtC02DWseZUK92enw9OGo_NuLGAFyqkiToeXSgPWg2_tOBrCmiDpbp7X_8D_F0U4zCNHrH4tu3mygO-_SYKYTByhtq8tE4A6XxbKiPxxvtdaHxHbabSk9qKT16a_il_N5Fb055KaJURQ/4qe/m7eedKXhQWKic_TODInwPw/h1/h001.itZIMijhLrA90IujTyghoVi0keDN40Brwisi8cxbuNY)

| TIME WELL SPENT
---
| Hi friends, Kelly and I covered some ground last week, from Sublette County down through southern Wyoming, and I came away encouraged. Students at UW's School of Energy Resources, College of Agriculture, and Wyoming Construction Management Program asked me to speak to them about my Legislative work. We had a great discussion about keeping public lands public, decisions local, and what it really takes to build Wyoming’s future. Growth brings opportunity, but it also asks something of us: a strong workforce, reliable infrastructure, steady energy, practical land solutions and communities ready for what comes next. I was glad to see students taking that responsibility seriously. Out on the road, we heard from folks in energy, education, small business, emergency response and local services. In Rawlins and Carbon County, we heard how communities along I-80 are carrying a burden that reaches beyond their own community. The state needs to be a better partner before problems become crises. Across every stop, I heard the same steady, practical approach. People want things done right, done fairly and built to last. We’re grateful for the time and the conversations everywhere we went. If we saw you last week, thank you. If not, we’ll get there. And if you’re willing to stay involved or support what we’re building, it makes a difference. \- Eric

| | | Release: Barlow Campaign Shows Growing Grassroots Strength Across Wyoming Eric Barlow’s campaign for governor continues to build statewide grassroots momentum, surpassing 2,000 volunteer and supporter sign-ups and more than 1,000 individual Wyoming donors since launching. The campaign has received support from all 23 Wyoming counties, with 96% of donations coming from Wyoming residents. Barlow is now on his fourth lap around the state, meeting with voters in every corner of Wyoming. "We're doing this the Wyoming way," Barlow said. "Face to face, one community at a time, one conversation at a time. I'm grateful for everyone who's gotten involved — whether that's volunteering, placing signs, hosting an event, or just chatting with their neighbors." While fundraising totals will be reported through the regular public filing process, this announcement reflects a different measurement of momentum: the number of people choosing to get involved. “This is about people,” Barlow said. “It's about the teachers, the oilfield workers, the retirees, the small business owners, the neighbors, the youth who want Wyoming to stay Wyoming and be a place they can choose to live in. They want steady leadership and real results. That's what this is about.” Barlow, a rancher, veterinarian, Marine veteran, and longtime public servant, has centered his campaign on showing up, doing the work, and getting results for Wyoming families and communities. “This race is about Wyoming’s future,” Barlow said. “People want a governor who listens, works hard and doesn't forget what makes this state worth fighting for. This campaign belongs to the people who are building it. That's not going to change when I'm in office."

| **On The Trail**
---
| | | PINEDALE
It was great to spend time in Sublette County. I had the opportunity to tour the Jonah Field near Pinedale, one of Wyoming’s most important natural gas fields and a place where energy development, wildlife, ranching, and recreation all share the same landscape. Wyoming has worked hard to make that balance possible. I also spent time downtown visiting with small business owners and seeing the work happening on Pinedale’s Main Street. Strong communities depend on people willing to serve their neighbors every day. Our meet and greet in Pinedale had a great turnout, and people showed up with thoughtful questions about education, public lands, property taxes, healthcare, and protecting Wyoming’s water. I’m grateful for the time, the questions, and the honest conversations.

---
| | |
---
|
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| | | MOUNTAIN VIEW
We started the day with Union Wireless, a family-run business that's been part of Wyoming since 1914, talking about what's ahead for broadband. Then on to Bridger Valley Energy Authority, followed with Mountain View town leadership, digging into power demands, water challenges, and the road ahead.
Stopped by a local grocery store with manager and owner Jim Benedict and Jamy Ferrin, then talked water with Bridger Valley Water Conservation District.
Wrapped up the day at a meet & greet at the Fairway Restaurant and Bar, hosted by Senator Wendy Schuler.
---
| | |
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
|
---
| **GREEN RIVER AND ROCK SPRINGS**
---
| | | I started the day visiting with Al Harris on the radio and talking with listeners across the Sweetwater County area. I always appreciate the chance to visit directly with folks about the issues they are seeing at home and what Wyoming needs moving forward. From there, I met with Rock Springs Chamber's Enterprise Committee before traveling to the Black Butte coal mine. Black Butte has long been part of Wyoming’s energy economy, supplying coal to the Jim Bridger Power Plant and supporting local jobs.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| **RAWLINS AND CHEYENNE**
---
| | | Kelly and I had two meet and greets in Rawlins. One was an after-work discussion at the Carbon County Higher Education Center, where we also got a tour of the woodworking, automotive, welding, and nursing shops and classrooms. The other was a morning coffee at Mukwano, where they added cardamom sugar to the latte, which made it just right for Kelly. After coffee, we went by the Carbon County fire protection district to meet with chief John Rutherford, and Jim and Scott to talk about issues as we come into the fire season. Top of mind is the impact additional property tax cuts would have on an already frugal and critical service, including what the right funding mechanism might be, if not through property tax. We rounded out our night with an awesome event in Cheyenne. There was great turnout with over 100 attendees, more than 75 yard signs taken. Thank you to the hosts Rita Meyer and Toni Thomson and volunteers Pam Landry and Jenny Wacker.
---
| | |
---
|
---
| **LARAMIE**
---
| | | | |
---
| | |
---
| |
---
| There is so much good stuff happening at UW.
I spent time with students in the University of Wyoming Construction Management Program talking budgets, data centers, nuclear, the Hathaway Scholarship, and immigration. A lot of sharp young people thinking seriously about Wyoming's future. The Associated General Contractors of Wyoming supports this program and it is a great example of partnership connecting their members with a talented workforce.
Stopped in for the $50K John P. Elbogen Entrepreneurship Competition. Great ideas and real momentum.
I also had the opportunity to speak at an event hosted by the University of Wyoming School of Energy Resources and the University of Wyoming College of Agriculture and Natural Resources. We had a strong conversation about my legislative record on public lands, private property rights, and responsible management, issues that matter in every corner of Wyoming.
We wrapped up at Bond's Brewing. I'm grateful to Mallory and Jay Bond for hosting and for the kind of place they've built. It's welcoming and set up to bring people into the conversation.
---
| | | I also had the opportunity to watch the Kentucky Derby with the On The Bit Dressage Club at Wolfe Ranch Arena and Kelly came away with the winning hat!
It was a good reminder of how important Wyoming’s horse culture remains. This facility, that Tom and Kelly Wolfe have built, is unique in the Mountain West and helps keep the tradition going by supporting clinics, shows, and learning opportunities for riders from Wyoming and neighboring states.

Three things happened on this week's _Amped Up_. We brought on our old friend **Bob Cesca** --sexy liberal, podcaster-before-podcasting-was-a-thing, brilliant Trump-era analyst, and exactly the right wingman for a long-form takedown. The conversation went exactly where you hoped it would. And **David Shuster** --the Emmy-winning former MSNBC anchor--turned in a comedy set so unhinged that Bob had to admit on the record that he was going to have to up his game. The man who used to read teleprompters at _Hardball_ is now riffing on six-inch ballroom glass, Trump's confused relationship with measurement, Stephen Miller drafting "Liebenstraum" at a Clinton-era Christmas party, and the geopolitics of ball-shaver inflation in the post-Hormuz economy. If you've never seen Shuster fully off the leash, this is the episode that earns him a second career.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/fc2ced3e-b384-4362-8613-7c2ea10e67d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Underneath the laughs is a real argument. Bob walks Cliff and David through the Trump-ballroom shakedown--Chuck Grassley quietly tacking **$1 billion in "security"** onto a DHS bill while 20 million Americans are about to lose their ACA subsidies and the predator class throws itself a Versailles cosplay party in front of the Oval Office. The conversation runs through Trump's increasingly visible cognitive collapse on camera (_mutilization_ is now a word, apparently), Republican primary-challenge cowardice, the right-wing influencer rebellion already chewing into the MAGA base (Megyn Kelly, MTG, Tucker, Massie, Alex Jones), the Suicide Squad cabinet, the Marco Rubio "taint" question, and the most ruthless Chuck Grassley take you'll hear this year--including the fact that he's the _only_ sitting senator who voted against the MLK holiday in 1982 and is currently fourth in line to the presidency. Hit play. Pour something. This one delivers.
This is the kind of show that doesn't happen on cable--because cable doesn't let you run an hour of substance, the funniest bit Shuster has ever turned in, _and_ a brutally honest read on the predator class without three executives panicking about advertisers. I enlisted in the Army at 18 to give back. Now, the democracy that gave me so much hope is under threat by Trump, Hegseth, and the House GOP.

I won’t stand down while democracy is threatened.
I won’t stand down while our communities are afraid.
And I won’t let them take this seat I flipped without a fight.

### **Three Ways To Get Involved This Week**
1. **[Share Rachel's recent endorsement!](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/86568236-860f-4148-8fca-4e77c3e89062?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** **Spread the news, Rachel 's been endorsed by the Boilermakers Local 13**, marking her [second union endorsement.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ff087efb-3c9e-49df-af1f-7ddb704a0cc2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) [Download the endorsement graphic here](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/08a8a24c-5be0-4aaf-ae41-45ebcd9ce3fe?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), post to your social media page, and tag Wallace for Congress!

Paychecks are too low. Costs are too high – utilities, health care, groceries, everything. Ohioans see more money going out the door, and not enough money coming in. And it’s because the system is rigged. Too many Ohioans are getting the short end of the stick while people in power are doing favors for billionaires and corporate special interests. You are working harder than ever, but you can’t get ahead. But instead of working to bring down costs and taking on corporate interests, politicians in Washington are making things worse. Politicians like Jon Husted. Ohio deserves better and Ohioans are showing up and insisting on change. Last night was an important step in that fight because it brought us one step _closer_ to flipping this seat and retaking Senate control. **But we also know this battleground race is about to get harder.** A new poll shows me down by 3 points. National Republicans are pouring $81 million into Ohio to defeat us – more than they’re spending in any other battleground state. And Jon Husted’s super PAC just launched a seven-figure ad buy attacking me. They know Ohio is in play. They know we can win. Hey Team Pratt - Quick reality check. Tonight is a BIG night for this race.
I'm stepping onto that debate stage with Karen Bass and Nithya Raman, and a lot of people are finally going to see this race for what it really is.

No filters.
No spin.
No hiding. Ballots are already out. People are submitting their votes. Which means opinions are being formed RIGHT NOW. | This is the moment where voters decide: Who actually cares about LA, and who's just saying whatever it takes to stay in power. That's what tonight is about.
---

---

**We set a $10,000 pre-debate grassroots goal to make sure we can capitalize on this moment...**
And right now?
Pre-Debate Grassroots Goal $10,000 We're still $7,421 short. | |

The emerging deal would require Iran to commit to a nuclear enrichment moratorium in exchange for lifting Hormuz transit restrictions, per a [source familiar with the talks](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckDuu2zAQRVcjdTRG_NkuWKRR99KmFEbkSBqEH4Gkn4KsPrCXkP7g4N7z62v5Qo6c95-YyNW-LaGEpddXOpsvlVogz42_iXNgzIsEaQUYAXbJcZnG4IIPOPmR3HS_PyZ4arDj4XDTyponrA-lKJhVGe0xGPAalFJgR3ZvFRiwUk1Wy9u0TqCfT_vQysNm10EDRqr9Vul8rZE95o7t91aqp5svaYzu6P1sg_oxyHmQ83VdtwvbwXnvJdMfTJypvtFBzpmu9mYO7iSO8mo0yFkbYx-gBzl_DgtfUuLeRDkpc95F6xW5i7KJo9T0-iu4Yha4V6ImAmEUJYt-kOi4xrdwrC6cF8fIzd4HDXtCjp-x_T_afjv5LwAA__9VnIqm). Trump paired the olive branch with a stark warning: [if Iran doesn’t sign](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyc0LHOozAQBOCnMR3R2hgDhYtr6P5rr0SLvYRVjEH2Jnn9U_IIfz2aT5r597P8ICfO9794kC-yLfGMi5TncdVwFqqRAld-EefImBcDxrXQt-CWnBbdRB9DRB0a8noYRg2TBdfsfgTATpsOVoNhc9ug-9UOOqwWbEcTNew_FPTgTKedNTe9arDT5EbbBdjcqixgoiK3QtdzTRwwC9bHdpZAt3AeTfK7yFVV90eZWZlZdto5pU-mzLyfB2V6V2VmjAdnrlJQ-MzKzP3oegdj-53Zyl4IhXJtuWBuUQTD49Nrio_Xm1Pi6gZl4X4gf_lGfvHUy5v_AQAA__-p23hf), bombing resumes “at a much higher level and intensity than it was before.” ★★★

In Ohio, [Vivek Ramaswamy won the Republican gubernatorial primary](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL2uozAQhZ8GOiNjiIHCxTZ02XZLNIwHMop_kO3A5u2vkke49dE5Ot_3777cgR2H_S94Mqlsi412Kenlj4wxUbaEnPkkDpYhLEoqLeRNSL0Et7S1NRYttFiTaYdhbOXUS10_jFUbKZq6obtBp5Fw7VHjqu2opLTDWLP5TMmb1Kprda-adm1lP0167DuUm16rXoKjVJpEx2t1jBAK5OcWE1KD0dfOPEo5ctX9qdRcqfm6rmaL_wNd-ZNXaj6i48KYKzV_icQK-CQrTj7pKRJ4yBf4t7g4ZBEfHMUeD7G_VkoBSkwMThyJPaS32ABJWPIRExTxaQGWGOpk7HGxc5z1UPVy98Due6_8wuZp1E8AAAD___EdiN8), defeating rival Casey Putsch and setting up a November race against Democrat Amy Acton. Democrats answered with a counterpunch: Chedrick Greene [won Michigan’s 35th District special election](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL_upCAUhZ8GOwwgohYU29jNtluaK9zRm-WPAWbcx9_MPMKvOqc4Ofny_XlsD6BA6fgNEW1pz81nv7Xyild1uWD16KjSGyl5grQpoQwXIxdmS2GTnbfeeZCuQyunaZZi0cJ0p0UzL5P0y6iUGGGeAXEYYd7lPguxI3ZkP1diFEYN0mjVy10KvSxm1oMTT7MzLSBgaX3B67UHcpAa1L_PXBz2Lscu2LO1q7LhF1MrU-t93_0N9aR0tJzwH0RKWD5TptaEd2VqdRAvoCN9uh5HM2nB1BrJnXRA4h5jdgVa5RXdqyB3ObWSA68NGvKK6RsXOoLAMaBrlBO_KTG1dsX666YQqJqJaXFEoPAlbT8Q-7bqfwAAAP__UemKbg), preserving Democrats’ narrow majority in the state Senate. ★★★

Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) agents executed a search warrant on Wednesday at the office of Virginia Senate President pro tempore L. Louise Lucas, the most powerful Democrat in that chamber, [as part of a corruption probe](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckL3OpSAUAJ9GOwygohYU29h9225p-Dl4TxaBcPC6-_abu4_w1ZNMJvPr6_gyGDGdP80FurZw-OyPVu-rkMsVyINDwjdg8mjSIblUjM-MqyPFQ_Ree-eNcD1osSyr4NvEVf_Sa_BBhhnmeVxDcPOyBbHACuPmFs7t1qP-qPjMlRyFmuQgrODTtql1Gh0PynYTNxFqGyqU20Z0JjVDv0OuDgaXrz7qV2uFuvFHJ_dO7s_zDCH_SfDQh3dyLzliQ0ed3INFVg16YlRMslBPqMzE-JflENABC-ChmshcrvUuDXNipWYLrJl6QiPmTErGIjF7EyYg6qv25cEYkdTSTfy8DMb_Ze0bI99a_gsAAP__Ia6G-g). Two sources say the [investigation traces to a Biden-era probe](https://email.alert.republicantaskforce.com/c/eJyckLGu3CAQAL8Gd7ZgDfhcUKRx99KmtDC73G2CsQX4nPx9dPmE9KPRaH58rV-eE-fnd7-TKy2ueODayrWfNRyFKlLgym_ijOzzChJsL00v7ZrTqjp0GNCr0JFT0_RQctbSdi83mw0fcYJoPKBBq2ejQoij9oRyjNix-6ikkRZGZTUMalNSz7N96DHIaDehpU9U2lDovLbEwefm6694lEBDOPYuuVdrZxXjNwGLgOW-7-H29cX52Y5Mv_3OmcoHFbBkuquA5edVGwcSsGhjJpBGwJKOiyv16Qq-9keMHKgvnpGw3_70cWMBS1ccnjenxNVOQsvn7jn9q2j_Me3t4G8AAAD__8NFfJk) of possible bribery connected to marijuana dispensary businesses. Lucas has not been charged. Lucas, a Portsmouth Democrat and ally of Gov. Abigail Spanberger, had been central to Virginia’s redistricting fight. clean_body: Read my trial update: | Dear Peter, I spent a lot of time over the Easter weekend reflecting on the big picture of what my trial in Arizona is really all about. I thought back to all the despicable things the vengeful Democrats have done to me... A dawn raid on my home. Arresting me alongside President Trump as innocent men. Freezing my bank accounts. Seizing my assets. Forcing me to the point of bankruptcy. And now, a vengeful Democrat Attorney General making me stand in a rigged trial for bogus state-level crimes, because she knows that not even the most powerful man on the face of the planet – President Trump – can save me with a federal pardon in state court. The lunatic Left’s desire to DESTROY yours truly knows no bounds. They even stripped me of my law licenses so I would have no means to defend myself, leading pundits in the media to label me a “ DEAD MAN WALKING!” But what I came to realize over the Easter holiday was that the pursuit of truth, freedom, and justice are worth infinitely more than any earthly possession. They can strip me of all I’m worth – all I’ll ever be worth – but what I REFUSE to surrender to the Democrats and their Deep State thugs is my LEGACY! And that is what my final trial is truly all about, Peter. I’d rather lose everything than betray what I know to be true. I could never lie and say what I'm going through is a fair and honest process just to hang on to “earthly possessions.” "For what shall it profit a man, if he shall gain the whole world, and lose his own soul? " (Mark 8:36) You see, this FINAL BATTLE for my freedom is about ensuring this injustice can NEVER AGAIN happen to another innocent patriot all for standing by what he knows to be right and true. I pray to God that will be my legacy when we win this trial. But now, as I fight with all I’ve got, I have only one place left to turn to help me reach the finish line and secure my freedom: good and honest Americans like YOU. Peter, I understand this was probably the last thing on your mind today. I get it. And that’s why I always say that if you can’t afford to help me in this fight, please delete this message and carry on with your day. Don’t even think twice about it. But if you can help, I’m going to need the best defense I can get to defeat this radical Democrat Attorney General who is hell-bent on locking me up for the rest of my life. Thank you and God bless you, Rudy Giuliani Rudy Defense Trust Paid for by Rudy Defense Trust |

FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260506EM-fires]
This is the governing body overseeing the National Science Foundation, one of the most important scientific institutions in the United States — and he fired all of them. At once.
The National Science Board exists for a reason. It oversees billions in federal research funding, advises Congress on science policy, and helps ensure taxpayer dollars support real, evidence-based innovation.
Now that independence is being stripped away.
Let me say this clearly: When political leaders start dismantling independent science institutions, it doesn’t just hurt scientists. It hurts all of us — because that means fewer medical breakthroughs, less climate research, slower progress on cancer treatments, degraded pandemic preparedness, and more.
As a microbiologist and educator, take it from me: Science only works when it is allowed to be independent, transparent, and guided by evidence — not politics.
But what we’re seeing now is a systematic effort to replace expertise with loyalty, and it’s happening at the highest levels of government.
This is exactly why I’m running for Congress. Because we need leaders who will defend science and protect vital institutions like the NSF.
But I can’t take on that fight alone. We’re heading into a critical stretch of this campaign, and we need the resources to compete against entrenched interests that are perfectly comfortable ignoring science. So I’m asking you: Can you chip in $10 or whatever you can today to help me fight for science, facts, and the future of research in America? DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260506EM-fires]
When we let science lead, people thrive. Let’s put facts back in charge — and build a Congress that reflects reason, reality, and hope.

# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260506-2790)
Peter,
Just this week alone, Wisconsin's average price for a gallon of gas jumped 44.8 cents, the fifth-biggest increase of any state in the country. Diesel is even worse, up 73.2 cents, the third-largest weekly increase in the nation.
Researchers at the Federal Reserve [studied](https://act.francescahong.com/go/11786?t=1&akid=2790%2E105371%2Eulb85r) who's actually absorbing the hit. In March, households earning under $40,000 cut their gas consumption by 7% — the most of any income group. Households earning over $125,000 cut consumption by just 1%, and pushed their gas spending up 19%. The Fed has a name for what they found: a K-shaped economy. The rich keep driving. Working people carpool, take the bus, or skip the trip.
But a lot of Wisconsinites don't have the option to drive less. Farmers running diesel tractors through planting season. Service workers who clock out after the buses stop running. Nurses on the night shift. Construction crews on the road before dawn. They have to fill the tank no matter what it costs.
Our campaign is in that group too.
With less than 100 days until the primary, we’re kicking into high gear. We can't pull back on travel now.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/1?c0=em_ms_fh_20260506.8Fm_T5&refcode=em20260506-2790&t=2&akid=2790%2E105371%2Eulb85r)
Nobody has been campaigning harder than Fran. She’s the only candidate committed to meeting voters in every corner of this state and listening to working people. Help us fill the gas tank so we can keep getting out and hearing what matters to our neighbors.

clean_body: Like lighting money on fire Peter, Just this week alone, Wisconsin's average price for a gallon of gas jumped 44.8 cents, the fifth-biggest increase of any state in the country. Diesel is even worse, up 73.2 cents, the third-largest weekly increase in the nation. Researchers at the Federal Reserve who's actually absorbing the hit. In March, households earning under $40,000 cut their gas consumption by 7% — the most of any income group. Households earning over $125,000 cut consumption by just 1%, and pushed their gas spending up 19%. The Fed has a name for what they found: a K-shaped economy. The rich keep driving. Working people carpool, take the bus, or skip the trip. But a lot of Wisconsinites don't have the option to drive less. Farmers running diesel tractors through planting season. Service workers who clock out after the buses stop running. Nurses on the night shift. Construction crews on the road before dawn. They have to fill the tank no matter what it costs. Our campaign is in that group too. With less than 100 days until the primary, we’re kicking into high gear. We can't pull back on travel now. Nobody has been campaigning harder than Fran. She’s the only candidate committed to meeting voters in every corner of this state and listening to working people. Help us fill the gas tank so we can keep getting out and hearing what matters to our neighbors. With gratitude, Team Hong Email us: mailto:info@francescahong.com

body:
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21486?t=1&akid=41293%2E3422442%2EVGAif3)
Big news, Peter:
**The McClatchy Media California editorial board just endorsed Katie Porter for governor** after conducting interviews with every major Democratic candidate and Republican Steve Hilton. They called her “by far the most impressive” out of all the candidates.
That endorsement represents five major California newspapers: _The Sacramento Bee, The Modesto Bee, The Fresno Bee, Merced Sun-Star, and The San Luis Obispo Tribune._
And what put Katie over the top?
_Her agenda. Plain and simple._
Katie understands the challenges working families face because she’s lived them herself.
She’s a single mom of three. She drives an old minivan. She knows what it feels like to worry about rising costs, shrinking budgets, and not having enough breathing room at the end of the month.
Katie isn’t running to protect billionaires or corporate interests. She’s running to lower costs, take on Big Oil and corporate greed, and fight for the people who are getting squeezed every single day.
**That’s why this endorsement matters so much. It proves that when voters hear Katie’s message, they respond to it.**
But here’s the reality: ballots are _already_ landing in mailboxes, and the primary election is just a little over three weeks away.
That means we’re in the most critical stretch of this campaign. Every ad we run, every voter we reach, and every conversation we spark could make the difference. So we’re asking:
**[Will you chip in to power Katie’s campaign, keep our ads on the air, and reach undecided voters across California?](https://act.katieporter.com/go/21531?c0=em_ms_kp_20260506_2_ak.nvLLJd&refcode=em20260506-41293&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=3&akid=41293%2E3422442%2EVGAif3)**

Thank you,
Team Katie Porter

---
| | Peter,
---
I'm going to be blunt with you.

We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit.

Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way."

Right now.

And the scariest part?

It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms.

High schools. Colleges.

Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped.

If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: _" What happened to this country?" _

You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly.

Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything...

The other side is doing something far more dangerous.

They're raising the next generation.

Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places.

That's how countries are lost.

Slowly. Then all at once.

But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope...

There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged.

_And it shouldn 't even exist. _

**Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools.**
That alone felt like a miracle.

Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have.

Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down.

And yet...

_They stepped up anyway. _

About that time, Charlie called me.

He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent.

"Andrew, we've got to move faster."

I told him we were. He stopped me.

"No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools."

I actually laughed.

"Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America."

"Okay," he said. "How many are there?"

"About 27,000."

And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000."

I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools.

We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet.

But Charlie wasn't fazed.

_" We'll figure it out." _

That was him.

He didn't wait for perfect conditions.

Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... _we lose everything. _

And now?

Less than a year later...
---
[](http://links.bestamericanow.com/u/click?_t=f6e78b69acbb4291bd75bc93fae35a62&_m=d155f6af4a64488a94d4a6136b56773a&_e=QKzW-Y4on1m6lnckiXg16i7a4NZlUyYJrAGH3dPw53b58TSaIZXS3PquCBt4vq08fY97j7fZXMX6HetsOdUpP3MscBPDSzAWtOB01rU3sQCXDR53Gdgj0s_ZaIb2FfeIw0A8gGryeOAbw07LVd4gKkUSZsOwRvkGdFHncRe_CmKNfcDcN7ol-5wMxo-3eWh0yuQeqp8s2fJWKqvT0QRsT0VlZzpkv-oeJMeD9D-6w0eOZ743bGhDJDvjZGCw6b1NkHKrJI3SR-qFk2uwZWpcnevXVlEH3fHJ-KS89sQTk8SHPsTy4vV29ypzGXtO79_ofJPWCDEXZtpL-Ablfg5u2jBWTFVoAwZpJPu8JmIIxC0BpoKsnR-cQYHKdtwyRQOB_TuR9e0XapYERComhNvMrylWkuI8oNWqhQCrYpTxuHT-hxQPRJ6R9TzHMi_Zci5GUiGP7aZDPun6pspMTmOY8yV0Wyxu8LC4L9GmKyWxO55MUkHqIUSfMLk872sILQ3-Y5n8u91RJKyd7ycnJuscG-zGHKCTK8xDTYc4gpe06kl8ZFh23azpfFoCDRy-dTU5bfR7jDY24HHDICaVAFk-Vvhm5_TpUu5beJS0OTRuYUwXFBuzKAob9RLht4iGXq2zhmP5Bl4z3obAlN0cL3r-tfcbiwpFc9AMClze_fgDDK4I5BNdT_Lsoskc53tXTDkTYnqlqDysdYV58lJRh9WEMg%3D%3D)
---
**We 're in 3,300 schools. **

**Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. **

**Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. **

_That shouldn 't be possible. _

Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day.

And yet... it's still happening.

_But Peter, here 's the part you need to understand: _

This is not a victory. It's a foothold.

_Because in the other 87% of schools? _

There is no resistance. None.

Just one-sided propaganda from the Left.

One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them.

That's the reality.

The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are.

clean_body: I debated sending this... until now | | | | | Peter, I'm going to be blunt with you. We are closer to losing this country than most people are willing to admit. Not someday. Not "if things keep going this way." Right now. And the scariest part? It's not happening in Washington. It's happening in classrooms. High schools. Colleges. Places where the next generation is being shaped -- or more accurately... reshaped. If you've ever looked at what's coming out of our schools and thought: " What happened to this country?" You're not wrong. You're seeing it clearly. Because while most people are arguing online... while they're hoping things will turn around... while they're waiting for the next election to fix everything... The other side is doing something far more dangerous. They're raising the next generation. Earlier. Faster. And with zero resistance in most places. That's how countries are lost. Slowly. Then all at once. But here's the thing that should give a patriot like you hope... There is one place where that trend is actually being challenged. And it shouldn 't even exist. Just one year ago, Turning Point USA 's high school program -- which is now called "Club America" -- was in about 1,200 schools. That alone felt like a miracle. Because starting even ONE chapter today takes courage most adults don't have. Conservative students get mocked. Targeted. Threatened. Shut down. And yet... They stepped up anyway. About that time, Charlie called me. He didn't sound optimistic... He sounded urgent. "Andrew, we've got to move faster." I told him we were. He stopped me. "No. You're not thinking what I'm thinking. I want to be in 35,000 high schools." I actually laughed. "Charlie... there aren't even 35,000 high schools in America." "Okay," he said. "How many are there?" "About 27,000." And without hesitation: "Good. Let's do 27,000." I remember sitting there thinking to myself... we're barely in 1,200 schools. We didn't have the staff. We didn't have the infrastructure. We didn't even have the roadmap yet. But Charlie wasn't fazed. " We'll figure it out." That was him. He didn't wait for perfect conditions. Because he knew something most people don't want to face: If we wait... we lose everything. And now? Less than a year later... We 're in 3,300 schools. Thirteen percent of all high schools in America. Eight states are now backing this effort to put a Club America chapter in every high school statewide. That shouldn 't be possible. Not in this environment. Not with the level of hostility these students face every single day. And yet... it's still happening. But Peter, here 's the part you need to understand: This is not a victory. It's a foothold. Because in the other 87% of schools? There is no resistance. None. Just one-sided propaganda from the Left. One-sided pressure on kids who are too young to even realize what's happening to them. That's the reality. The question isn't whether we're fighting. We are. The question is whether it's enough. Because right now, the students stepping up through Club America... They're not the majority. They 're the exception. They're the ones willing to take the heat. The ones willing to stand alone. The ones willing to risk being targeted just to say: " I love this country." And every time one of those students raises their hand... We have a choice. Back them. Or leave them on their own. Because when a student starts a chapter, we send them an activism kit -- with American flags. Pocket Constitutions. Leadership tools. Everything they need to actually stand their ground. Not symbolically. For real. They've already made the decision to lead. All they're waiting on... is you and me. Each activism kit costs $25. That 's it. $25 to make sure one student doesn't have to stand alone against the Left in a hostile school. $25 to put real tools in their hands. $25 to push back -- even if it's one campus at a time. But here's what gives me hope, Peter... Club America isn't slowing down. It's accelerating. Because every day, more students are stepping forward. Not because it's easy or popular... But because they know what 's at stake. They're starting chapters in schools where they were told not to. They're speaking truth in classrooms where the Left once went unchallenged. They're choosing courage in places designed to make them conform. And they're not alone. They're finding each other. They're bringing more students with them every day. They're building something real -- rooted in faith and freedom, grounded in truth, and unafraid to say that America is worth defending. That's how movements are built. Not from the top down... But from the ground up. One student. One school. One chapter at a time. And Peter -- that's exactly how we take this country back. But only if we move fast enough. Because the Left isn't slowing down. They're not taking a break. They're not afraid to push their anti-American ideas in every classroom they're in. And if we don't match that urgency... if we don't meet that moment with equal conviction... Then the generational window Charlie Kirk opened to save our country closes. And once it closes... It closes for good. That's what's at stake. Let's not waste this moment. Let's back our brave students -- while it still matters. | | For Charlie, Andrew Sypher Chief Field OfficerTurning Point USA P.S. I need you to hear this clearly... Charlie Kirk wasn't just dreaming big when he called me last year about Club America's progress. He was warning us: "The enemy is moving younger. They're coming after students earlier. We don 't have time to wait." And he was right. Look around. Club America may be in 13% of high schools... But in the other 87%? There is no pushback against the Left. No one telling those kids the truth. Just a Leftist pipeline -- from classroom... to belief... to voting booth. And once that pipeline is complete... It 's over. Peter, this is one of the last places a patriot like you can stop it before it 's too late to save our country. You may not be able to step into a hostile high school and stand for truth like these students do. But you can give critical support to a young freedom fighter who will. There's still time to turn this country around... and this is one of the few ways we can actually do it -- one student, one school, one chapter at a time. 4940 East Beverly Road Phoenix, Arizona 85044

The Court’s cruel ruling in _Louisiana v. Callais_ is a direct hit to the heart of the Voting Rights Act and the fragile promise that every American’s vote should carry equal weight.
Until the Voting Rights Act, the 15th Amendment — which barred the federal government and the states from denying the right to vote based on race, color, and servitude — was routinely ignored by Southern states using the legal mechanism of Jim Crow.
Poll taxes, literacy tests, and language restrictions were the most visible tools of voter suppression.
But hostile political regimes also drew the boundaries of voting lines and districts to make it impossible for Black and brown voters to elect anyone who represented their interests.
Enter the Voting Rights Act.
Section 2 of that act made it illegal to design districts to dilute or block racial communities from finding common cause. It also required a corrective action.
But now the _Callais_ decision has dramatically narrowed that core protection against racially discriminatory redistricting.
**The consequences of this disastrous ruling are already reverberating across our country.**
Majority-Black districts could be dismantled or diluted. Latino districts in fast-growing areas could lose political muscle. Representatives championing the minority communities they represent will likely lose their seats. Congressional maps in closely divided states could be tilted further away from competitiveness.
**But the Roberts Court is not the only actor in this story. Alongside groups like Fair Fight Action, we can continue the fight for multiracial democracy. We can continue calling for reforms that ensure equal representation in the halls of power.**
Congress retains the authority to strengthen voting rights protections. State legislatures can adopt independent redistricting commissions or refuse to vote for racially discriminatory maps. Voters can reach out to elected officials at every level of government and demand that they publicly take a stand for voting rights. Civic organizations can mobilize communities to solve for voter suppression tactics even when the rules shift.
**Fair Fight Action will continue pushing this vital work forward.**
As the Roberts Court considered Callais, Fair Fight Action laid bare the stakes of the case by identifying how gutting Section 2 could secure enough safe Republican seats to lock in one-party rule for a generation.
**Now the team is mobilizing advocates across the country. Just this past weekend, Fair Fight Action directly contacted our communities in Tennessee, Louisiana, and Alabama. And collectively, we are rallying a movement behind fair elections with fair maps, pressing forward for proactive voting rights protections at the state and national level, working to mitigate the effects of voter suppression attempts, and fighting to reverse the authoritarian playbook.**

Callais is a direct hit to the heart of the Voting Rights Act and the fragile promise that every American’s vote should carry equal weight. Until the Voting Rights Act, the 15th Amendment — which barred the federal government and the states from denying the right to vote based on race, color, and servitude — was routinely ignored by Southern states using the legal mechanism of Jim Crow. Poll taxes, literacy tests, and language restrictions were the most visible tools of voter suppression. But hostile political regimes also drew the boundaries of voting lines and districts to make it impossible for Black and brown voters to elect anyone who represented their interests. Enter the Voting Rights Act. Section 2 of that act made it illegal to design districts to dilute or block racial communities from finding common cause. It also required a corrective action. But now the Callais decision has dramatically narrowed that core protection against racially discriminatory redistricting. The consequences of this disastrous ruling are already reverberating across our country. Majority-Black districts could be dismantled or diluted. Latino districts in fast-growing areas could lose political muscle. Representatives championing the minority communities they represent will likely lose their seats. Congressional maps in closely divided states could be tilted further away from competitiveness. But the Roberts Court is not the only actor in this story. Alongside groups like Fair Fight Action, we can continue the fight for multiracial democracy. We can continue calling for reforms that ensure equal representation in the halls of power. Congress retains the authority to strengthen voting rights protections. State legislatures can adopt independent redistricting commissions or refuse to vote for racially discriminatory maps. Voters can reach out to elected officials at every level of government and demand that they publicly take a stand for voting rights. Civic organizations can mobilize communities to solve for voter suppression tactics even when the rules shift. Fair Fight Action will continue pushing this vital work forward. As the Roberts Court considered Callais, Fair Fight Action laid bare the stakes of the case by identifying how gutting Section 2 could secure enough safe Republican seats to lock in one-party rule for a generation. Now the team is mobilizing advocates across the country. Just this past weekend, Fair Fight Action directly contacted our communities in Tennessee, Louisiana, and Alabama.
